Your pay, energy bills and cash Isa: How the Budget affects you - BBC News
Image source,Getty ImagesByKevin PeacheyCost of living correspondent
Families facing cost-of-living pressures are being offered some help, or "breathing space" as Chancellor John Healey is calling it.
The help comes as prices are rising faster than expected with annual energy bills in particular likely to increase by hundreds of pounds in January.
Here's how the key announcements in the Budget affect you and your money.
If you are living in a home in council tax bands A to D in England, you will receive a one-off £100 "Household Energy Payment" from January, funded by extra tax on banks.
It will be paid directly into your bank account.
Council tax bands are listed below - you can check which one you are in by looking at your annual bill or checkingthe government's website,external, although that was struggling to cope with traffic after the announcement.
Administrations in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland will receive the equivalent funding, and they will decide whether to introduce the same payment.
This is designed to help with soaring energy bills, with some forecasts suggesting a typical annual bill could rise by £400 or so to £2,100 in January the saving will be only a portion of that. Although it's designated for energy bills, you can spend the money on anything you wish.
The VAT cut on electricity bills, which was introduced in October, will also be extended to July. It was due to end in April.
The fee for connecting to your gas supply so called standing charges will be scrapped in England, Scotland and Wales, next year "or as soon as possible after", the chancellor said.
These fixed daily charges will then be shifted onto the price you pay for each unit of energy.
The Treasury calculates that 60% of households will save an average of £45 a year, with lower users gaining the most. But the saving will come after the projected big rise in bills in January.
Higher users - in the biggest houses but also large, low-income families - will pay more than they currently do.
The government wants to extend reforms to electricity standing charges later.
The 5p "temporary" cut in fuel duty on petrol and diesel, introduced by Rishi Sunak in 2022, will be extended to July. It was scheduled to be phased out from January.
It means drivers will still pay the levy at 52.95p per litre.
Motor fuel prices have risen sharply owing to the continued impact of the Iran war on drivers, with diesel having recently hit new records when it moved above £2 per litre.
The cost of filling a typical family car with diesel has gone up by around £30 since late February. A tankful of petrol costs about £23 more.
The chancellor has scrapped his predecessor's plans to reduce the annual amount people can save tax-free in cash in Individual Savings Accounts (Isas).
Rachel Reeves had wanted the policy to encourage personal investment in stocks and shares.
It meant, from April 2027, if you're under 65, you would only be able to save £12,000 a year in cash in an Isa, rather than £20,000.
Instead, the government plans to create a new "Starter Isa" for first-time investors.
More tax for some savers and landlords
If you have a large amount in savings, or if you fail to use the tax-free Isa allowance, then you will pay more tax from April.
You do not pay tax on all savings. There is the annual £20,000 Isa allowance, and an annual savings income allowance (in other words, the interest received on a savings pot) of £1,000 for basic rate taxpayers and £500 for higher-rate taxpayers.
But beyond that savings tax rates will rise by four percentage points to 24% and 44% respectively from April.
Landlords could also pay more in tax. In analysis published on Wednesday, the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) said these steps along with measures over the past decade that have reduced private landlord returns "collectively risk leading to a steady rise in rents".
Minimum wage rise but you'll pay more tax
Minimum wage rates will rise by 3.9% in April. It means:
Eligible workers aged 21 and over on the National Living Wage will receive £13.21 an hour, up from £12.71
If you are aged 18, 19 or 20, the National Minimum Wage will increase to £11.27 an hour, up from £10.85
For those aged 16 or 17, the minimum wage will rise to £8.31 an hour, up from £8
The separate apprentice rate which applies to eligible people under 19 - or those over 19 in the first year of an apprenticeship – will also increase to £8.31 an hour, from £8
However, these figures mean, this time around, there's no progress on Labour's manifesto promise to narrow the gap in minimum wages between older and younger workers.
For all workers,the ongoing freeze in the income bands, or thresholds, at which income tax is paid went unmentioned in the Budget.
But it means any kind of pay rise could drag you into a higher tax bracket, or see a greater proportion of your income taxed than would otherwise be expected. Scotland has its own income tax bands.
How much is the minimum wage going up by?
The triple lock policy means that the state pension will go up in line with average wage increases, at 3.9%.
the flat-rate state pension for those who reached state pension age after April 2016 will be £250.70 a week, or £13,036.40 a year, up £488 on now
the old basic state pension for those who reached state pension age before April 2016 will be £192.10 a week, or £9,989.20 a year, up £374.40 on now
The government had already committed to not taxing people who only get an income from the state pension.
The chancellor said this would be the case until at least 2030, as there will be a new Pension Tax Allowance, so pensioners with an income up to the value of the full new state pension will not pay income tax.
The First Time Buyer Isa has been in the planning stages with the government for a while.
Healey has confirmed that it is intended to replace the often-criticised Lifetime Isa.
The penalty for withdrawing savings from a Lifetime Isa if you are buying a home above the £450,000 threshold will be scrapped.
Separately, he confirmed the Your First Home equity scheme to allow first-time buyers in England to buy a new-build home with a deposit of 2.5%. It would provide them with a loan worth 20% of their property's value to help pay for the purchase.
The government has made no changes to student loan rates - saying only that it is being "kept under review".

J-PAL North America launches ARTEMIS to train early-career researchers
The Applied Research Training in Evaluation, Methods, and Impact Studies program provides dedicated support to help researchers overcome barriers to pursue and obtain funding for randomized evaluations.Katherine Rodriguez Marquez|J-PAL North AmericaPublication Date:October 30, 2026Press Inquiries
ErinGraeberEmail:egraeber@povertyactionlab.orgPhone:617-324-6916Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action LabCloseCaption:J-PAL North America's inaugural ARTEMIS cohort attended Summer Institute — an intensive week-long course at the MIT Endicott House — to begin their training last June.Credits:Photo courtesy of J-PAL North America.
The Applied Research Training in Evaluation, Methods, and Impact Studies (ARTEMIS) program, launched by J-PAL North America, equips early-career researchers with high-level technical training and practical skills to design randomized evaluations (also referred to as a randomized controlled trials, or RCTs) on issues of poverty in the U.S. context. Fully funded and highly rigorous, the program's inaugural cohort of 20 participants — including PhD students through pre-tenure faculty — is receiving training, mentorship, and proposal development support through December.
ARTEMIS is the newest offering within J-PAL North America’s Economics Pathways program, which broadens and strengthens the pipeline of economics researchers by providing support to aspiring scholars at every stage — from undergraduate interns to research staff and, now, academic researchers preparing to launch their first randomized evaluations.
ARTEMIS programming commenced this past June with the Summer Institute — an intensive weeklong course at MIT Endicott House in Dedham, Massachusetts, that focused on delivering technical content and building participants' practical skills and confidence to design and pursue funding for rigorous evaluations to address poverty in the United States. During the Summer Institute, participants had the opportunity to learn from researchers in the J-PAL network, including Gerald Daniels,associate professor of economicsat Howard University, who served as a lecturer for the program. “ARTEMIS is an amazing program that bridges the gap for researchers who haven't previously had the opportunity to work with randomized evaluations,” notes Daniels. “It takes rigorous methodologies, like randomized evaluations, and makes them approachable, helping scholars translate their research ideas into high-impact evaluation designs."
The inaugural cohort brought together early-career researchers from institutions across the United States, each tackling a research question addressing an issue related to poverty that is well-suited for a randomized evaluation. Their interests spanned the breadth of J-PAL’s work, touching on education, climate, health and labor markets, racial equity, and social protection — reflecting the wide range of policy questions that rigorous, evidence-based research can help answer.
“I really appreciated being a part of the ARTEMIS Institute this summer,” says Felipe Juan, an ARTEMIS inaugural cohort participant. “I initially thought the randomized evaluation methodology would be out of reach for me, but the summer training helped to break down the practical steps of conducting an RCT and identify creative ways to approach experimental designs.”
Bolstered by the intensive Summer Institute training, ARTEMIS participants are now engaging in six months of continued study design and proposal development support, including proposal webinars with J-PAL grants staff and office hours with senior technical staff who will advise on study design and proposal challenges. ARTEMIS participants will also participate in a research design workshop, where participants present their early-stage RCT designs and receive feedback from the broader J-PAL research network. Finally, participants will receive introductions to researchers in the J-PAL network with shared research interests to forge connections that may lead to future collaboration and opportunities. Through this sustained mentorship model, ARTEMIS is designed to help participants bridge the gap between developing a promising research idea and launching a funded, policy-relevant randomized evaluation.
For early-career researchers, this hands-on, sustained support has already proven to be transformative. “Participating in ARTEMIS Summer Institute was an incredibly valuable experience. The combination of lectures by experts in the design and implementation of randomized controlled trials, hands-on workshops, and thoughtful feedback helped me sharpen my research questions and think more carefully about research design, implementation, statistical power, and meaningful stakeholder engagement,” says Hoyoung Yoo, an ARTEMIS 2026 participant. “I also greatly appreciated the opportunity to learn from J-PAL faculty and staff and exchange ideas with an inspiring group of fellow researchers. I left the training with a clearer path toward transforming an early-stage idea into a feasible, rigorous, and policy-relevant evaluation.”
For many, the program’s value also extends beyond technical training to the community and long-term relationships it builds. “J-PAL North America’s support has continued well beyond the Summer Institute, which has been especially valuable, and the connections I made have already started shaping how I am approaching the work,” notes Tessie Krishna, an ARTEMIS 2026 participant. “I left with a clearer proposal, a wider network, and a real sense of belonging in the J-PAL community. I am grateful to the J-PAL team for creating something so thoughtful and welcoming.”
By building the technical capacity and confidence of the next generation of researchers, ARTEMIS is advancing J-PAL’s global mission to reduce poverty by ensuring that policy is informed by rigorous, scientific evidence. Every individual trained through ARTEMIS is joining a growing network of researchers working to answer the most critical questions of today.

Microsoft fixes a Windows 11 annoyance as PC revenue declines - Ars TechnicaSkip to content
Text settingsStory textSizeSmallStandardLargeWidth*StandardWideLinksStandardOrange* Subscribers only
Microsoft is beginning the rollout of a Windows 11 preview update that finally addresses a persistent power user complaint with the operating system: the right-click menu that obliterated years of muscle memory on command locations and hid others behind an additional click. The timing is notable, as the announcement comes alongside Microsoft’s quarterly financial report, which showed a continued decline in the business of selling Windows licenses for new PCs.
The preview update,KB5127936, is cumulative for Windows 11 versions 26H2 and 25H2. The update will be a gradual rollout before eventually moving on to a normal rollout for all Windows 11 devices once it reaches general availability. The highlight of the new update should calm annoyed users who have spent years with custom scripts and services in an attempt to shape Windows the way they would prefer it. Users will get a “customize menu” button that controls what commands appear when they right-click their mouse. Users can toggle built-in commands such as Send To or Create Shortcut on or off, rearrange what appears on the main menu, and control which third-party extensions show up in either the main or submenus. The gripe with the right-click menu had been that Microsoft hid familiar command locations behind a top row of icons while moving other familiar commands under the “Show more options” submenu. Now, Windows users can customize the whole thing around their habits.
The original Windows 11 right-click menu is a mess.Credit:MicrosoftThe original Windows 11 right-click menu is a mess.Credit:Microsoft
The new preview also highlights a new Windows feature called Cloud Rebuild, a recovery option that can reinstall Windows 11 directly from the cloud, even when an existing Windows 11 fails to boot. Cloud Rebuild will pull the Windows 11 image and needed system drivers directly from Windows Update. Users will not need a custom recovery image or external media to reinstall Windows. There is an important distinction to note, however. Microsoft classifies Cloud Rebuild as a recovery option, but it behaves more like a fresh Windows install than a repair, as existing applications and files will not be included. Those worried about data security can sanitize entire system drives prior to reinstalling. For a full list of improvements coming to Windows 11, including changes to Xbox mode and settings, you can view the officialMicrosoft release announcement.
Microsoft’s latest quarterly report, released this week, paints a less encouraging picture of its Windows OEM business. “Windows OEM revenue was below expectations and decreased 27% and 28% in constant currency, driven by the Windows 10 end of support demand in the prior year, inventory drawdowns by OEM and channel partners and weaker PC market demand,” said CFO Amy Hood, according to atranscript of the call. The broader Windows OEM and devices category, which includes Microsoft’s own Surface lineup, fell 22 percent, per the earnings release. Hood went on to state that “we expect these trends to continue through the rest of the fiscal year.”
Recent hardware efforts like theSurface Laptop Ultraand broader RTX Spark platform arrived too late in the quarter to register in the results, and Microsoft forecastfurther dropsbefore any possible boost from new hardware can show in its numbers. The news for Microsoft isn’t negative all around, though, as its Azure platform saw a 48 percent jump, and Microsoft Cloud revenue was also up 30 percent, year over year—now roughly 70 percent of the company’s $92.3 billion total quarterly revenue.

Watch: Has Flávio Bolsonaro left Brazil to evade justice?
ByVanessa Buschschlüter,Latin America and Caribbean editor,Ione Wells,North America correspondentandMax Matza
Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who landed in Miami after losing the presidential election on Sunday, has said it was never his intention to "leave my homeland".
"I did not flee Brazil; I left for the sake of Brazil," he said in his first statement since his departure.
The US provided visas to him and his family after Brazil cancelled his passports as part of a criminal investigation. Bolsonaro denies any wrongdoing. On Wednesday, US President Donald Trump told reporters: "We gave him a pass to come into the country".
Newly re-elected President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva hascriticised Bolsonaro's secretive exit from the country, saying "those who have nothing to hide have nothing to fear".
Watch: Bolsonaro shielded from media by umbrellas at Florida airport
Bolsonaro's arrival in Florida ended days of confusion over his whereabouts, after he was reported to have travelled to Argentina, and then prematurely reported to have already entered the US on Tuesday.
In a statement, Bolsonaro thanked both the presidents of Argentina and the US, and the American public "who share the same values ​​as the good people of my own country".
"It was never my intention to leave my homeland, but I know exactly where this is heading," he said. "I departed from a regime of exception so that I could become the leader my people deserve."
He called himself a victim of a coup d'état and political persecution, and said his travel to the US was to protect his family.
In the lengthy letter, he also repeated unsubstantiated allegations of "electoral fraud" which he said allowed a "mathematical impossibility" to occur in the election.
On Wednesday, Trump declined to discuss the allegations made in Bolsonaro's letter.
"I won't get involved. It was a very strange election, that's for sure," Trump said. He went on to add that he thought Bolsonaro "and his family were treated very unfairly".
After Bolsonaro won the first round of Brazil's election, Lula won the second round by more than four million votes, which was attributed to significantly higher turnout, and swaying more undecided voters.
The result was confirmed by the president of Brazil's top electoral court, who was appointed by Bolsonaro's father, former president Jair Bolsonaro.
Speculation about Bolsonaro's whereabouts was first triggered by a report on an Argentine news site, which claimed that he had crossed the land border between Brazil and Argentina and then boarded a private plane en route to the US.
Brazilian police took the rumours seriously. Early on Tuesday, they checked border crossings but found no evidence that Bolsonaro had left the country, and Argentine officials said they had no reports of him crossing.
For a little while, it seemed like Bolsonaro may just be keeping an uncharacteristically low-profile after being unexpectedly beaten by his left-wing rival in the presidential run-off vote on Sunday, in addition to a criminal investigation that led to orders that his passports be turned into authorities.
But when he failed to surrender his passports in time to meet a 24-hour deadline on Tuesday, Brazilian authorities cancelled the documents and ordered police to make checks at border posts.
Speculation quickly grew that he'd left the country and Bolsonaro's lawyers said they had no idea where he was.
How did Flávio Bolsonaro end up in Miami?
Confusion about Bolsonaro's whereabouts as Argentina says he flew to Ecuador
Hours later on Tuesday evening, several sources told the BBC and other broadcasters that he was on his way to the US.
A cousin, who is close to Flávio Bolsonaro and his younger brother Eduardo, told BBC Brasil that the defeated right-wing candidate had arrived in Miami.
Another close aide to Eduardo Bolsonaro told BBC Mundo that Flávio was with his younger brother in Miami.
Neither Flávio nor Eduardo Bolsonaro could be reached directly for comment at the time.
But later, however, Argentine migration authorities posted on social media saying that Bolsonaro, his wife, and two daughters had only just crossed into Argentina over land on Tuesday night local time.
Flight tracking data verified by the BBC suggested the Bolsonaros departed from Puerto Iguazú in Argentina at 00:18 local time (03:18 GMT) on Wednesday to head to Guayaquil in Ecuador.
After a brief stop, the same private jet took them to Miami-Opa Locka Executive Airport, where they were pictured disembarking just before 09:30 local time (13:30 GMT).
Photographers, who had been waiting for his arrival to finally put an end to all the speculation, swarmed around Bolsonaro as he left the airport in Miami, while his team tried to cover him with umbrellas.
Later, Eduardo Bolsonaro posted a photo with his brother Flávio on social media, with the location listed as "United States".
The caption read: "Today's photo after reuniting with my brother Flavio Bolsonaro. Yesterday was a long day, perhaps the longest of my life. But we prevailed. Even here outside, we will not give up on Brazil."
Flávio Bolsonaro is not the first member of his family to travel to the United States.
His father, Jair Bolsonaro, also left Brazil for Florida in December 2022 before his successor, Lula, was inaugurated.
Jair was still in the US when his supportersstormed Brazil's government buildings and Supreme Courton 8 January. He later used his absence as part of his defence in his coup trial, which ultimately led to his conviction and 27-year sentence.
Flávio's brother, Eduardo Bolsonaro, meanwhile, has been living in Texas after taking leave from Brazil's Congress. While in the US, he lobbied officials there in an attempt to influence the coup trial of his father, which led to the US imposing punitive tariffs on Brazil and sanctions on key officials.
Eduardo wasconvicted in absentiaover this by Brazil's highest court earlier this year.
It is not yet clear what Flávio Bolsonaro's ultimate destination will be, nor how long he plans to stay in the US.
He is the subject of two investigations currently pending before Brazil's Supreme Federal Court.
One is regarding possible irregularities in the transfer of nearly $70m (£53m) from private bank Banco Master to the film Dark Horse – a biopic about his father.

lead_title: Democrats have high hopes for midterms, but polls have let them down before

evidence_pages.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmg4:
Democrats have high hopes for midterms, but polls have let them down before - BBC News
Image source,Getty ImagesByAnthony ZurcherNorth America correspondent
The Democratic Party has high expectations as it heads into these pivotal US midterm elections.
A historically unpopular Republican president, an American public unhappy with the rising costs of food and bills, and months of favourable polls point to a good night for them on Tuesday.
Democratic candidates lead in well over the 218 seats needed to flip control of the lower chamber of Congress, the House of Representatives, the polls suggest. And they are tied or narrowly ahead in the key Senate races.
A recent New York Times poll had the Senate race in South Carolina, a state Donald Trump won by 18 percentage points in 2024, as a tie. Recent CNN surveys put the Democrats ahead in Texas, Kansas and Maine.
Recent US political history is littered with examples where public opinion polls, even ones just days before an election, were off the mark. Trump outperformed predictions on his way to White House victories in 2016 and 2024. His narrow defeat in 2020 came after most surveys indicated a more comfortable win for Democrat Joe Biden.
Earlier this year, polls suggested Democrat Abdul El-Sayed was poised for a double-digit win in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary. Instead it was 1%. In Wisconsin's Democratic primary for governor, the candidate that had a polling lead that approached 20 points lost by a fraction of a percent.
Democrats have an identity crisis - it won't be an easy fix
According to Clifford Young, president of Ipsos Public Affairs, which conducts political and market research surveys, polling has become difficult in recent years because it's harder to reach Americans as they abandon their land lines and screen their calls. And many of those who pollsters do contact have become less willing to participate.
"Conservatives, especially those on the far right, are much more anti-establishment by nature," Young says. "And they don't participate in anything. They hate the system. That's the challenge."
If Republican voters are being undercounted in a systematic way, and polling companies don't take that into consideration when constructing their voting models, it could skew their data towards the Democrats.
That's one of the reasons why it has become trickier for pollsters to predict what the electorate will look like.
IN DEPTH: The real reasons there are so few young US politicians
EXPLORE: Where the US midterms will be won and lost
VERIFY: How the US economy is really doing under Trump
NEWSLETTER: Sign up for Anthony Zurcher's analysis in your inbox
One explanation for why Trump overperformed in previous presidential elections is that his supporters – many of whom were not regular voters – flocked to the polls in higher-than-expected numbers.
That unpredictability is one of the main contributing factors to those notable recent polling misses, even if the margins in most reputable polls were only off by a few percentage points.
In a close race, those few points can make the difference between victory and defeat for a candidate. And this year, many of the key Senate races are within those narrow margins.
What's at stake for Trump in the US midterms?
In recent years, midterm general election polls have proven to be more accurate, in part because Trump - and his unique ability to draw disaffected Americans to the polls - was not on the ballot.
In 2022, they suggested Democrats would defy conventional expectations and avoid an electoral wipe-out despite Biden's low approval numbers.
While the party lost control of the House of Representatives, the margins were slim and Democrats maintained control of the US Senate.
While this year's primary results did provide bigger surprises, Young says that nominating contests have historically been volatile, with voters more likely to make up their minds at the last minute. It shouldn't be seen as an indication that the current crop of general election polls are off the mark.
It's common for the party of the president to have a bad night in the midterms.
One of the most notable examples in recent years came in 2010 when Republicans flipped more than 60 House seats and made gains in the Senate.
It came off the back of an economy struggling to recover from the financial crash and conservative fears over President Barack Obama's healthcare reforms. A defeat had been predicted by the polls but not quite on that scale.
The roles are reversed this time, with the Democrats in opposition and the economy on the minds of voters. But there are a number of reasons why Democrats may not have as good a night as history might suggest or as some might expect, given Trump's low approval rating.
Firstly, much of the territory in play in this election Trump conquered with ease in the presidential election just two years ago. It's like a home game for Republicans.
Then there have been changes to House election boundaries over the years that have meant fewer seats switch between parties.
Thirdly, there are fewer swing voters due to the deeper polarisation of the country. Some experts describe the electorate as calcified.
There's also the cash advantage Republicans have enjoyed which has given them hundreds of millions of dollars to spend on attack ads in the final weeks.
Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,
Obama gives a press conference the day after the heavy 2010 midterms defeat
Polling models try to capture shifting fundamentals. And a well-designed poll is built to anticipate issues that may make it less than reliable.
Individual polls do have a built-in margin of error – a statistical level of uncertainty based on the sampling size compared to the population as a whole. Taken as an aggregate, polling averages and not individual surveys can provide a more accurate prediction.
At the moment, even the kind of polling lean we saw in recent presidential elections would suggest Democrats are likely to have a good night on 3 November. And polling inaccuracies can go both ways. In last year's state and special elections, Democrats outperformed most surveys as it was their voters who turned out in unexpectedly larger numbers.
The sight of Trump holding rallies in the final days of the campaign in states he won comfortably in 2024 will have lifted Democrats' hopes that Republican internal polling has conservative candidates in trouble.

Democrats could target prediction markets after midtermsSkip Navigation
MarketsBusinessInvestingTechPolitics & PolicyVideoWatchlistInvesting ClubPROLivestreamMenu
Lawmakers in Washington haven't done much to support or rein in prediction markets beyond rhetoric, but that may change.
Democrats disproportionately have proposed legislation to tackle prediction markets in the current Congress, and leading companies Kalshi and Polymarket's ties to President Donald Trump's son could make them ripe candidates for oversight inquiries.
At the same time, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the regulator for event contracts, could face increased questions on whether it has the capability to regulate these booming markets.
The Capitol in Washington, Sept. 16, 2026.Daniel Heuer | Bloomberg | Getty Images
The rise of prediction markets has confounded Washington, with lawmakers still learning how the exchanges work — and little done in Congress to support or rein in the companies. But themidterm electionsmay spark movement, with both platforms and their regulator set to come under increased scrutiny as part of a broader oversight agenda by the Democratic Party.
For now, prediction markets have appeared as a nonpartisan issue, with both supporters and opponents on each side of the aisle.
Nearly 30prediction market-related billshave been introduced in both chambers since 2025, with most sponsored by Democrats and introduced in the House of Representatives. Those measures focus on banning orrestricting congressional members and stafffrom participating on the platforms andprohibiting particular contracts, primarily sports-related ones.
With polls signaling Democrats are on track to flipthe Housenext month, those bills and proponents seeking totackle the industrymay stand a better chance to succeed under Democratic leaderHakeem Jeffries.
Even beyond any sort of legislation, Democrats through committee investigative powers could confrontPresident Donald Trump'sson, Donald Trump Jr., and his advisory role with leading companiesKalshiandPolymarket, whichmany Democrats, and evensome Republicans, fear may have been used to gain favorable regulatory rulings from the administration.
The regulator in question, theCommodity Futures Trading Commission, may face greater scrutiny too. Some lawmakers have worried whether the agency, after recent staffing cuts, can handle oversight of the booming prediction markets industry.
The CFTC disputes that concern, telling CNBC its work in other markets proves it can handle emerging event contracts. Meanwhile, both leading platforms said they welcome engagement with lawmakers and even potential legislation as the industry grows.
"We welcome scrutiny," a Polymarket spokesperson said in a statement. "We are a new concept to most and our biggest problem is typically a lack of understanding of the way our platform operates … We want to work with lawmakers and staff to ensure all the promise and value of prediction markets is captured and regulations meet the scale and scope of the massive demand for the product."
Why Democrats might go after platforms
While both parties have expressed concerns over prediction markets, where things might get more partisan is over Trump Jr.'s role as anadvisor at bothKalshiand Polymarket.
His venture capital firm1789 Capitalalso has an investment in the latter company, though a spokesperson told CNBC that Trump Jr. doesn't sit on the firm's investment decision-making committee and "therefore has no ability to allocate capital to companies." The spokesperson added Trump Jr.'s advisory role at Polymarket was done outside of the firm's investment.
Both leading prediction market companies have soughtfavorable CFTC rulings, including for new products and ongoing rulemaking in the emerging space, as they grow, and some lawmakers have worried how Trump Jr.'srole may impactthose decisions.
"I know that the appearance of conflicts of interest was significant enough that aRepublican senator called for a probeinto Don Trump Jr. interests and specifically his interests in polymarket and culture," said Joseph Konizeski, a former trial attorney in the CFTC, referencing a letter by Sen. John Curtis, R-Utah, a skeptic of prediction markets. "So when you have a Republican senator making that sort of a public plea, I think that that tells you that it's a serious issue."
The office for U.S. Rep.Robert Garcia, D-Calif., who is set to be the chair of theHouse Oversight and Government Reform Committeeif Democrats retake the chamber, did not respond to a request for comment.
A spokesperson for the president's son called the concerns on his relationship and role on the platforms as politically motivated.
"Democrats are obsessed with harassing Don because of his last name, despite having zero evidence that he has actually engaged in any wrongdoing whatsoever," the spokesperson said in a statement. "Don does not ever interface with the Federal Government on behalf of any company that he advises or invests in."
A person familiar with Polymarket's operations said the company's investors and advisors, such as Trump Jr., give business and strategic advice. Polymarket's internal management and legal teams handle regulatory obligations, the person added.
Donald Trump Jr., co-founder of World Liberty Financial, during the Future Investment Initiative Priority Summit conference in Miami, Florida, March 27, 2026.Zak Bennett | Bloomberg | Getty Images
Both Kalshi and Polymarket also have relationships with Democrats too. Former President Barack Obama staffer Stephanie Cutter is a senior policy advisor at Kalshi, while Polymarket hired in September Rob Eskridge, a former chief of staff to a Democratic congressman, to lead its government relations team.
Kalshi CEOTarek Mansoursaid last week on MS NOW that Trump Jr.'s connection to the company creates an "optics issue," but added that it has never used that relationship to gain favor with the U.S. government.
Over the past nine months, Kalshi has had numerous conversations with lawmakers over Trump Jr.'s role in the company, reassuring them that the president's son solely advises on its marketing, the platform said. The company added it has seen bipartisan progress with lawmakers on how they view prediction markets by noting the benefits of a federally regulated exchange rather than one hosted offshore.

European football: Mbappé penalty helps Real Madrid stroll to sixth straight win | European club football | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation
Kylian Mbappé shows his elation after opening the scoring for Real Madrid with Dean Huijsen.Photograph: Vincent West/ReutersView image in fullscreenKylian Mbappé shows his elation after opening the scoring for Real Madrid with Dean Huijsen.Photograph: Vincent West/Reuters
European football: Mbappé penalty helps Real Madrid stroll to sixth straight win
Bellingham and Diomandé complete 3-0 win over Racing
Lazio top Serie A after fighting back to beat Cagliari
Kylian Mbappé moved on from a tumultuous week by scoring a penalty to help Real Madrid win 3-0 atRacing Santanderon Sunday.
The French forward narrowlylost out on the Ballon d’Orto Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane on Monday and then had to apologise after a social media storm following a video inwhich he jokedabout the former Chinese leader Mao Zedong.
European football: Kane misses penalty as Dortmund share spoils in Der KlassikerRead more
Real Madrid’s match, along with other Spanish fixtures this weekend, was not broadcast by Chinese state television because of the fallout.
Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomandé were also on target to keep third-placed Madrid within three points of theLa Ligaleaders, Barcelona, who thrashed Alavés 6-1 on Saturday.
José Mourinho’s side have won six straight games across all competitions and are a point behind Atlético Madrid, who beat Levante 2-0.
Real Sociedad’s four-match winning run came to an end after they lost 2-1 toAthletic Bilbaothanks to first-half goals from Inaki Williams and Alex Berenguer, who scored a penalty.
Gennaro Gattuso’sLazioconsolidated their position at the top of Serie A with a 2-1 victory overCagliari, nudging ahead of Inter after the two clubs had started the weekend level on points.
Lazio made a poor start as Cagliari took the lead through M’Bala Nzola in the 20th minute before goals in either half from Gustav Isaksen and Andrea Pinamonti gave them a sixth straightSerie Awin.
Comomoved back into the top four as they eked out a 1-0 victory at home over bottom sideVeneziaon Sunday for a fifth consecutive victory across all competitions.
The hosts dominated, but needed a penalty to find the back of the net. TheComocaptain, Lucas Da Cunha, converted in the 43rd minute for the French international’s first goal of the season. “This is the type of match we found hard to win last season,” Da Cunha told DAZN.
Second-half goals from Kerim Alajbegovic and Jeremie Boga ensuredJuventusreturned to winning ways with a 2-0 victory over 10-manNapoli,who had Luca Marianucci sent off in the second half as they slipped to their fourth defeat of the campaign.
LyonandParis FCboth won to close in on the defending Ligue 1 champions, Paris Saint-Germain, with the capital team defeatingMonaco3-1.
View image in fullscreenLyon’s Corentin Tolisso embraces coach Paulo Fonseca after scoring the second goal against Angers.Photograph: Manon Cruz/Reuters
Lyon won 2-0 at home toAngerswith goals in each half from Ernest Nuamah and Corentin Tolisso, as they bounced back from a 2-0 defeat away to PSG last time out.

Kimi Antonelli became the youngest Formula 1 world champion in history after finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix.
Formula 1 has its 36th world champion after Kimi Antonelli clinched his maiden title by finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix.
The Italian youngster has reached the summit of motorsport in just his second season at the top levelafter a stellar campaign in which he has won nine races for Mercedes.
And while a world championship triumph for any driver is notable, Antonelli's first title carries particularly strong historical significance.

Beating Vettel's 16-year youngest benchmark
Formula 1 has a new youngest world champion in the sport's 76-year history.
After holding the record for 16 years, Sebastian Vettel spell as F1's youngest-ever champion has been beaten - by a full three years.

Vettel was aged 23 years and 134 days when he won the first of his four world titles with Red Bull in 2010.
Antonelli clinched his maiden crown aged 20 years and 68 days, a record that may well stand for decades - if not, all time.
In modern times, Antonelli follows Jacques Villeneuve (1997) and Lewis Hamilton (2008) in winning his first F1 title in just his second year competing in the top category of single-seater racing. Juan-Manuel Fangio also won his first of five crowns in the second season of the F1 world championship in 1951, although the Argentine had already been competing in Grand Prix racing before 1950.
Sebastian Vettel congratulated Kimi Antonelli on breaking his record as the youngest ever Formula 1 world champion.
Ending Italy's seven-decade wait for another champion
Antonelli has also made history as an Italian driver in F1.
Considering an Italian won three of the first four Drivers' Championships following F1's inception in 1950, and Ferrari is the sport's most successful team, there had been a dearth of individual success in recent decades before Antonelli came along.
Antonelli is Italy's first world champion since 1953, when Alberto Ascari clinched his second and final title.

Antonelli's nine wins this year have already put him second to Ascari (13) in the list of Italian race winners.
One of those wins came on home soil, at Monza in September, which made Antonelli the first Italian winner of the Italian Grand Prix since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966.
The other records Antonelli has beaten
While Max Verstappen's win as an 18-year-old at the 2016 Spanish Grand Prix remains the youngest for a driver in F1, Antonelli is the only driver to win multiple races as a teenager.
He won six races before his 20th birthday in August.
He did become the sport's youngest polesitter (China) and the youngest to lead the world championship (Japan) this year, along with the youngest to claim a pole-win-fastest lap hat-trick (China). He is also the youngest to achieve a Grand Slam - which requires a driver to add the lead of every race lap to a hat-trick - in Monaco.

Kimi Antonelli heads list of F1's youngest champions from Vettel, Hamilton, Alonso, Verstappen and Fittipaldi - BBC Sport
Kimi Antonelli has made history by becoming the youngest title winner in the 77th year of the Formula 1 World Championship.
The Italian, at 20 years and 68 days, has beaten the record of Sebastian Vettel, who was 23 years and 134 days old when he won the first of his four drivers' championships in 2010.
Antonelli, who was still a teenager until 25 August, has secured the title in his second season in the sport.
We take a look at F1's other young champions and how Antonelli's achievement compares with theirs.
Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,
Kimi Antonelli is the youngest F1 world champion and has won nine grands prix since his debut in 2025
Stage of his F1 career when title was won:Second full season
F1 debut:2025 Australian Grand Prix (aged 18)
Antonelli has already broken a number of records on the way to becoming F1's youngest champion.
In his second season, he became the youngest driver to achieve a pole position in China and the youngest to lead the championship at the next race in Japan.
In Monaco, he became the youngest driver to complete a 'grand slam' of pole position, fastest lap, leading every lap and winning the race.
All this after a rookie season in 2025 in which there were occasional highs but plenty of errors, and his final total of 150 points was less than half of the 319 accumulated by Mercedes team-mate George Russell.
Sebastian Vettel's four drivers' championships were won between 2010-13
Stage of his F1 career when title was won:Third full season
F1 debut:2007 US Grand Prix (aged 19)
Vettel was one of four drivers who could win the title going into the season-ending 2010 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.
He was far from the best placed, though, trailing Ferrari's Fernando Alonso by 15 points before the race and his Red Bull team-mate Mark Webber by seven.
The German did what he had to do by winning the grand prix and Alonso could only finish seventh, having become stuck behind the Renault of Vitaly Petrov.
With Webber in eighth, Vettel won the championship by four points from Alonso.
It was yet another F1 record for Vettel. He had become the youngest F1 points scorer on his debut for BMW Sauber in Indianapolis in 2007, before becoming the then youngest pole sitter and race winner at the 2008 Italian Grand Prix for Toro Rosso.
Lewis Hamilton won the 2008 championship by overtaking Timo Glock into the final corner of the Brazilian Grand Prix
F1 debut:2007 Australian Grand Prix (aged 22)
Lewis Hamilton's debut season in 2007 almost delivered a fairytale title but he faltered in the final two races of the year.
He failed to score in China and finished seventh in Brazil, which allowed Ferrari's Kimi Raikkonen to pip both Hamilton and fellow McLaren driver Fernando Alonso by a single point.
Somehow the climax to the 2008 championship, also in Brazil, was even more dramatic.
Hamilton was battling for the title with Ferrari's home favourite Felipe Massa and the Briton's fourth place was going to be enough to secure the crown when a late rain shower changed everything.
Leader Massa and Hamilton were among those who changed to intermediate tyres but Toyota's Timo Glock stayed out, which lifted him up to fourth.
Hamilton, now in fifth, had Toro Rosso's Vettel right behind him and couldn't afford to lose another position. With just over two laps to go, he ran wide and Vettel was through.
Massa crossed the line to win the race with Hamilton still sixth. The Ferrari pit crew, Massa's family and the Brazilian fans celebrated but with the rain intensifying, Glock was slowing on his dry-weather tyres and Hamilton passed him into the final corner to take the title by a single point. It was heart-stopping stuff.
Fernando Alonso made his F1 debut in 2001 for Minardi and was Renault's reserve driver in 2002 before being promoted to the race team in 2003
Stage of his F1 career when title was won:Fourth full season
F1 debut:2001 Australian Grand Prix (aged 19)
Alonso established control of the 2005 championship early in the season by winning four of the first seven races and never relinquished it.
The Spaniard's speed and consistency ensured he prevailed over Raikkonen, whose McLaren-Mercedes was fast but fragile. A third place at the Brazilian Grand Prix was enough to give Alonso the title with two races to spare.
He won a second consecutive title in 2006, also for Renault, and the 45-year-old remains one of the great personalities and outstanding talents in F1.
He'll be back for another season with Aston Martin in 2027, 26 years after his debut for Minardi.
Max Verstappen remains the youngest driver to win an F1 race, having done so in his first race for Red Bull in Spain in 2016 at 18 years and 228 days
Stage of his F1 career when title was won:Seventh full season
F1 debut:2015 Australian Grand Prix (aged 17)
Hamilton won the title on the final lap of the 2008 season but he would lose it on the final lap in 2021 in circumstances that remain a source of huge controversy.
His rival in a thrilling and intense season-long duel was Red Bull's Max Verstappen. There were plenty of flashpoints along the way and it all came to a climax in Abu Dhabi.
Verstappen and Hamilton went into the final race of the season level on points. The Dutchman qualified on pole but Mercedes' Hamilton beat him off the line and largely controlled the race thereafter, until Williams' Nicholas Latifi crashed with five laps to go, bringing out a safety car.
Hamilton did not have enough of an advantage over second-placed Verstappen to pit for fresh tyres and maintain the lead, so stayed out. Verstappen, with nothing to lose, came in and fitted softs.
Race director Michael Masi allowed the lapped cars between Hamilton and Verstappen to go past, but not those behind the Red Bull. He allowed the race to restart for one final racing lap and Verstappen overtook Hamilton, who was a sitting duck on his old hard tyres.
Verstappen and Hamilton, in their own ways, were both stunned and Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff shouted over the radio to Masi: "No, Michael, no! That was so not right!"
As happened with Vettel from 2010-13, this was the first of four consecutive titles for a Red Bull driver with Verstappen dominating the 2022, 2023 and 2024 seasons.

lead_title: Scientists discover a surprising brain benefit of eating peanuts every day

evidence_pages.https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20:
Scientists discover a surprising brain benefit of eating peanuts every day | ScienceDaily
Science Newsfrom research organizations
Scientists discover a surprising brain benefit of eating peanuts every day
Date:November 1, 2026Source:The Peanut InstituteSummary:A surprising new study suggests that eating peanuts every day could help support brain health and memory in older adults. Researchers found that consuming about two servings of unsalted, skin-roasted peanuts daily for 16 weeks improved insulin responsiveness in brain regions important for memory, a function that often weakens with age and has been linked to Alzheimer's disease.Share:FacebookTwitterPinterestLinkedINEmailFULL STORYEating peanuts every day may help protect the aging brain by improving insulin responsiveness in regions critical for memory. Credit: AI/ScienceDaily.com
Eating peanuts every day may offer surprising benefits for the aging brain. Researchers at Maastricht University Medical Center in the Netherlands have found that regularly consuming unsalted, skin-roasted peanuts can improve how certain brain regions respond to insulin in older adults. The findings come from the Institute of Nutrition and Translational Research in Metabolism (NUTRIM) and were published in the peer-reviewed journalFood & Function.
Although insulin is best known for regulating blood sugar, it also plays an essential role in the brain. It helps nerve cells grow, survive, and communicate with one another, supporting memory and other cognitive abilities. Healthy insulin signaling may also help protect against processes associated with Alzheimer's disease.
After participants consumed peanuts daily for 16 weeks, researchers observed improved insulin responsiveness in a group of brain regions in the right hemisphere. These included portions of the lingual gyrus, hippocampus, parahippocampal gyrus, and posterior cingulate gyrus, all of which contribute to memory-related processes.
"The hormone insulin plays an important role in the brain, where it supports memory and other cognitive processes. As people age, the brain may become less responsive to insulin, which has been linked to age-related cognitive decline," says Dr. Peter Joris, the study's senior author and an associate professor in the Department of Nutrition and Movement Sciences, NUTRIM, Maastricht University Medical Center. "Our study found that daily peanut consumption beneficially affected insulin responsiveness in memory-related brain regions in older adults. These findings suggest that enhanced regional brain insulin responsiveness may contribute to the cognitive benefits of unsalted, skin-roasted peanut intake."
Daily Peanuts Linked to Better Memory and Brain Blood Flow
The study included 31 healthy adults between the ages of 60 and 75. During the peanut consumption phase, participants ate 60 grams (approximately two servings) of peanuts each day for 16 weeks. Researchers used a randomized, controlled crossover trial, a rigorous study design that allowed them to compare the effects of eating peanuts with those of avoiding them.
The new findings build on earlier research by Joris published in 2025. That investigation found that consuming peanuts for 16 weeks increased overall cerebral blood flow (CBF) by 3.6% and improved verbal memory performance by 5.8%.
Cerebral blood flow measures how much blood circulates through the brain, carrying oxygen and nutrients that brain cells need to function properly. It is an important indicator of the health of the brain's blood vessels. Those earlier results appeared in the peer-reviewed journalClinical Nutrition.
How Scientists Measured the Effects of Peanuts on the Brain
One distinguishing feature of the NUTRIM research was its combination of a carefully controlled dietary intervention lasting several months with sophisticated brain imaging technology.
To examine changes in brain function, researchers used arterial spin labeling magnetic resonance imaging (ASL-MRI), a technique that measures blood flow in different regions of the brain. They evaluated insulin responsiveness by tracking changes in regional cerebral blood flow after insulin was administered through the nose.
The team also used abdominal MRI scans to measure fat accumulation in the liver, known as intrahepatic lipid (IHL) content. Cognitive abilities were assessed using the Cambridge Neuropsychological Test Automated Battery (CANTAB), a standardized collection of computerized tests.
Researchers believe several components of peanuts may contribute to their observed effects on brain health, rather than any single nutrient being responsible.
"Multiple nutrients present in peanuts, including unsaturated fats, dietary fiber, vitamins and minerals and bioactive phytochemicals, could potentially contribute to the observed brain benefits," says Joris. "Peanuts are also a good source of plant-based protein and are especially rich in L-arginine. L-arginine is a key precursor of nitric oxide (NO), which has been reported to facilitate learning and memory performance."
What Participants Ate During the 16-Week Study
To ensure participants consumed a consistent amount, researchers supplied premeasured packets of skin-roasted peanuts throughout the peanut intervention period.
Participants were instructed to eat their peanuts in the morning or afternoon, but they could choose how to incorporate them into their daily routine. They could consume the entire portion at once, divide it into smaller amounts throughout the day, or include the peanuts in their meals.
During the control phase, participants avoided peanuts entirely. After 16 weeks, they switched to the opposite study condition, allowing researchers to compare brain health measurements under both dietary approaches.
The study was led by principal investigator Associate Professor Dr. Peter J. Joris and conducted by Ph.D. candidate Lucia Kerkhof of the Department of Nutrition and Movement Sciences at Maastricht University Medical Center.
Funding was provided by The Peanut Institute Foundation. According to the researchers, the foundation had no involvement in designing or conducting the study, analyzing or interpreting the results, or preparing the manuscript.

What Democrats Can Learn From New York’s Data Center Moratorium | WIREDSkip to main content
Welcome back toPower Play! Each week, senior writer Molly Taft tackles a topic around this midterm season’s biggest issue: data centers. If you’ve got a question or thought for the column, feel free to shoot Molly an email at[email protected]or reach them securely on Signal at mollytaft.76.
When New York became the first state in the country to enact amoratorium on data center development, Adrienne Yocina was excited. For the past two years, the mom of three has been organizing in western Genesee County to stop a 600-megawatt data center from coming to a site close to the Tonawanda Seneca Nation’s reservation and a federal wildlife refuge.
But almost four months after the one-year moratorium began, Yocina tells me that she’s “getting nervous.” She’s worried that Democratic governor Kathy Hochul won’t sign a stronger bill to impose a stricter moratorium, and is concerned that the state Department of Environmental Conservation is not adequately involved in the process of evaluating data centers in New York.
“I feel like she’s just trying to shut us up,” she says of Hochul.
Data centers are at the center ofmidterm races across the country, with politicians of both parties making promises to enact regulations or moratoriums on development. After next week comes the tough part: Newly elected officials must either break their word or follow through on those promises as they weigh large infrastructure projects coming to their states and residents who say they’ll reject data centers no matter what.
How will those compromises go—and will they appease voters? New York’s moratorium, and the continued opposition from some groups, may offer clues.
In July, just two months after dismissing the idea of adata center moratorium, Hochul signed the nation’s first executive order to put a pause on development. Her order was a compromise. Just weeks prior, the state legislature had passed an omnibus bill that would have implemented a one-year moratorium throughout New York. The bill contained several provisions that made it more aggressive than Hochul’s moratorium, including stricter limits on the size of data centers and a mandate that the Department of Environmental Conservation conduct a thorough environmental impact review of data center operations. Rather than sign the bill, Hochul issued her own order. (The governor has until the end of the year to sign that bill, and her office says they are still looking at it.)
One of the bill’s State Senate sponsors, Democrat Kristen Gonzalez, has been publicly supportive of Hochul’s moratorium. The governor’s office, Gonzalez says, proactively reached out to her after her bill passed to help design the moratorium for more immediate relief for New Yorkers.
Gonzalez went on adata center tour of New Yorkat the end of the summer, talking to residents around the state about their concerns. She told me that the people she talked to overwhelmingly wanted Hochul to go further and implement more aggressive measures to protect communities from data centers.
“There are local communities statewide that are living near existing data centers, dealing with significant air pollution and noise pollution, who are struggling with rising utility bills and rising water bills,” she told me. “We see the moratorium as a first step, but it can’t be the last.”
Hochul has a comfortable lead over Republican challenger Bruce Blakeman ahead of Tuesday’s election—something that may have been helped by the moratorium’s passing. In arecent Quinnipiac pollof New York voters, 53 percent of respondents said they trusted Hochul to do a better job in handling AI and data centers, compared to just 31 percent trusting Blakeman. Blakeman, who hasvoiced supportfor data centers, called Hochul’s moratorium “crazy” when it was passed in July. His campaign didn’t immediately respond to WIRED’s request for comment.
Hochul has also touted her tough-on-data-center bona fides on the campaign trail. Early last month, she hosted a roundtable discussion on data centers with agricultural, environmental, and business leaders at a farm in the Hudson Valley. There, she told reporters that she wanted to work with the state legislature to implement more aggressive protections, including banning tax breaks for data centers. At the event, Hochul was flanked by Gonzalez and Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, one of Washington’s most prominent data center critics.
I asked Hochul at the event how she anticipates handling continued opposition after her moratorium ends. How does New York balance economic development with community opposition if some people don’t want data centers in their backyards under any circumstances, even with the assurances from the state that Hochul’s office is working to create?
The purpose of her pause, she said, was that communities should be able to choose. “This is democracy in action,” she said. “If you want it, it should come with all kinds of guardrails and restraints, but if you don’t want it, it doesn’t come.”
More New Yorkers may end up choosing the latter option. ASiena pollfrom September found that 63 percent of New Yorkers would oppose data centers being built in their area even after Hochul’s moratorium expires. (It’s even higher for New York Democrats, with 75 percent saying they’d remain opposed to data center development post-moratorium.)
Many newly elected (or reelected) governors will face a similar dynamic: At least 20 gubernatorial candidates have promised a data center moratorium or pause, according toresearchcompiled by government relations company MultiState. Even more have promised to regulate the industry more tightly. Formerly data-center-friendly incumbents like Texas’s Greg Abbott and Pennsylvania’s Josh Shapiro have also made pledges to be stricter on their development.
Come January, new governors will face highly engaged constituents who are finding a political home for the first time in the fight against data centers. That includes Yocina, who says she had never voted in a local election before.
She says she understands the need for industries and jobs in upstate New York: Her youngest son decided to join the Army after a fruitless job search and is about to be deployed. Now, her organizing group is moving from focusing on just stopping the data center to brainstorming new ideas for the site.

Manchester United Munich air disaster memorial items stolen - BBC News
Image source,Manchester Munich Memorial FoundationImage caption,
The glass display case at Manchesterplatz, which has been fixed, contains memorabilia and tributes commemorating the Munich air disaster
A glass sculpture and medals have been stolen from a memorial to the 23 people killed in the Munich air disaster, including eight Manchester United players.
The items were taken from a display case at Manchesterplatz in Munich,where the plane crashed on take-off on 6 February 1958after refuelling on its return from a European Cup match in Belgrade.
Munich Police said the glass case around the memorial was smashed with a rock when the items were taken between 08:00 and 13:00 local time on Monday 26 October.
The Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation (MMMF) said it was "deeply saddened", while its chair, Ifty Ahmed, said the theft had caused emotional harm to families.
The memorial foundation said the glass was repaired on the same day, but some memorabilia remains missing
The foundation's chair has said it was still unclear exactly how many medals were missing
"They don't understand the damage that they've caused," Ahmed told BBC News.
He said the memorial had provided solace for families who lost loved ones in the crash.
"And whatever they've taken from inside the showcase, they haven't taken our memories," he said.
Ifty Ahmed (second left) has urged those responsible to return the stolen items, saying they mean so much to Manchester United supporters and families of those killed in the Munich air disaster
Mark Salzmann, chairman of Red Docs Munich, a Bayern Munich supporters' group which helps care for the memorial, said his mother discovered the damage while driving past.
Salzmann said a glass sculpture originally presented to Munich's former mayor, Dieter Reiter, was among the stolen items.
His group collects tributes left by visitors from around the world and places some of them in the display case.
He said the objects were unique and could not easily be replaced, but the group was discussing possible replacements with the foundation.
About 1,500 people attended the annual remembrance service at Manchesterplatz in February, according to the memorial foundation
Ahmed said it was still unclear exactly how many medals were missing.
He said Manchester United had offered to pay for repairs, but the foundation had already agreed to cover the costs itself.
The broken glass was replaced on the same day, according to the foundation.
Ahmed said supporters of Liverpool, Manchester City and Leeds had also sent messages of support.
Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,
Eight Manchester United players were among 23 passengers killed in the Munich air crash in 1958
A scarf bearing the date 6 February 1958, marking the Munich air disaster
A memorial stone was installed in 2004, while the display case was added in 2020 and officially inaugurated in 2023.
About 1,500 people from around the world attended the annual remembrance service at Manchesterplatz in February, according to the foundation.
Salzmann said the messages of support he had received showed how important the memorial was, adding that the connection between Manchester and Munich "will never go away".
Police said no suspects had been arrested and appealed for witnesses or anyone with information to come forward.
The BBC has contacted Manchester United for comment.

Nhà vô địch Olympia 2026: "Em học kiến thức mới trên Wikipedia"
(Dân trí) - Giành 240 điểm và trở thành quán quân Đường lên đỉnh Olympia năm thứ 26, Đoàn Lê Anh Đức cho biết em rất vui, xúc động khi nhìn lại hành trình 6 năm nỗ lực để chạm tới ước mơ của mình.
Sau khi xuất sắc giành vòng nguyệt quế chung cuộc tại trận chung kết Đường lên đỉnh Olympia năm thứ 26 ngày 1/11, Đoàn Lê Anh Đức, Trường THPT chuyên Hà Nội - Amsterdam đã có những chia sẻ về hành trình chinh phục cuộc thi.
Bảo vệ thành công chức vô địch cho trường
Khác với hình ảnh quyết đoán, những câu trả lời dứt khoát và giọng nói đầy tự tin trong các phần thi, khi được hỏi về cảm xúc sau chiến thắng, Anh Đức trở nên trầm lắng hơn.
Nam sinh cho biết em rất vui, xúc động khi nhìn lại chặng đường đã qua và cho rằng có chút may mắn. "Hành trình ấy suốt 6 năm nay là sự nỗ lực không ngừng. Em đã có thêm khá nhiều bạn bè và cuối cùng đạt được mong muốn của mình", Anh Đức nói và chia sẻ ước mơ đi thi Đường lên đỉnh Olympia từ khi học lớp 6.
Tân quán quân cũng gửi lời cảm ơn đến gia đình, thầy cô, bạn bè và tất cả những người đã theo dõi, cổ vũ em trong suốt cuộc thi.
Nhà vô địch Đoàn Lê Anh Đức (Ảnh: VTV).
Anh Đức cho biết, khoảnh khắc được xướng tên ở vị trí nhà vô địch mang đến niềm vui rất lớn. Em cũng tự hào khi Trường THPT chuyên Hà Nội - Amsterdam có hai năm liên tiếp giành chức vô địch Đường lên đỉnh Olympia và em là người đã bảo vệ thành công chức vô địch cho trường.
Nhìn lại trận chung kết, Anh Đức cho rằng vẫn có những thời điểm bản thân có thể làm tốt hơn. Ở phần thi Vượt chướng ngại vật, nam sinh đã suy nghĩ đến các dữ liệu và từng nghĩ đến từ khóa "học", nhưng chưa tìm ra đáp án chính xác là "tự học".
Trong phần thi Về đích, với một câu hỏi toán học, Anh Đức thừa nhận đã tính toán hơi vội vàng, chưa thật sự cẩn thận. Nam sinh cũng cho biết có những thời điểm chưa chắc chắn với đáp án nên đã không bấm chuông.
Dù vậy, với tổng điểm 240, Anh Đức đã giành chiến thắng chung cuộc, trở thành chủ nhân vòng nguyệt quế Đường lên đỉnh Olympia năm thứ 26.
Anh Đức vô địch Olympia 2026 (Ảnh: Minh Phong).
Bên cạnh bản lĩnh và khả năng xử lý câu hỏi tại sân chơi Đường lên đỉnh Olympia, Đoàn Lê Anh Đức cũng chia sẻ bí quyết xây dựng nền tảng kiến thức mà em đã duy trì trong nhiều năm học tập.
Theo Anh Đức, ngay từ nhỏ, em đã hình thành thói quen đọc và chủ động tìm hiểu những kiến thức mới trên Wikipedia (dự án bách khoa toàn thư mở). Đây là một trong những cách giúp nam sinh tiếp cận nhiều lĩnh vực khác nhau, mở rộng hiểu biết và tích lũy tri thức một cách thường xuyên.
Bên cạnh việc đọc, Anh Đức dành thời gian tham gia ôn luyện, chuẩn bị cho các cuộc thi kiến thức ở nhiều cấp độ. Qua mỗi sân chơi, em có thêm cơ hội củng cố kiến thức, làm quen với nhiều dạng câu hỏi và tích lũy kinh nghiệm thi đấu.
Nam sinh cho biết, quãng thời gian ôn thi vào trường chuyên cũng là một dấu mốc quan trọng, giúp em củng cố kiến thức ở nhiều môn học. Quá trình học tập và chuẩn bị này góp phần xây dựng nền tảng để em tự tin hơn khi bước vào các cuộc thi đòi hỏi vốn hiểu biết rộng như Đường lên đỉnh Olympia.
Các bạn cùng trường đến cổ vũ cho Đoàn Lê Anh Đức tại trường quay của VTV (Ảnh: VTV).
Ngoài ra, sau khi giành chiến thắng ở cấp trường để đại diện dự thi Đường lên đỉnh Olympia 2026, Đoàn Lê Anh Đức cho biết đã có khoảng thời gian chuẩn bị kỹ lưỡng để chinh phục vòng nguyệt quế năm nay.
Các nhà leo núi nói gì sau trận chung kết?
Bên cạnh niềm vui của nhà vô địch, ba thí sinh còn lại cũng có những chia sẻ về trải nghiệm đáng nhớ tại trận chung kết năm. Nguyễn Huy Quang Minh, học sinh Trường THPT Chuyên Thái Bình, Hưng Yên về nhì với 180 điểm.
Nguyễn Huy Quang Minh cho biết em hài lòng với kết quả đạt được sau hành trình tham gia Đường lên đỉnh Olympia. Nam sinh gửi lời cảm ơn đến những người thân, thầy cô và khán giả tại quê nhà đã dành tình cảm, sự cổ vũ cho mình.
Sau cuộc thi, Quang Minh dự định dành thời gian nghỉ ngơi, ở bên gia đình sau quãng thời gian dài tập trung cho việc ôn luyện và thi đấu.
Các thí sinh tại trận chung kết Đường lên đỉnh Olympia năm thứ 2026 (Ảnh: VTV).
Hai thí sinh Trần Võ Gia Bảo, Trường THPT Chuyên Lê Quý Đôn - Đông Hải (Khánh Hòa) và Lý Thái Dương, Trường THPT Chuyên Hùng Vương (Phú Thọ) cùng đạt giải Ba.
Trần Võ Gia Bảo bày tỏ niềm tự hào khi nhận được sự cổ vũ nhiệt tình từ người dân Khánh Hòa tại điểm cầu quê nhà. Nam sinh hy vọng những thế hệ học sinh tiếp theo sẽ tiếp tục nỗ lực, mang thêm nhiều cầu truyền hình chung kết Đường lên đỉnh Olympia về với Khánh Hòa. Nhìn lại phần thi của mình, Gia Bảo cho biết em có chút tiếc nuối ở phần Tăng tốc.
Thí sinh Trần Võ Gia Bảo (Ảnh: VTV).
Thí sinh Nguyễn Huy Quang Minh (Ảnh: VTV).
Với Lý Thái Dương, cảm xúc sau trận chung kết là sự tiếc nuối khi chưa thể mang vòng nguyệt quế về với Đất Tổ Phú Thọ.
Nam sinh chia sẻ có những khoảnh khắc có thể làm tốt hơn nhưng chưa tận dụng được cơ hội. Đặc biệt, ở phần thi Tăng tốc, câu hỏi thứ ba khiến em khá rối và không thể đưa ra câu trả lời như mong muốn.
Thái Dương gửi lời xin lỗi đến những người đã cổ vũ, tiếp sức cho mình vì chưa thể giành chiến thắng chung cuộc. Tuy nhiên, em cũng bày tỏ sự xúc động, trân trọng trước tình cảm mà thầy cô, bạn bè và người dân quê nhà dành cho mình.
Nam sinh hy vọng những thế hệ học sinh tiếp theo của tỉnh nhà sẽ tiếp tục nỗ lực, đạt thành tích tốt hơn và mang vòng nguyệt quế chung kết Đường lên đỉnh Olympia về với Phú Thọ.
Kết quả chung cuộc đường lên đỉnh Olympia năm thứ 26:
Đoàn Lê Anh Đức giành vòng nguyệt quế với 240 điểm, giúp Trường THPT chuyên Hà Nội - Amsterdam lần thứ hai liên tiếp có học sinh đăng quang.
Vị trí á quân thuộc về Nguyễn Huy Quang Minh với 180 điểm. Hai thí sinh Trần Võ Gia Bảo và Lý Thái Dương cùng giành giải Ba, lần lượt đạt 165 và 105 điểm.
Anh Đức vô địch Đường lên đỉnh Olympia 2026
Đoàn Lê Anh Đức, học sinh chuyên Hà Nội – Amsterdam chiến thắng thuyết phục tại Chung kết Đường lên đỉnh Olympia 2026. Năm thứ 2 liên tiếp học sinh Hà Nội – Amsterdam giành được vòng nguyệt quế.

Đề cập việc tổ chức các kỳ thi, Bộ trưởng Hoàng Minh Sơn cho biết Bộ Giáo dục đã đánh giá, rà soát và tới đây sẽ có biện pháp vừa nâng cao chất lượng thi cử, vừa kiểm soát những gian lận, tiêu cực.

"Điều quan trọng tạo nên chiến thắng của em, trước hết là sự ủng hộ và giúp đỡ của mọi người và nỗ lực của bản thân suốt những năm qua đã được đền đáp. Về chuyên môn, trước trận chung kết, em thấy mình là thí sinh duy nhất học chuyên sử, thì đấy là thế mạnh rất riêng mình cần tận dụng", Đức nói tiếp.
Nam sinh Trường THPT chuyên Hà Nội - Amsterdam cũng nhắc đến 3 khoảnh khắc tiếc nuối trong trận chung kết: "Một là trong phần thi vượt chướng ngại vật, khi có hàng ngang Bác Hồ, em thấy chữ học nhưng em lại nghĩ là đi học, khi Trần Võ Gia Bảo bấm chuông thì em thấy bạn có suy luận tuyệt vời. Hai là ở câu toán đầu tiên trong về đích, không quá khó nhưng em hơi ẩu nên tính thiếu trường hợp, Lý Thái Dương đã giành điểm câu đó. Ba là tình huống câu hỏi tiếng Anh, em đã nghe đến một chi tiết, vì không chắc nên em không bấm chuông".
Ông Nguyễn Thanh Lâm, Ủy viên T.Ư Đảng, Tổng giám đốc Đài Truyền hình Việt Nam(bìa phải)và ông Trần Bá Dương, Chủ tịch Hội đồng quản trị Công ty cổ phần Tập đoàn Trường Hải (THACO), trao giải thưởng cho các thí sinh
Đức cho biết: "Em đang muốn bình tâm một chút sau cả hành trình chinh phụcvòng nguyệt quế Đường lên đỉnh Olympia 2026. Khi MC công bố nhà vô địch, trong suy nghĩ đầu tiên, có một điều em rất vui là Trường THPT chuyên Hà Nội - Amsterdam là trường đầu tiên bảo vệ được chức vô địchĐường lên đỉnh Olympia" (Trần Bùi Bảo Khánh, Trường THPT chuyên Hà Nội - Amsterdam vô địchĐường lên đỉnh Olympia 2025-PV).
6 năm giữ lời hẹn với giấc mơĐường lên đỉnh Olympia
Đức kểĐường lên đỉnh Olympialuôn hiện diện trong ký ức tuổi thơ của cậu bạn. "Em và bà ngoại đều yêu thích chương trình. Từ nhỏ, em đã mê các gameshow trí tuệ, đặc biệtAi là triệu phú. Khi học lớp 6, sau khi xem trận chung kếtĐường lên đỉnh Olympia 2020, em bắt đầu ấp ủ ước mơ một ngày được đứng trên sân khấu ấy", Đức chia sẻ.
Đó không phải một mong muốn thoáng qua. Đức cho hay đã dành nhiều năm theo dõi các cuộc thi, xem lại những trận đấu cũ, tìm hiểu dạng câu hỏi, tham gia các sân chơi mô phỏngĐường lên đỉnh Olympiavà rèn luyện phản xạ. "Em đã chuẩn bị choĐường lên đỉnh Olympiasuốt 6 năm", Đức nói.
6 năm ấy cũng là khoảng thời gian Đức tích lũy kiến thức từ nhiều lĩnh vực, tham gia các kỳ thi học sinh giỏi và duy trì việc học trên lớp. Với sở trường môn sử và các môn khoa học xã hội, Đức có lợi thế riêng nhưng không vì thế mà chỉ tập trung vào một nhóm kiến thức.
"Em thường tự đặt câu hỏi để kiểm tra mức độ hiểu bài, lưu lại những thông tin thú vị trong quá trình đọc và tìm hiểu. Những điều tưởng như không liên quan đến chương trình học đôi khi lại trở thành chất liệu cho các câu hỏi củaĐường lên đỉnh Olympia", Đức kể.
Đoàn Lê Anh Đức và bạn bè sau chiến thắng trong trận chung kết
Hành trình thi đấu của Đức có một dấu ấn dễ nhận ra, đó là sự tự tin và cách trả lời dứt khoát. Ở những lần giành quyền trả lời, Đức thường bắt đầu bằng câu nói: "Câu trả lời của em là…"; sau đó, đáp án được đưa ra một cách chậm rãi, rõ ràng. Không ít lần, Đức khẳng định với MC rằng mình "chắc chắn 100%" về câu trả lời. Câu nói ấy đã trở thành một nét riêng của "nhà leo núi" Hà Nội.
Ở cuộc thi tuần, Đức giành 230 điểm, về nhì nhưng có số điểm đủ để bước tiếp vào cuộc thi tháng. Tại cuộc thi tháng, Đức bứt phá với 330 điểm. Đến cuộc thi quý 4, nam sinh tiếp tục giành vòng nguyệt quế với 220 điểm, trở thành gương mặt cuối cùng ghi tên vào trận chung kết năm.
Sáng 1.11, tại trường quay S14 của Đài Truyền hình Việt Nam, giấc mơ được nuôi dưỡng suốt 6 năm chính thức bước vào thử thách cuối cùng. Đức giành 80 điểm phần thi khởi động, 10 điểm phần thi vượt chướng ngại vật, 100 điểm phần thi tăng tốc rồi về đích với 240 điểm, chiến thắngĐường lên đỉnh Olympia2026.
Từ cậu học trò cùng bà ngoại ngồi trước màn hình xemĐường lên đỉnh Olympia, Đức bước lên sân khấu, chạm tay vào vòng nguyệt quế mà mình từng mơ ước. Từ những trang sổ chép lời quốc ca bằng nhiều ngôn ngữ, những bài học lịch sử và 6 năm bền bỉ chuẩn bị, nam sinh Hà Nội đã có một cái kết trọn vẹn cho hành trình tuổi học trò.
Cũng cần kể thêm, cậu bạn có nhiều tài lẻ. Đáng chú ý trong đó là khả năng hát quốc ca của 136 quốc gia. Tại các cuộc thiĐường lên đỉnh Olympia 2026, khả năng đặc biệt ấy từng khiến khán giả bất ngờ. Đức có thể hát những đoạn quốc ca của Cuba, Angola, Sri Lanka, Maldives... Đức cũng dành tình cảm đặc biệt cho nhạc cách mạng Việt Nam, thơ ca cách mạng và dân ca. Đức cho biết yêu thích những giai điệu mang âm hưởng truyền thống, có thể hát nhạc đỏ, dân ca, ví giặm Nghệ Tĩnh bằng nhiều thứ tiếng.
Về học tập, Đức từng giành nhiều giải thưởng các cuộc thi học sinh giỏi môn sử. Sau khi hoàn thành THCS, nam sinh này đã đậu 4 trường chuyên, gồm: THPT chuyên Hà Nội - Amsterdam, THPT chuyên Nguyễn Huệ, THPT chuyên Khoa học xã hội và nhân văn (ĐH Quốc gia Hà Nội) và THPT chuyên Ngoại ngữ (ĐH Quốc gia Hà Nội).
Chia sẻ sau chiến thắng của Anh Đức, ông Đoàn Quốc Hùng (67 tuổi, ở P.Nam Định, tỉnh Ninh Bình) cho biết việc cháu nội giành vòng nguyệt quế là điều tuyệt vời dành cho bản thân cháu cũng như cả gia đình. Kể về khoảnh khắc trực tiếp "đội nắng" trên khán đài để cổ vũ cháu, ô

Ryanair considers pay freezes and reducing crew on flights as fuel costs soar | Ryanair | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation
Ryanair anticipates its jet fuel costs will increase by about €2bn (£1.6bn) in its next financial year, which ends in March 2028.Photograph: Pier Marco Tacca/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenRyanair anticipates its jet fuel costs will increase by about €2bn (£1.6bn) in its next financial year, which ends in March 2028.Photograph: Pier Marco Tacca/Getty Images
Ryanair considers pay freezes and reducing crew on flights as fuel costs soar
Airline also weighs up increasing use of AI as part of cost-cutting measures to offset impact of Iran war
Ryanair is considering cost-cutting measures including implementing pay freezes, reducing crew on flights and increasing the use of AI to offset soaring fuel costs because of theMiddle East conflict.
Europe’s biggest low-cost carrier said it expects European airlines to raise their ticket prices byas much as 20%, as it anticipates its jet fuel costs will increase by about €2bn (£1.6bn) in its next financial year, which ends in March 2028.
“Unless there is a swift resolution of the Middle East conflict we expect jet fuel prices to remain elevated well into 2027,” said Michael O’Leary, the chief executive ofRyanair. “While we believe European short-haul fares will increase materially to reflect these much higher jet-fuel prices and competitor capacity reductions, this is unlikely to provide a full offset for an estimated €2bn increase in our fuel bill.”
The oil price hit a six-month high last Friday but fell on Monday to about $110 a barrel.
Ryanair said it expects European short-haul fares will “increase materially” next year as a result, as the oil hedging deals taken out by airlines to reduce costs come to an end.
“To help address this, we’re reviewing all costs across group airlines with a particular focus on airport churn negotiations, maturing labour agreements (which may require temporary pay freezes), lower crew ratios and increased use of AI,” O’Leary said.
The company said the AI drive would be focused on “further operational and back office/support functions” productivity.
Ryanair said its fuel requirements through to the end of March remain 80% hedged at $67 a barrel.
The company’s hedges for the following 12 months are 25% hedged at $95 a barrel.
The Irish airline, Europe’s largest in terms of passenger numbers, said that average fares fell by 2% year on year in the quarter to the end of September. Ryanair added that fare prices in the final three months of the year were trending “modestly ahead” of the same quarter last year.
“The booking window remains closer-in which reduces visibility,” the company said.“[The current quarter’s] fare outcome will heavily depend on the strength of close-in October-November school midterm [holiday] and Christmas bookings.”
The airline reported a post-tax profit of €1.61bn in the quarter to the end of September, a fall of 6% year on year but in line with analyst expectations. Passenger numbers grew 5% year on year to 64.5 million for the quarter.
