Prop 45 in California could be hiding a loophole for data centers
Proposition 45 makes it easier for developers to speed through environmental reviews.
Image: Cath Virginia / The Verge, Getty ImagesPart OfAll the latest updates on AI data centerssee all updatesJustine Calma
is a senior science reporter covering energy and the environment with more than a decade of experience. She is also the host ofHell or High Water: When Disaster Hits Home, a podcast from Vox Media and Audible Originals.
A high-stakes California ballot measure pitched as a fast track for “essential” infrastructure could wind up giving data center developers a loophole to evade public scrutiny, environmental advocates warn.
Proposition 45 would shorten timelines for state-mandated environmental assessments for eligible projects and make it more difficult for residents to challenge those projects in court. Proponents say passing the measure would help alleviate the state’shousing shortageand meet rising electricity demand with new renewable energy projects. Environmental groups and some legal experts, however, warn that data center developers backing the proposition could escape scrutiny if Prop 45 becomes law.
“The concern here is that data center developers will find a way to shoehorn their projects into the definition of an essential project and then get to take advantage of … the fast-track review that it’ll create,” says Fernando Gaytan, a senior attorney at the nonprofit environmental law organization Earthjustice, which opposes Prop 45. “Communities get cut out of the conversation.”
“Communities get cut out of the conversation.”
Prop 45 would loosen standards for certain projects subject to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). CEQA requires state agencies to perform environmental reviews and work with project developers to find ways to limit any harmful impacts to the environment and public health. Crucially, CEQA also mandates that state agencies gather community input and consider public comment before issuing any approvals.
Specifically, Prop 45 would create a365-day deadlinefor agencies to complete the environmental impact report for a project. It also stipulates that any legal challenges would need to be settled within 270 days. It would only allow for 45 days of public comment, and it would only require state agencies and developers to consult with Native American tribes that have been federally recognized. CEQA as it’s currently written sets a minimum rather than a maximum number of days for public review, and mandates consultation with tribes that might be impacted by a project even if they’re not formally recognized by the federal government as having “government-to-government” relations with the US.
During the CEQA review process, state agencies develop alternatives that developers can take to mitigate environmental and health risks. Prop 45 would turn that on its head, making developers responsible for coming up with a single alternative project plan for regulators to consider. The proposition would also strip away an agency’s authority to repeatedly ask a developer for more information about a proposed project; state regulators would need to specify all the information a company is required to provide at the start of the application process.
On top of all that, Prop 45 would bar courts from halting a project altogether even if it finds that the regulatory agency failed to correctly comply with CEQA. The judge would only have the ability to pause specific parts of a project that are problematic, rather than forcing a full stop to construction. That’s the piece that’s most egregious for Gaytan. “It’s hard to undo harms once you’ve already started a project,” he says.
Data centers are ahot-buttonelectionissuefor midterms across the US and have become a point of contention for Prop 45 as well. The proposition lists nine types of “essential” projects that would be eligible for streamlined review, including housing, clean energy, and “broadband Internet access.”
Gaytan and someother legal experts contendthat the latter designation — broadband internet access — could include data centers. Thelanguageincludes any project that would “provide mass-market retail service by wire service, wireless service, or radio to customers in this state that provides the capability to transmit data to, and receive data from, all or substantially all internet endpoints, including, but not limited to, any capabilities that are incidental to and enable the operation of the communications service.”
Data center backlash is uniting America
Proposed data centers that include any broadband transmission infrastructure might be able to squeeze into that definition, UC Davis School of Law professor emeritus Richard Frank and attorney Matthew McKerley write in a recentcolumnin theDaily Journal.They also point out that companies currently developing data centers have poured hundreds of thousands of dollars into a campaign to support Prop 45. And while Prop 45 excludes certain types of projects, like nuclear energy and dial-up internet access service, it doesn’t explicitly bar data centers.
Proponents, meanwhile, argue that Prop 45 would not apply to data centers. “The fact that data centers may play a role in supporting the Internet does not make them ‘essential broadband Internet access projects’ under Prop 45,” attorney and lobbyist Kurt OnetowritesinThe National Law Review. The Yes on Prop 45 campaign didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.
Prop 45 has managed to garnersupportfrom the California and Hawaii chapter of the NAACP, which has been among one of the most vocal civil rights organizations tooppose data center developments across the US. evidence_pages.https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n:
Guardian Essential poll: record number of Australians are turning their backs on the Melbourne Cup | Melbourne Cup | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation
More than two-thirds of Australian polled now say they have low or zero interest in the annual Melbourne Cup horse race.Photograph: Robert Cianflone/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMore than two-thirds of Australian polled now say they have low or zero interest in the annual Melbourne Cup horse race.Photograph: Robert Cianflone/Getty Images
Guardian Essential poll: record number of Australians are turning their backs on the Melbourne Cup
Growing disdain for gambling and animal cruelty concerns drive sliding interest in race that once ‘stopped the nation’
Get ourbreaking news email,free appordaily news podcast
A record number of Australians are turning their backs on theMelbourne Cup, with more than two-thirds surveyed saying they have low or zero interest in the annual horse race.
Support for the Melbourne Cup has been sliding consistently for a number of years, butthe Guardian Essential pollfound just 9% of Australians said they had high interest in the race now – nearly half the proportion in 2025.
“The race that once stopped the nation is now just white noise for many,” Peter Lewis, chair of Essential Media, said.
The Guardian Essential poll of 1,003 Australians in late October highlights thelatest erosionin popularity of the eventamid growing ambivalence to the event.
Guardian Essential poll: One Nation and Labor’s primary vote on par as discontent with Albanese risesRead more
Just 9% of people said they had high interest in the Cup, down 7 percentage points from 2025, with another 23% professing moderate interest, also down 3 points. About 29% of voters said they had low interest (up 5 points from last year), while another 39% said no interest at all (up 8 points).
The combined high and moderate interest came to only 32%, the lowest on record since Essential began asking this question in annual polling in November 2022. The combined low and no interest vote was 68%, jumping 12 points from last year to its highest on record.
Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email
In November 2022, the low and no interest vote came to a combined 52%; it was 62% in 2023, 52% in 2024, and 56% in 2025.
The“nup to the Cup” movement, backed by some high-profile politicians and celebrities, has contributed to declining support for the race.
But 62% of Australians nonetheless agreed the Melbourne Cup was a unique part of Australia’s national identity. That number remains a strong majority view, despite falling from 78% agreement when Essential asked this question in 2019.
Half of Australians (50%) believe the Cup promotes unhealthy gambling behaviour, up 3% since 2025, while 36% say they feel the Cup normalises animal cruelty, down 3 points from 2025.
Another 48% said they were less interested in the Cup than they used to be.
“The key driver appears to be a growing disdain for gambling, although concern for animal cruelty comes a close second,” Lewis said.
“More broadly this reflects the decline in unifying atonal moments in a world where more and more people have their experiences mediated by targeted advertising algorithms.”
Just 12% of voters in October’s poll said they regularly wagered on horse races and would bet on Tuesday’s Melbourne Cup, down 5 points from 2025. In contrast, 46% of people said they were not interested in the Cup and would not place a bet, up 6 points from last year.
Another 25% said they rarely bet on horses but would watch the race and place a bet, while 17% said they would watch but not bet.

More European supermarkets are getting their freezers hacked
Stores in Belgium, Sweden, Luxembourg, and Estonia have had their cooling systems tampered with.﻿
Employees at an ICA Kvantum supermarket in Sjoebo, Sweden, unload spoiled food from the freezer units.Image: Johan Nilsson / TT News Agency / AFP via Getty ImagesJess Weatherbed
is a news writer focused on creative industries, computing, and internet culture. Jess started her career at TechRadar, covering news and hardware reviews.
Grocery stores across Europe have been hit by another wave of suspected cyberattacks, reporting sudden changes in the temperatures of their fridges and freezers. Major supermarket chains across Belgium, Sweden, Luxembourg, and Estonia were affected according to local reports shared byBloombergandReuters.
One Ica Kvantum store in Sweden said on itsFacebook pagethat its fridges and freezers had been hacked overnight, with temperatures remotely raised to 50 degrees Celsius (122 Fahrenheit). In a statement toBusiness Insider, a spokesperson at Swedish supermarket chain Coop also confirmed that “unauthorized actors were able to access and tamper with the cooling systems at a small fraction of our stores.” Dutch retailer Ahold Delhaize said an “IT incident” was responsible for adjusting the temperature of refrigeration units in dozens of its ⁠supermarkets in ​Belgium ‌and ‌Luxembourg. The full scale of the incident has yet to be confirmed.
Many modern supermarket fridges and freezers are connected to the internet to support remote maintenance and system failure alerts, but the increasing number of these suspected hacks is raising concerns around how security flaws can impact food supply chains. This latest incident follows an apparent cyberattack that targetedhundreds of French supermarket refrigeratorslast month, with the resulting food spoilage estimated to be worth millions of Euros, along with astring of US military base freezer malfunctionsalso suspected to be the result of a cyberattack.

Brisbane 2032: the sports being forced to modernise in bid to stay in Olympic race | Brisbane Olympic Games 2032 | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation
Race walker Isaac Beacroft (left) is one of many Australian Olympic medal hopes, so long as his sport is included in the final program.Photograph: Jane Barlow/PAView image in fullscreenRace walker Isaac Beacroft (left) is one of many Australian Olympic medal hopes, so long as his sport is included in the final program.Photograph: Jane Barlow/PA
Brisbane 2032: the sports being forced to modernise in bid to stay in Olympic race
Microchips, ninja obstacle courses and other ‘modern’ tweaks are being made by sports vying for a coveted spot on the Olympic program in Australia
Australia’s teenage race walker Isaac Beacroft won gold at the Commonwealth Games this year, propelling him into contention for a medal at the home Brisbane Olympics in six years’ time. There is just one problem.
The International Olympic Committee is considering culling events like his – as well as surfing, skateboarding and climbing, in which Australia also has strong podium chances – in secretive deliberations under way in Switzerland that are set to transform the Olympic program.
Warning over future of Olympic Games if Brisbane 2032 program is not modernisedRead more
Officials within sports are not watching idly while their fates are determined in Lausanne, however. Modern pentathlon has ditched its horse riding component for a ninja obstacle course. Canoe sprint is moving away from longer distances to focus on the more dramatic, explosive 500m events.
Some in race walking, like Beacroft, have their own plan: a microchip in competitors’ shoes. The 19-year-old, who won gold in Glasgow thanks toa final-lap surge, says the chip – alongside shifting the event distance from 20,000 metres to the more broadly relatable half marathon – is “the race walkers’ play to keep it in the Olympics”.
The chip “detects the flight time” of walkers, Beacroft explains, thereby eliminating the subjectivity from judging. “That’s going to go a long way in creating some sort of reliability and respect towards the sport.”
The tiny contraption could be the difference between an Olympic future and a slide away from the sporting spotlight. A planned reduction in the number of sports for Brisbane, a decreased cap of 10,500 athletes, and aneed for the Olympics to moderniseleaves emerging sports competing with traditional pursuits such as fencing and wrestling. The IOC is also assessing each “discipline” – seeing, for example, track and road cycling as separate – based on its television audience, cost and complexity of facilities, and size of athlete cohort.
Chart to show the number of athletes at recent Olympic Games.
The traditional heavyweights are swimming, gymnastics and athletics, the latter with 1,810 competitors at LA 2028 or close to one-fifth of the entire athlete body. Each will retain their place, though some events or disciplines such as race walking may be vulnerable. Meanwhile, sports with bespoke venues like triathlon, or large athlete quotas like rowing and hockey, will be looked at closely in a process dubbed as “fit for future” by the IOC.
As IOC officials enter their final months of decision-making, several of Australia’s potential podium contenders for 2032 including Beacroft, skateboarders Arisa Trew and Chloe Covell, climber Oceana Mackenzie (currently ranked second in the world in bouldering) and surfers like world No 1 Molly Picklum are in jeopardy of missing out if the IOC leaves their disciplines out of the core program.
View image in fullscreenArisa Trew won skateboard gold for Australia at the Paris Olympics.Photograph: Frank Franklin II/AP
Their participation would then require the Brisbane organising committee to include these sports as one of the hosts’ additional picks, limited to four, akin to how breaking was included in Paris. Competition for those places is set to be fierce as Australian favourites like netball, surf lifesaving and touch football join the frenzy of aspirants vying for an Olympic berth.
Chart to show individual sports’ revenue from the IOC for Tokyo 2020
There is another consideration, however, that has officials sweating. The cost of holding the additional sports must be borne by the local organising committee alone, rather than co-funded by the IOC. Organisers therefore face budget overruns if the IOC shunts preferred sports with large numbers of athletes or complex venues from the core program.
This dynamic partly explains the stance by the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, expressed at the Future Brisbane conference last weekend, that Brisbane 2032 officials and the Queensland government should consider using existing facilities in Sydney and Melbourne for sports beyond football, which already has interstate pool games planned.
“One of the things I’ve said is that it’s Queensland’s games, it’s their decision,” he said. “They could consider, just as the Paris Games had surfing in Tahiti, and all of the Games aren’t always just in the city where they’re held, if you want to save money and save time, then you could give consideration to that.”
View image in fullscreenSydney Olympic Park could host some bonus Brisbane 2032 events if the final program requires more facilities.Photograph: David Gray/Getty Images
Co-funded by the state and federal governments, $7.1bn has been committed to Games venue infrastructure, but a detailed budget will not be possible until the IOC decides the final program. That had been expected in 2026, but now all that will be known by the new year is the list of core disciplines, as well some fringe proposals no longer in the running.
Instead, a final decision on the program will not arrive until the IOC session in April next year – a farcical situation around which the Brisbane 2032 president, Andrew Liveris, has already expressed frustration. “I think we’re all very anxious to get that finalised, and for good reasons,” he said at the launch ofthe Games logotwo weeks ago.
Beacroft is confident race walking will make the cut, but says it is not easy for athletes currently in limbo. “You don’t want to be in denial about it or anything like that … I kind of keep my fingers crossed that it’s going to be in Brisbane, because that’s a massive goal of mine and a big, big motivator for my career.”

Hyrox partners with World Triathlon in bid to become Olympic sport - BBC Sport
Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,
Hyrox holds more than 100 events worldwide each year
Hyrox has moved closer to fulfilling its ambition of gaining inclusion into the Olympic and Paralympic Games after entering into a partnership with World Triathlon.
The agreement will see 'hybrid racing' become a recognised discipline within World Triathlon, the sport's global governing body.
Hyrox, the fitness craze which combines running with exercise stations, will be contested across three formats - ultimate, fast and ultra - each sanctioned and governed by World Triathlon.
World Triathlon and Hyrox said in a statement that obtaining Olympic and Paralympic status for the discipline was the "ultimate ambition".
World Triathlon president Antonio Arimany said hybrid racing was "a natural evolution for our movement".
He added: "This partnership will not only accelerate the growth of World Triathlon on the global stage, it will open genuine new opportunities for every one of our national federations to grow participation, engage new audiences, and strengthen our sport at every level.
"This is exactly the kind of forward-looking collaboration our members deserve."
Hyrox co-founder Christian Toetzke said: "From the very beginning, our goal was to build a global sport that could earn a place on the world's biggest athletic stage.
"Partnering with World Triathlon is a monumental step toward that vision.
"Hybrid racing is no longer just a global fitness movement, it is officially on the road to the Olympics."
Great Britain's Olympic triathlon champion Alex Yee reacted to the news by sharing a poll with his 227,000 followers, who had voted 82% against being in favour of the move after a couple of hours.
Fellow British triathlete Max Stapley commented on the joint announcement on Instagram: "This is crap."
Olympic triathlete Roksana Slupek, of Poland, wrote "the two sports have absolutely nothing in common" and questioned what her sport would gain from the partnership.
How Hyrox became the latest sporting craze
Hyrox apologises for allowing race to continue after athlete soils herself
Hyrox was founded in 2017, primarily as an indoor discipline in which athletes take part in eight legs consisting of a one-kilometre run followed by a fitness exercise.
The exercises include 1km on a standing ski machine, 50m sled push, 50m sled pull, 80m burpee jumps, 1km row, 200m kettlebell carry, 100m lunges carrying a sandbag, and 100 throws and catches of a medicine ball against a wall.
World championships are held each year, with athletes contesting both singles and doubles races.
Under the agreement with World Triathlon, Hyrox will continue to oversee world, continental and national championships for elite athletes in the 'ultimate' format, which mirrors its existing format.
The additional formats included under the new discipline of hybrid racing - 'fast' and 'ultra' - offer high intensity and extended adaptations.
Only sports governed by recognised international federations which comply with the Olympic Charter, the World Anti-Doping Code and the Olympic Movement Code on the Prevention of the Manipulation of Competition - as is the case for triathlon - are eligible for inclusion at the Olympic and Paralympic Games.

A Paralympian vs a former TV news anchor - and other US Senate races to watch - BBC News
Opponents in Iowa - Democrat Josh Turek and Republican Ashley Hinson
Millions of Americans are about to decide the future of the Republican-controlled Congress in a midterm election that will have a significant impact on President Donald Trump's final two years in office.
All eyes are on a handful of Senate races that will decide control of the prized upper chamber.
A four-seat gain by Democrats would give them control - and with it the power to limit Trump's ambitions, reject his judicial nominations and investigate his administration.
Billions of dollars are being poured into the 35 races across the country, but only a handful could go either way.
There are seven Senate races deemed to be a toss-up byindependent elections analyst Cook Political Report,external.
Here, we profile the personalities making waves in these much-watched contests.
This race has been marred by controversy over the appearance of a second candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot. The Republican senator of that name faces stiff competition from Mary Peltola and accuses her of introducing his namesake to confuse voters, which she denies.
Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,
Dan Sullivan is aiming for his third term against Alaska Native Mary Peltola
The race may ultimately be the tipping point state that decides which party controls the chamber if, as expected, Alaska is one of the slower states to reach an outcome.
Peltola, a former House member and the first Alaska Native to be elected to Congress, has run on a platform of "fish, family, freedom" and has attacked Sullivan's record as Alaska's natural resources commissioner.
Two-term senator Sullivan, a long-time Marine Corps reservist who also served as Alaska's attorney general, has accused Peltola's campaign of links to an effort to confuse Republican voters which led to a second man named Dan Sullivan entering the race.
The Peltola campaign denies any such link, though the issue is the subject of a state investigation and a justice department lawsuit, which on Sunday was rejected by a judge.
Alaska's ranked-choice system also adds uncertainty to the mix, and the state has historically been difficult to poll, with surveys historically underestimating Republican voters.
Sullivan, 61, only retired from the US Marines as recently as 2024, after a 30-year career that included deployments in to Afghanistan and the Middle East. Peltola, 53, grew up fishing salmon with her father, later becoming the first person born in the state to actually represent it in Congress.
One of the few Republicans who voted to convict Trump when he was impeached in 2021, longtime senator Susan Collins has outperformed her party in this Democratic-leaning state, partly by presenting herself as a rebel. Her opponent Troy Jackson, who draws on his background as a lumberjack to persuade blue-collar Mainers he can relate to them, hopes that time is finally running out for one of the great survivors of US politics.
Susan Collins, the incumbent, takes on logger Troy Jackson in Maine
Collins is hoping her reputation as a centrist will persuade independent-minded voters in a state that reliably votes Democratic in presidential elections.
Now her campaign will test whether Republicans can win by distancing themselves from Trump.
Collins, who is seeking her sixth term, entered the midterm cycle as one of the most vulnerable incumbent Republicans seeking re-election.
But she has been helped by controversy on the other side of the aisle involving Graham Platner, who was ultimately replaced as the Democratic nominee by Jackson, a former president of the Maine state senate.
Both Jackson and Collins oppose Trump's tariffs on Canada, mindful of the impact they are having on this border state. Unlike Collins, though, he favours the abolition of the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency (ICE).
Collins, 73, began her political career fresh from college in the 1970s and she entered the US Senate in 1997. Jackson, 58, is a logger who became politically active when he helped to lead a protest to block lower-paid workers from Canada entering Maine.
James Talarico aims to end a decades-long electoral drought for the Democrats in Texas - and show that one of the Republicans' main strongholds could be in play for the 2028 presidential election. His match-up with Ken Paxton has become the most expensive Senate race ever.
Trump ally Ken Paxton (L) faces a challenge from former teacher James Talarico (R) in the Texas contest
Republican Paxton knows his party has been winning statewide races in Texas for more than 30 years.
Texas State Representative James Talarico, a former schoolteacher and Presbyterian seminary student, is the latest Democrat hoping to break his party's long losing streak.
Texas Republicans are facing a daunting combination of headwinds. It is a challenging national political environment for conservatives and there are several state issues like data centre construction and aggressive immigration enforcement that have cut against their party. Added to that is a controversial candidate, Paxton.
The campaign has been acrimonious, with Talarico targeting Paxton's 2023 impeachment by the Republican-controlled state House of Representatives for alleged corruption, bribery and abuse of power. Paxton denied the charges and was later acquitted by the state Senate, calling the impeachment a "politically motivated sham from the beginning".
Supported by more than $170m in funds from tech mogul Elon Musk, Paxton has attempted to paint Talarico as a liberal who is out of touch with Texans on issues like transgender rights, law enforcement, immigration and energy policy.
A Democratic victory here might indicate America's second-biggest electoral prize in a presidential election could be within their reach in 2028 - a notion that could dramatically reshape the nation's political landscape.
Before he entered public service, Paxton spent 14 years launching and building his own law firm. He served in the state House and Senate before becoming the chief legal officer in Texas.

Australia Test captain Pat Cummins to miss upcoming England matches

Test captain Pat Cummins and fellow quicks Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood will be rested during Australia’s upcoming one-day and T20 series against England.
Australia will play three ODIs and five T20 internationals, but Cummins, Starc and Hazlewood were not named in either squad on Monday as the pace trio refresh for a gruelling 10 Tests in 14 weeks this summer.
Australia’s bizarre selection choices backfired – predictably – in South Africa. It’s time for a reality check | Geoff LemonRead more
Key batsmen Travis Head, Matthew Renshaw, Josh Inglis, Cooper Connolly and all-rounder Cameron Green will be managed through the T20 series following long tours to Zimbabwe and South Africa, as they prepare for four Tests against New Zealand and five in India.
“We are in the middle of a highly demanding phase of our schedule,” said chair of selectors, George Bailey. “Our multi-format players are transitioning directly from the tour of South Africa into an ODI and T20 series, leaving a narrow window to ensure the squad is physically prepared and fresh for the upcoming New Zealand Test series.
“Then, from when the Test players assemble in Perth through to the conclusion of the 150th anniversary Test against England, the team will have been on the road for more than 100 days. To manage this workload, each player’s build-up to the New Zealand series will be carefully planned and focused on individual’s physical and mental preparation.”
Rising WA paceman Mahli Beardman will make his national one-day debut after playing one T20 for Australia.
View image in fullscreenWestern Australian Mahli Beardman (right) has impressed Australia’s selectors.Photograph: James Worsfold/Getty Images
“Mahli Beardman’s recent performances for Australia A were impressive and we are incredibly excited for his return to the national team across the ODI and T20 formats,” Bailey said. “We think he can continue to develop into an all-format player across the coming years.”
Jack Edwards was rewarded for an impressive recent tour of South Africa and consistent domestic cricket performance with a place in both squads. Left-arm quick Spencer Johnson and all-rounder Liam Scott return to the ODI squad. Nathan Ellis has not recovered in time for the ODI series as he returns from a side strain.
The Hobart Hurricanes’ recently crowned Australian T20 player of the year Tim David will spearhead the Twenty20 squad. Hard-hitting opening batter Jake Fraser-McGurk has also won back a place in Australia’s T20 team for the first time since 2025. And promising young NSW batter Lachlan Shaw joins the T20 squad for the first time, having impressed on the recent Australia A tour to India and in the BBL.
The ODI side continues to build towards Australia’s 2027 World Cup defence in Africa, while the T20 squad has a longer-term goal of the 2028 LA Olympics and T20 World Cup.

MarketsBusinessInvestingTechPolitics & PolicyVideoWatchlistInvesting ClubPROLivestreamMenu
Binance said it processed $4.65 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits on Nov. 1.
The net outflows amounted to 2.1% of Binance's $171 billion in total assets.
The exchange said it had covered around 95% of the impacted amount following the $6.3 billion hack.
Cfoto | Future Publishing | Getty Images
Binance said it recorded $3.64 billion in net outflows after reopening withdrawals on Sunday following a $6.3 billion hack, as customers rushed to move funds off the platform.
The exchange processed $4.65 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits between 6 a.m. and 3:30 p.m. UTC on Nov. 1, Binancesaidin a post on X.
The resulting net outflows represented 2.1% of Binance's $171 billion in total assets, based on its latest available proof-of-reserves data as of Oct. 28.
Binance said withdrawal volumes had declined and were stabilizing following an initial spike, while deposit volumes remained substantial.
The exchange began restoring withdrawals in phases at 6 a.m. UTC on Sunday, with services resuming across all 15 networks and assets included in the initial phase by 12:36 p.m. UTC. It said testing was continuing for the remaining networks and assets.
"Circle activated its incident response procedures and coordinated with law enforcement to freeze more than $1.1 billion in USDC associated with the incident," a spokesperson for the stablecoin issuer told CNBC in an email. The company said the investigation is ongoing.
The updated figure follows a Fridaypostfrom Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire, who said at the time that more than $800 million in USDC linked to the incident had been frozen.
Binance founder and former CEO Changpeng Zhao sought to reassure users following the breach,writingon X that "98% choose to stay!" He said most of the net outflows occurred within the first couple of hours after withdrawals resumed. "Trust isn't earned by what you say in good times. It's earned by what you do in hard times," Zhao added.
The withdrawals followed a record $6.3 billion hack of Binance last week. The FBIattributedthe attack to North Korean hackers, identifying the operation as TraderTraitor.
The exchange has said it wouldabsorbthe financial impact of the stolen funds rather than pass the losses on to users.
Binance said it had coveredaround 95%of the impacted amount, up from 90% in its previous update. The exchange said the remaining 5% consisted of less liquid tokens that would take longer to source in the quantities required.

Binance hack: Users withdraw $3.6bn after record crypto heist - BBC News
Image source,ReutersByOsmond ChiaBusiness reporter
Binance customers withdrew $3.6bn (£2.7bn) of assets from the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange as it reopened on Sunday following what is believed to bethe largest hack in history.
The firm suspended all transactions in the wake of the incident, which impacted $6.3bn worth of digital assets.
Major organisations, including the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), haveaccused North Korea of being responsible for the cyber-attack.
The company said it has covered around 95% of the assets stolen in the breach but the remaining amount may take longer to source. Binance has repeatedly said it would cover all of the losses linked to the attack.
Binance said on X: "Between 06:00 and 15:30 [GMT] on November 1, we processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits, resulting in a net outflow of approximately $3.64 billion."
There was an "initial spike" in withdrawals, which later declined and "are stabilising as expected", it added.
Sunday's net withdrawals account for just over 2% of the $171bn of assets under its management, said Binance.
The firm said last week that it has reserved more than $6.3bn in funds, to deal with ​the fallout of the attack.
Binance also said withdrawals of more than two dozen major cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum have resumed and that more services will resume in phases once security checks are completed.
Funds linked to the Binance hack continue to be laundered, according to Alec Zebrick, senior manager in global services at Chainalysis, which has been working with the firm and governments to get the stolen money back.
"We continue to see funds being laundered quite actively," he told the BBC's Today Programme.
"The attackers are layering these funds across many thousands of addresses, across thousands of deposits," he added.
AI discovered a massive cyber-security flaw - here's what happened
The attack on Binance has been attributed to TraderTraitor, a North Korean cybercrime group also known as the Lazarus Group, whichstole a then-record $1.5bn from crypto exchange Bybit in 2025.
The FBI on Saturday published a list of cryptocurrency wallet addresses linked to the group and urged partners in the industry to help by blocking transactions involving them.
The exchange scrambled to urge cryptocurrency issuers to freeze affected assets.
Binance said last week that early checks suggest the incident may have started with a compromised laptop that belonged to an engineer, allowing hackers to find a way to make unauthorised transactions.
The hack hit Binance's global centralised exchange, Binance.com, while its US-facing platform has said it was not affected by the issue.
Watch: What we know about Binance's $6.3bn hack and what to do if you're affected
Binance said it had replaced customers' assets using a combination of sources, including its corporate treasury as well as its futures insurance and emergency reserve funds.
"Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident," the firm said.
Cryptocurrencies are digital assets traded on exchanges such as Binance. Unlike cash, they do not exist in physical form and are managed on computers, smartphones and other digital devices.
Binance was founded in China and has hundreds of millions of registered users globally.

evidence_pages.https://www.wired.com/story/the-trump-ad:
The Trump Administration Is Wreaking Havoc on the Electoral System Before the Midterms | WIREDSkip to main content
Polls are looking prettybleak for Republicans—and the Trump administration’s various attempts tointerferewith the electionshaven’t been too successfuleither.
In recent weeks, the Department of Justice, helmed by Attorney General Todd Blanche, aproponent of conspiracy theoriesabout widespread noncitizen voting in the 2020 election, has pulled out all the stops to sow doubt in voters’ minds about the security and validity of the electoral process.
To do this, the DOJ has spent the last yeardemanding unredacted voter rolls,issuing executive ordersto wrest control of elections from states,raiding election offices, proposing new laws todisenfranchise millions of citizens, and claiming thatnoncitizenswere voting en masse across the country. (Incidents of verified noncitizen voting are vanishingly rare, as multiplebipartisaninvestigationshave shown.)
There have also been escalating threats by the DOJ against election officials. On Thursday,the DOJ sent lettersto election officials in all 50 states warning them that they would pursue criminal action if they failed to preserve election records for 22 days. Earlier that week, a federal judge had admonished the Trump administration for making similar threats around criminal prosecution against election officials in a different case.
“They're trying to create chaos and distrust in the system,” says Shelby Wayment, staff attorney at UCLA Law’s Safeguarding Democracy Project. “They're trying to file these now knowing they have virtually no chance of winning and then after they can claim the election was fraudulent.”
“This Department is following the facts and the law, not anyone’s political timetable,” a spokesperson for the DOJ tells WIRED, pointing out that the previous administration’s Justice departmentsued AlabamaandVirginiaahead of the 2024 election, claiming the DOJ was at the time trying “to stop them from removing suspected noncitizens from their voter rolls.”
Experts say that while the DOJ’s current legal efforts, including escalating fights inAlaskaandCaliforniaover candidates and voter rolls, are faltering, they’re also designed to lay the groundwork to question the results of this week’s vote.
“We have to expect absolutely, if the election doesn't go the way the president wants, that we will see the administration’s attempt to sow doubts in the election and maybe even challenge those results, but I'm also not worried about it,” David Becker, a former DOJ lawyer and the head of the Center for Election Innovation and Research, tells WIRED.
“They have failed at everything they've tried to do. Our systems have held firm. Our institutions have held firm.”
34 federal district courts have ruled against Trump since he took office in 2025 blocking access to voter rolls and preventing executive orders being implemented, according toanalysis from the Brennan Center.
Former deputy assistant attorney general at the DOJ’s Civil Rights Division Justin Levitt thinks that a lot of the actions taken by the Trump administration are about a show of force and optics more than anything else. “What you’re seeing now is a ton of marketing. They are trying to communicate that they're in charge, and I think it's not working,” says Levitt, now a law professor at Loyola Marymount University. “But it is really important to remember that the federal government isn't in charge of the election process. State and local officials are.”
WIRED has laid out the details of the DOJ’s legal efforts in California, Nevada, Washington, and Alaska below, which have all been met with disdain from local and state officials.
California is officially a hotbed of election controversy. In October, theDOJ filed a federal lawsuitseeking a court order against California to compel them to sequester mail-in ballots associated with approximately 20,000 voters, claiming that these voters were noncitizens. On Wednesday, a federal judgein a strong-worded orderrejected the request.
“Never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon their own Constitutional elections procedures and bend to the will of the Executive Branch,” US District Judge David Carter wrote in his order filed late on Wednesday.
Almost immediately, the DOJ filed an appeal and a federal court quickly denied it.
The judge pointed out that similar claims from the administration about noncitizens on voter rolls hadn’t held up to scrutiny, and he had “further questions of credibility” about how they arrived at that number in the first place.
Last week, a federal judge also ruled that the DOJ had to turn over its list of around 20,000 names to the Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights, so that the group could analyze the dataset. On Saturday, the group submitted a legal filing stating that an analysis of the list found thatover 40 percent of the namesweren’t even in the state’s current voter files. In response, the DOJhas suggestedthat the publication of their analysis violated the terms of the lists released to them, and is urging a federal judge to consider whether contempt charges might be applicable here.
“The DOJ has clearly written rules that prevent it from engaging in any investigative activity close to an election—rules that private attorney Todd Blanche cited when representing his client, Donald Trump, in September 2024,” Becker says. “But the DOJ continues to violate its own policies.”
To cap it all off, the DOJissued grand jury subpoenasto California’s local election officials last week, indicating that despite repeated court losses it has no intention of backing down.
In October, the Justice Departmentfiled a lawsuitdesigned to block certification of the election result in Alaska’s Senate race if Democrat candidate Mary Peltola wins.
The reason for the lawsuit is the presence of a spoiler candidate on the ballot with a similar name as the incumbent Republican candidate Daniel Sullivan. The DOJ’s lawsuit was filed despite the Alaska Supreme Courtruling in the summerthat Daniel J. Sullivan Jr could remain on the ballot as no laws had been broken.

Jack Grealish left out of Everton squad again for Premier League trip to Newcastle
Grealish omitted last Thursday for disciplinary reasons
Playmaker left on Merseyside to work on his fitness
Jack Grealish is poised to miss his third successive game forEvertonwhen David Moyes’s side visit Newcastle in the Premier League on Monday night.
Grealish wasdropped from Everton’s Carabao Cup winagainst Matthias Jaissle’s team last Thursday for disciplinary reasons. The 31-year-old had missed training without permission in the buildup to the fourth-round tie. He was also absent from the previous game, a Premier League defeat at Arsenal, owing to illness.
Everton have travelled to the north-east without the playmaker, who rejoined the club on a second lucrative loan deal from Manchester City this summer.

evidence_pages.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art:
No Jack Grealish, no problem - the rise of Everton's youngsters - BBC Sport
Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,
Players aged 24 or under are playing a higher proportion of minutes for Everton this season
ByMatthew Hobbs and Matt JonesBBC Sport journalists
AsEvertonprepared to faceNewcastlein the fourth round of the EFL Cup at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday, the stakes were high.
A quarter-final tie against League Two opposition in Fleetwood awaited the winner, and a fanbase starved of trophies began to look ahead - albeit, for some, through covered eyes.
Then, in the build-up to the match, it was revealedJack Grealish had been dropped from the squadover what is understood to have been an unauthorised absence from training.
The unwanted headline threatened to derail preparations for the latest round of a competition that perhaps offersEverton's best chance of winning a trophy for the first time in 31 years.
Instead, the club's younger players came to the fore, led by the influential Hayden Hackney.
A £16.5m summer signing from Middlesbrough, the 24-year-old made light of his inexperience at the highest level against a strongNewcastleXI, assisting James Garner's opening goal before scoringEverton's second with a close-range volley.
Hackney, though, has needed to be patient early in hisEvertoncareer.
After starting the opening game of the season - a 2-0 win againstCrystal Palace- his only subsequent start prior to Thursday's cup victory was in the third round of the same competition against Wolves.
The central midfielder is not known for being prolific - the fourth-round win was only the second time in his career he had scored and assisted in the same game - but he knitted together phases of possession and carried the ball with the confidence that led to him being named Championship player of the year last season.
David Moyes, though, is a demanding manager and one perfectly prepared to keep young feet on the ground.
"I thought there were bits of his game that were very good," said theEvertonboss. "Getting a goal was great. There were other bits where I didn't think it was where it was [supposed to be].
"But I see this as a bit of bringing in Championship players, getting them used to the Premier League. A couple of times he got caught on the ball.
"But I really enjoyed bits. He gave us a bit of an attacking play, getting into the box, and obviously getting the goal was really good. A really good assist from Thierno Barry as well, to be fair."
While Hackney was ably assisted by strong performances from Garner and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall inEverton's midfield, the threadbare nature of the Toffees' squad means the development and contribution of the club's younger players could prove crucial in any success this season.
Of the 10 players signed on permanent deals since Moyes rejoined the club in January 2025, seven are aged 24 or under, including Barry.
The France Under-21 international is playing just a third season in a top-five European league after joining from Villarreal in July 2025, but his introduction to elite football has been more pressurised because ofEverton's lack of options up front.
Barry is the club's only specialist centre-forward, starting every match and playing 918 minutes this season. His tally of seven goals is already just one off his total from last season, despite playing 30 fewer matches.
Evertonhave recorded 24 big chances, and Barry has been involved in 15 of them (62.5%).
Whiles Moyes' hand has been somewhat forced in giving Barry game time because of a lack of alternatives, there has been a broader indication he is more prepared to back the younger members of his squad this season.
The average age ofEverton's starting XI in the Premier League has dropped by almost 18 months this season to 26 years and 216 days.
The departure of veteran midfielder Idrissa Gueye has made a difference but first-team players aged 24 or under are playing a much higher proportion of Premier League minutes than in the previous campaign.
Moyes used just 22 players in the Premier League last season. He has already used 22 in this one.
Even the youngest players in the squad appear to have gained more trust. In 2025-26, players aged 21 or under totalled 1,088 minutes for the Toffees, a figure that has already been exceeded this season (1,206).
At 19, Harrison Armstrong is the youngest regular inEverton's senior squad. In January, he had completed a six-month loan spell at Preston and Moyes considered sending him back to Deepdale for the remainder of last season before slowly integrating him into the first team.
This season, the teenager has started every Premier League match.
Winger Tyler Dibling, 20, initially struggled after a £35m move from Southampton in the summer of 2025 but was positive in gettingEvertonon to the front foot on againstNewcastleon Thursday night.
Tyrique George joined on a permanent deal fromChelseain the summer after spending the second half of last season on loan atEvertonduring which he made only one league start.
The 20-year-old has already made five this season, scoring his first goal for the club in the 2-2 draw withManchester Unitedin September.
George also started the EFL Cup fixture last week and won back possession for the opening goal.
Merlin Rohl broke into the team towards the end of last season and the 24-year-old midfielder, who also signed permanently in the summer following an initial loan spell, has since been trusted to fillEverton's problem position of right-back.
After missing four games because of injury, he was immediately brought back into the starting XI againstChelsea. He was then preferred to the more experienced Ainsley Maitland-Niles at right-back for matches againstArsenalandNewcastle.
When asked if Grealish would return to the squad for Monday's rematch at St James' Park, Moyes said he would not reveal any team news, though there is no doubt that experience still counts among the 63-year-old's most valuable commodities.
Defender James Tarkowksi, 33, has been a standout performer so far this season, while the form of fellow senior players such as Jordan Pickford, 32, and Dewsbury-Hall, 28 remain critical to thisEvertonside.
But whenEvertonmeetNewcastlefor the second time in less than a week on Monday, Grealish could again miss out.
In his absence, younger heads were good enough to win a cup tie. It would be further indication of their growing influence if they were to repeat that result in the Premier League.

Judge tosses case accusing ex-FBI officials of lying to CongressSkip Navigation
MarketsBusinessInvestingTechPolitics & PolicyVideoWatchlistInvesting ClubPROLivestreamMenu
A federal judge in Washington dismissed the Department of Justice's case accusing two former FBI officials of lying to Congress about investigations into Hunter Biden.
The judge reportedly blasted the Justice Department, saying the situation "cannot be described as anything other than weaponization."
He accused the DOJ of a "slapdash job" prosecuting ex-officials Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, suggesting it rushed the case ahead of the midterm election.
Deputy Assistant Director for Counterterrorism at the FBI Nikki Floris, testifies before the House Judiciary Committee hearing on Capitol Hill in Washington, Oct. 22, 2019.Susan Walsh | AP
A federal judge on Monday blasted the Department of Justice for "weaponization" as he dismissed itscaseaccusing twoformer FBI officialsof lying to Congress about investigations intoHunter Biden, multiple news outlets reported.
Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui, in a hearing in U.S. District Court in Washington, reportedly tore into the DOJ over its "slapdash job" prosecuting ex-officials Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, saying he was "deeply troubled by what has happened here."
Faruqui said the government lacked probable cause and failed to present evidence that the officials' statements before the House Judiciary Committee in 2023 were knowingly false, MS NOW reported.
He also accused the DOJ of wrongly rushing the case ahead of themidterm election. The situation "cannot be described as anything other than weaponization," he said, according to MS NOW.

The judge even apologized to the government's lawyers, calling it "incredibly unfair" that they were assigned to defend the flawed case.
"This does not feel like an investigation," Faruqui reportedly added. "It feels like a broken one-wish willow obsession."
The DOJ did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.
Attorneys for Floris and Benavides praised the judge's decision outside the courthouse later Monday morning.
"This case should never have been brought. The government had no case, as the judge just laid out," a lawyer for Floris said, slamming the prosecution as a "spaghetti-at-the-wall, Hunter-Biden-conspiracy fever dream."
A lawyer for Benavides said they hope the DOJ will not try to keep the case alive by seeking an indictment before a grand jury "where they get to be behind closed doors and get to shape the narrative, and we are unable to present our side."
The DOJ did not take that step when they unveiled the allegations against Floris and Benavides on Oct. 23.
Rather, despite the alleged misconduct taking place years earlier, prosecutors acquired a criminal complaint, which only requires a judge's signature. Criminal complaints are often used to obtain arrest warrant in situations where prosecutorsneed to move quickly.
Faruqui had flagged that circumstance as unusual, and last week refused to sign off on a superseding complaint that added an obstruction charge against the two ex-officials.
"I'm concerned with your view as to what the law is," the judge told the prosecutors in a hearing last Tuesday. "Why today, on this one case, have you changed the entire history of how you charge cases?"

Judge tosses case against two officials accused of lying about Hunter Biden | FBI | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation
Hunter Biden, son of former president Joe Biden, and his wife Melissa leave the federal court building in Los Angeles, California on 5 September 2024.Photograph: David Swanson/ReutersView image in fullscreenHunter Biden, son of former president Joe Biden, and his wife Melissa leave the federal court building in Los Angeles, California on 5 September 2024.Photograph: David Swanson/Reuters
Judge tosses case against two officials accused of lying about Hunter Biden
The two FBI agents were charged with making false statements to Congress while testifying about the bureau’s role in investigating Biden’s laptop
A federal judge dismissed criminal charges against two former FBI officials who were accused of lying about theirinvolvement in the investigation into Hunter Biden, the son of former president Joe Biden, on Monday.
Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui said prosecutors failed to show probable cause that the two former officials, Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, had knowingly made false statements.
Faruqui also suggested prosecutors purposefullybrought the chargesat a sensitive time, just 10 days before the midterm elections.
“What has transpired here cannot be described as anything other than weaponization,” Faruqui said during the court hearing. “I will ​not bury ​my head in the sand and pretend I cannot read a calendar.”
The judge criticized federal prosecutors for rushing the prosecution and making “critical mistakes”. Faruqui said that some of the former officials’ ​statements were not actually false and others could be attributed to “honest mistakes of memory”.
Federal prosecutors in Washington DC charged Floris and Benavides last month with making false statements to members of Congress in 2023 while testifying to the House judiciary committee.
The two former officials were testifying about the bureau’s role in investigating the contents ofa laptop that belonged to Hunter Biden.
Floris and Benavides served on anFBItaskforce that examined potential foreign influence in American politics. The taskforce was initially formed after the 2016 presidential election when officials raised concerns that Russia attempted to interfere with the election.
The FBI taskforce had raised concerns in the lead-up to the 2020 presidential election that Russia could have engaged in another disinformation operation to assist Donald Trump’s campaign by bolstering claims about Hunter Biden’s laptop.
Last week, an FBI agent testified last week ​that the probe into Floris and ‌Benavides began with the president’s ​primetime address in July on election ​security, during which he announced the FBI would investigate whether US intelligence agencies had suppressed information about Chinese meddling in the 2020 election.
The next day, the FBI director,Kash Patel, tasked the bureau’s Kansas City field office with scrutinizing Floris, who had cast doubt on an FBI intelligence report claiming that China sought to interfere in the 2020 election to boost Joe Biden over Trump.
Trump has publicly criticized individuals that he believes undermined his efforts to overturn the 2020 presidential results.
But since returning to office in January 2025, the justice department has targeted people that Trump views as enemies through indictments and complaints. However, some high-profile attempts have failed to bear fruit.
While the justice department’s complaint against Floris and Benavides has been dismissed, prosecutors could try to charge them again by asking a grand jury to review evidence and approve charges.

He said it “cannot be described as anything other than weaponization”.
“I will not bury my head in the sand and pretend I cannot read a calendar,” Faruqui said in court, referring to its proximity to the midterms. “I will not lobotomize myself that way.”
The case suggested that Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides misled Congress in 2023 by lying about their knowledge of and involvement in an investigation into a laptop the Justice Department said was dropped off at a Delaware tech shop in 2019 by Hunter Biden.
An FBI agent who worked on the case testified that the investigation into Floris and Benavides began last July under the direction of FBI Director Kash Patel. The Associated Press news agency reported that the case echoed complaints by President Donald Trump and his allies that potentially damaging information about the Biden family was suppressed during the 2020 election, which Trump lost.
The Justice Department may still have the chance to pursue a grand jury indictment of the former FBI officials.
Nonetheless, Faruqui’s early ruling and concerns about the case hamper the Justice Department’s case.
In a preliminary hearing last week, the judge pointed out that the Justice Department was not acting in accordance with legal procedure when it filed an amended complaint with an additional charge without first clearing the charge with the court — something he said he had never seen before.

Trận cầu tâm điểm của ngày 2-11 là màn so tài giữa hai trong số những đội mạnh nhất củabóng chuyềnnam Việt Nam lúc này: Biên Phòng và Công An TP.HCM.
Đội bóng quân đội là đương kim vô địch quốc gia, sở hữu những nội binh chất lượng với nhiều tuyển thủ như Ngọc Thuân, Văn Duy, Thế Khải, Duy Tuyến.
Bên kia chiến tuyến, Công An TP.HCM có lợi thế sân nhà. Họ cũng có nhiều VĐV là thành viên tuyển quốc gia, đồng thời có thêm 2 ngoại binh "xịn" là Farhan Halim (Indonesia) và Morteza Sharifi (Iran).
Ghi ít điểm hơn, Thanh Thúy vẫn vượt qua Bích Thủy ở Giải bóng chuyền Nhật BảnĐỌC NGAY
Màn so tài giữa hai đội bóng lớn không khiến người hâm mộ thất vọng khi kéo dài tới 5 set và không ít tình huống tranh cãi. Công An TP.HCM có nhiều thời cơ ở trận này.
Nhưng rồi Biên Phòng mới là đội thể hiện tốt hơn vào thời điểm quan trọng, để giành chiến thắng nghẹt thở 3-2 (22-25, 26-24, 22-25, 25-17, 17-15).
Kết quả này giúp đội bóng áo lính duy trì chuỗi bất bại từ đầu mùa, với thành tích đến lúc này là 12 trận toàn thắng và chắc chắn đứng nhất vòng bảng dù vẫn còn 2 lượt.
Trong khi đó Công An TP.HCM rơi xuống hạng 3 với 8 trận thắng, thua đội nhì bảng Thể Công 1 trận (9 trận thắng).
Ở một trận cầu tâm điểm khác, LPBank Ninh Bình đánh bại Hà Nội 3-1 (25-23, 25-21, 17-25, 25-23). Kết quả này cũng giúp xác định đủ hai nhóm ở vòng đấu tiếp theo.
Cụ thể, nhóm chắc suất top 4 và tiến vào vòng chung kết đua vô địch là Biên Phòng, Thể Công, Công An TP.HCM và LPBank Ninh Bình. Nhóm 4 đội cuối bảng phải bước vào vòng tranh trụ hạng là Hà Nội, TP.HCM, Đà Nẵng và Sanest Khánh Hòa.
Giai đoạn vòng bảng vẫn còn 2 lượt đấu. Tại đây, các đội vẫn còn mục tiêu là giành vị trí cao nhất có thể để tránh gặp các đối thủ mạnh ở vòng tiếp theo.
Giải bóng chuyền nam vô địch quốc gia 2026 sẽ tạm nghỉ trong ngày mai (3-11) và sẽ trở lại thi đấu vào ngày 4-11.

CLB Biên Phòng (trái) khẳng định sức mạnh với 12 trận toàn thắng ở giải bóng chuyền nam quốc gia 2026

Trận thắng này giúp CLB Thể Công Tân Cảng qua mặtCLB Công an TP.HCM, vươn lên vị trí nhì bảng. CLB Thể Công Tân Cảng vươn lên vị trí thứ 2 trên bảng xếp hạng sau chiến thắng trước CLB TP.HCM
Với 12 trận thắng (31 điểm), CLB Biên Phòng chắc chắn giữ ngôi nhất bảng, ngay cả khi thua ở 2 trận đấu còn lại của giai đoạn 2. 3 đội còn lại là Thể Công Tân Cảng (9 trận thắng, 26 điểm), Công an TP.HCM (8 trận thắng, 27 điểm), CLB Ninh Bình (8 trận thắng, 24 điểm) sẽ tranh chấp vị trí hạng 2, 3, 4. CLB Công an TP.HCM chính thức ghi tên vào vòng bán kết giải bóng chuyền nam quốc gia 2026

Harry Kane đoạt Quả bóng vàng 2026: Hình mẫu nhà vô địch toàn diện
(Dân trí) - Một thời gian dài người hâm mộ chê cười, thậm chí mỉa mai Harry Kane là ngôi sao lớn không danh hiệu, khi anh trải qua quãng thời gian chưa từng đứng bục vinh quang cùng CLB Tottenham.
Nhắc đến Harry Kane, báo chíthế giớitừng tốn không ít giấy mực để bàn luận về một ngôi sao thường xuyên lỡ hẹn với các danh hiệu. Đó là quãng thời gian tiền đạo người Anh còn khoác áo Tottenham, nơi anh đã dành phần lớn thanh xuân để cống hiến cho đội bóng thành London.
Gia nhập học viện đào tạo trẻ của Tottenham khi mới 11 tuổi (năm 2004), ra mắt đội một vào năm 2009 và gắn bó với đội bóng quê hương trong suốt nhiều năm sau đó, Harry Kane đã không ít lần trải qua cảm giác hụt hẫng, tiếc nuối khi chỉ về nhì trong những cuộc đua danh hiệu.
Harry Kane là huyền thoại của Tottenham, đóng góp tới 280 bàn thắng trong suốt 14 mùa giải liên tiếp (Ảnh: Getty).
Trong quãng thời gian ấy, Harry Kane ghi tới 280 bàn thắng, ba lần giành danh hiệu Vua phá lướiPremier League(các mùa 2015-2016, 2016-2017 và 2020-2021) cùng một lần đoạt giải Cầu thủ kiến tạo xuất sắc nhất Premier League mùa 2020-2021. Thế nhưng, điều đáng tiếc là ngôi sao sinh năm 1993 chưa một lần được nâng cao chiếc cúp vô địch cùng Tottenham.
Mùa giải 2015-2016, Tottenham của Harry Kane lỡ hẹn với chức vô địch Cúp Liên đoàn Anh sau thất bại 1-2 trước đối thủ cùng thành phốChelseaở trận chung kết. Cũng trong mùa giải ấy, Kane lần đầu tiên giành danh hiệu Vua phá lưới Premier League với 25 bàn thắng, một thành tích đáng nể.
Một năm sau, Harry Kane tiếp tục tỏa sáng với 29 bàn thắng tại Premier League. Tuy nhiên, những nỗ lực của anh không đủ giúp Tottenham vượt qua Chelsea trong cuộc đua vô địch. Đội bóng thành London một lần nữa phải chấp nhận vị trí á quân.
Mùa giải 2018-2019, Tottenham thi đấu thăng hoa và lần đầu tiên trong lịch sử lọt vào trận chung kết Champions League. Harry Kane được kỳ vọng sẽ có danh hiệu lớn đầu tiên trong sự nghiệp, nhưng anh cùng các đồng đội phải nhận thất bại cay đắng 0-2 trước Liverpool.
Đến mùa giải 2020-2021, Tottenham lần thứ hai góp mặt trong trận chung kết Cúp Liên đoàn Anh dưới thời Harry Kane, nhưng tiếp tục thất bại trước Manchester City với tỷ số 0-1. Những lần lỡ hẹn liên tiếp khiến Kane trở thành hình ảnh tiêu biểu cho một nghịch lý củabóng đáAnh: một chân sút hàng đầu thế giới nhưng mãi chưa thể chạm tay vào những danh hiệu tập thể lớn.
Dẫu vậy, thất bại không khiến Harry Kane gục ngã. Anh quyết định rời Tottenham để gia nhập Bayern Munich vào năm 2023, đặt niềm tin vào đội bóng giàu truyền thống của nước Đức với hy vọng thay đổi vận mệnh và chấm dứt cơn khát danh hiệu kéo dài suốt nhiều năm.
Bước ngoặt khi chuyển đến Bayern Munich
Quyết định gia nhập “gã khổng lồ” Bayern Munich đã mở ra chương mới trong sự nghiệp của Harry Kane. Sau 280 bàn thắng cho Tottenham, tiền đạo sinh năm 1993 tiếp tục cho thấy hiệu suất săn bàn đáng kinh ngạc trong màu áo “Hùm xám”. Chỉ sau ba mùa giải, anh đã ghi 156 bàn thắng và có 40 pha kiến tạo sau 159 trận.
Riêng mùa giải 2025-2026, Harry Kane ghi 61 bàn sau 51 trận cho Bayern Munich. Tại Bundesliga, siêu sao 33 tuổi ghi 36 bàn thắng, bỏ xa người xếp thứ hai tới 17 bàn và giành danh hiệu Vua phá lưới lần thứ ba liên tiếp. Ở UEFA Champions League, Kane ghi 14 bàn, góp công đưa Bayern Munich vào bán kết.
Tiền đạo người Anh còn ghi 10 bàn tại Cúp Quốc gia Đức, trong đó có cú hat-trick ở trận chung kết giúp Bayern Munich đánh bại Stuttgart với tỷ số 3-0. Trong màu áo đội tuyển Anh, Harry Kane ghi 12 bàn sau 14 trận, góp phần giúp “Tam sư” giành huy chương đồng tạiWorld Cup2026.
Harry Kane đã chứng minh rằng không có giới hạn nào cho những ước mơ được theo đuổi bằng sự kiên trì và nỗ lực. Ở tuổi 33, khi nhiều người cho rằng các cầu thủ đã bước vào giai đoạn cuối của sự nghiệp đỉnh cao, Kane tự hào nâng cao danh hiệu cá nhân cao quý nhất của bóng đá thế giới: Quả bóng vàng.
Khoảnh khắc ấy càng trở nên đặc biệt khi ngày 26/10, lễ trao giải diễn ra tại Nhà hát London Palladium, ngay giữa thủ đô nước Anh, quê hương của Kane. Việc lễ trao giải được tổ chức tại London thay vì Paris dường như càng khiến câu chuyện về hành trình chinh phục đỉnh cao của anh thêm phần ý nghĩa.

Russian bombing kills 24 people at humanitarian aid centre in Ukraine, Kyiv says - BBC News
Video shows smoke rising from Komyshuvakha blast crater
At least 24 people were killed after Russian bombs hit an aid distribution centre, in an attack that Ukraine's leader has called "utterly horrific".
Five people were injured and 27 initially reported missing after at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit the village of Komyshuvakha in the southern Zaporizhzhia region, regional head Mykhailo Semikin said.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said that after the first strike on the local school "used for humanitarian needs", there was a second attack on the place where people were sheltering.
He posteda video showing a huge crater left after Monday's attack, and rescuer teams searching through the rubble.

Image source,National police of UkraineImage caption,
The Russian strikes left a huge crater where Ukrainian officials say people were sheltering
The Russian military has not publicly commented.
Zelensky initially put the death toll at 18, but Ukraine's state emergencies service DSNS later said 24 people, including two rescuers and four police officers, were confirmed to have been killed.
"The Russians could not have been unaware that the local residents who remained in Komyshuvakha received humanitarian aid there every week," the Ukrainian president wrote in a post on social media.
"This is yet another proof that Russia does not want any de-escalation."
He said that after a recent successful joint Russian-Ukrainian operation to evacuate civilians from the Russia-occupied southern city of Oleshky, "there was a moment when the next steps could show that peace is possible".
"With such killings, Russia is sending the exact opposite signal - Russia is counting on further killings," Zelensky said.
Meanwhile, Semikin described the Russian attack as a "terrible tragedy" for the village, confirming that "people are still under the rubble".
He said that rescue teams were working at the scene, but they were forced to halt their operation a number of times because of Russian drone attacks in the area.

White Noise Machines Worthy of Your Nightstand in 2026: Snooz, Hatch, and More | WIREDSkip to main content
I have chronicinsomnia. I need a white noise machine, asleep mask, a pitch-black room, and maybe some light tranquilizers just to fall asleep. (I'm joking, sort of.) If I'm traveling and forget my sound machine, I have to play white noise from myperpetually dying phone. Whether you're shopping for your kiddo or yourself, a white noise machine can help everyone sleep better at night.
These devices are simple, even as companies keep adding bells and whistles. They now come in all shapes and sizes, with options for playing different noise frequencies and soothing nature sounds—whether you need one at home or a portable model for life on the go. And they’re not just for kids or babies; if, like me, you want to quiet your inner monologue and finally drift off, this guide is for you.
We've tested everything: thebest sleep trackers,sunrise alarm clocks,mattresses, andextreme alarm clocks. Check out all of the WIRED Reviews team'ssleepcoverage for our recommendations.
Note:If you're buying for a child, keep sound machines to no more than50 decibelsand farther than 200 centimeters (6.5 feet) from where your baby sleeps.
Can White Noise Machines Typically Run All Night?
Does a Fan Make a Good White Noise Machine?
How Does WIRED Select Models to Be Reviewed?
What Does WIRED Do With the Sound Machines After Testing Them?
“Colors” of noiseare measured similarly to light. Pure white noise is a mix of all the frequencies humans can hear, so while these machines are often called “white noise" machines, white noise itself isn't always a relaxing sound (think of the static on your TV). Pink and brown noise are at the lower end of the spectrum, aren't as grating, and have been found to help people sleepa little more deeply. If you've seen pink noise, brown noise, and green noise amid all the white noise machine chatter, it's because, more often than not, you'll find those options bundled into one machine. If you think of sound waves as being loosely analogous to light waves, then the different colors of noise refer to different parts of the sound spectrum. The fun thing about using a sound machine for sleep is that you get to experiment with these noise frequencies to find what works best for you.

Newcastle United v Everton: Premier League – live | Premier League | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigationSkip to key events
Premier League updates from the 8pm GMT kick-off
Live scores|Read today’s Football Daily|Email Daniel
LIVEUpdated23m agoDaniel HarrisMon 2 Nov 2026 13.30 ESTLast modified on Mon 2 Nov 2026 13.31 ESTShareKey events
The scene inside the ground before Newcastle v Everton.Photograph: Richard Lee/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenThe scene inside the ground before Newcastle v Everton.Photograph: Richard Lee/ShutterstockKey events
Different people are motivated by different stimuli. Some of us need to feel secure to deliver our best work, struggling when put under pressure to perform, while others need provocation to get them going, indignance driving the desire to stop coasting in order to prove people wrong.
Chances are, Thierno Barry falls into the first category. He showed enough at Villarreal to persuade Everton to sign him but then struggled to settle intoPremier Leaguerhythm, subbed off 18 times in 21 league starts and beginning the other 17 games on the bench and returning a paltry eight goals. It was not an especially auspicious start.
As such, it was no surprise thatEvertonwanted to sign Folarin Balogun from Monaco – essentially, to go in front of Barry. But that move broke down on deadline day then Joshua Zirkzee, a desperate contingency, stayed at Manchester United – to what end is unclear – meaning, with Beto sold, Barry moved from second-choice to only choice.
Very quickly, crisis turned into fortune. Able to relax in the knowledge there were no options but him, so the chances of him being sub or subbed were minuscule, and no longer dealing with a newborn or playing with the shoulder problem that hampered his debut campaign, Barry looks a different player. He scored on the opening weekend of the season and most recently last Thursday, when Everton binned Newcastle from the League Cup – a contest which featured an affirming ruckus close to full-time. Having bagged seven in 11 appearances, he’s on a roll and will fancy himself to add to that tally this evening – though only bottom-placed Sunderland have managed fewer than his side’s eight league goals.
Newcastle, meantime, will hope to avoid a third Monday-night clattering of the season, already beaten 4-1 at Leeds and Coventry. There have been some good signs under Matthias Jaissle but also some absolute dross, the lack of physicality a particular issue and especially glaring given, until recently, that was a strong point.
Last weekend’s win at Palace, though, has earned a little respite and, with Will Osula given a start and scoring, they too have a centre-forward ready to go – or would have, had he not got injured, again. He’s unlikely to play tonight, exacerbating a pre-existing problem: only two clubs have created fewer than Newcastle’s 14 big chances and, with Jaissle so far unwilling to use the young attackers signed in the summer for anything other than late cameos, there’s no reason to expect things to change.
All of which is to say that this match, 12th v 14th, is unlikely to deliver a goalfest elevated by flowing football. But happily, different people are motivated by different stimuli, and it’s not possible to appreciate English football without enjoying aggression, intensity needle and incompetence – of which there will, without doubt, be plenty to enjoy.

lead_title: Judge accuses DOJ of 'weaponization,' tosses case against ex-FBI officials

evidence_pages.https://www.npr.org/2026/11/02/g-s1-1512:
Judge tosses case against ex-FBI officials over Hunter Biden : NPRAccessibility links
Judge tosses case against ex-FBI officials over Hunter BidenThe judge said he was "deeply troubled" by the mistakes and rushed nature of the case over the FBI's Hunter Biden probes — one of several politically charged DOJ actions ahead of the midterms.
Judge accuses DOJ of 'weaponization,' tosses case against ex-FBI officials
Updated November 2, 20262:31 PM ETOriginally publishedNovember 2, 20261:54 PM ET
Magistrate Judge Zia M. Faruqui speaks before a debate at the Prettyman Federal Courthouse in Washington, D.C. in November 2024.Craig Hudson/The Washington Post via Getty Imageshide caption
toggle captioniCraig Hudson/The Washington Post via Getty Images
A federal magistrate judge on Monday dismissed the Justice Department's criminal case against twoformer FBI officialscharged in connection with the bureau's investigations into former President Joe Biden's son.
Bradley Benavides and Nikki Floris were charged around two weeks ago with lying to Congress in 2023 about their knowledge of the FBI's investigations into Biden's son, Hunter Biden. It is one of several politically charged actions by the Justice Department under President Trump in the run-up to the midterm elections on Tuesday.
At a hearing in federal court in Washington, D.C., U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui castigated the government's investigation into Floris and Benavides, describing it as rushed and riddled with errors.
Politics, norms and the DOJ's unprecedented pre-election headlines
"I am deeply troubled by what has happened here," Faruqui said in a scathing ruling from the bench. "What transpired here cannot be described as anything other than weaponization."
The court's ruling came after a days-long preliminary hearing last week to determine whether probable cause existed to charge Floris and Benavides with lying to Congress. It featured testimony from one of the FBI agents who investigated the case.
In a statement, a Justice Department spokesperson said the department "disagrees with the Magistrate's decision, which remarkably appears to suggest that high-ranking government officials are immune from accountability for making materially false statements to Congress."
"We are evaluating all options but cannot comment further on an ongoing criminal investigation," the spokesperson said. "The Department's actions will continue to be guided by the facts, the evidence, and the law—not politics."
Over the course of an hour, Faruqui on Monday laid out the basis for his decision before a packed courtroom that included many former senior FBI officials.
The judge noted that the investigation into Floris and Benavides was opened on FBI Director Kash Patel's orders the day after President Trump delivered aprimetime addresson national TV in mid-July. In that speech, Trump repeated his false claims about fraud in the 2020 election and urged the FBI to investigate.
In primetime speech, Trump doesn't provide evidence for illegal voting
Faruqui noted that the alleged false statements were made to Congress in 2023, yet the Justice Department waited three years to pursue the case. Prosecutors then brought charges some two weeks before the midterm elections, despite a DOJ policy prohibiting timing any action to influence an election.
That was not the only unusual decision by the department. The judge also noted that charges were filed as a criminal complaint, a document usually used when there is some need for urgency such as an imminent danger, a statute of limitations deadline or a risk of flight—none of which existed in this case.
The only event that was looming here, he said, was the midterms.
"I will not bury my head in the sand and pretend I cannot read a calendar," Faruqui said. "I will not lobotomize myself that way."
Ex-FBI employees charged with lying to Congress over Hunter Biden inquiries
He also said prosecutors appear not to want to take this case before a grand jury, perhaps given the Justice Department's poor track record recently with grand juries in Washington, D.C.
On several occasions under the Trump administration, grand juries in the nation's capital haverefused to return indictmentsin high-profile, politically charged cases.
While Faruqui dismissed the case, he said that nothing is stopping prosecutors from going to a grand jury and trying to secure an indictment. Prosecutors could also appeal his decision to the district'schief judge.
After the hearing, a group of former FBI officials greeted Floris and Benavides outside the courtroom. Floris, tears in her eyes, hugged several of her former colleagues before sharing a hug with Benavides.
"This case should never have been brought. The government had no case," said Margaret Donovan, one of Floris' attorneys. "As the judge just laid out, this was a slap-dash complaint, spaghetti-at-the wall, Hunter Biden conspiracy fever dream. But facts still matter in a courtroom. The truth still matters in a courtroom. And that's what we say prevailed today."
