lead_title: Melbourne Cup 2026: King Charles’ former horse Point of Law storms home to win

evidence_pages.https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n:
Melbourne Cup 2026: King Charles’ former horse Point of Law storms home to win | Melbourne Cup | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation
Point of Law wins the 2026 Melbourne Cup as jockey Ethan Brown salutes ahead of Zahrann and Juja Kibo at Flemington Racecourse.Photograph: Josh Chadwick/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenPoint of Law wins the 2026 Melbourne Cup as jockey Ethan Brown salutes ahead of Zahrann and Juja Kibo at Flemington Racecourse.Photograph: Josh Chadwick/Getty Images
Melbourne Cup 2026: King Charles’ former horse Point of Law storms home to win
Jockey Ethan Brown salutes after chasing down Royal Supremacy
Winning trainer Ciaron Maher fills top three places at Flemington
Point of Law justified his favouritism at the 2026Melbourne Cupafter the three-year-old stallion that was owned by King Charles until earlier this year reeled in Royal Supremacy in a thrilling feature race at Flemington Racecourse.
Jockey Ethan Brown guided the Ciaron Maher-trained horse to victory in the $10m race after Royal Supremacy – another in Maher’s stable – had led by about 20 lengths at one point.
Guardian Essential poll: record number of Australians are turning their backs on the Melbourne CupRead more
Maher had a record seven horses in Tuesday’s race and became the first trainer to achieve the trifecta, with Zahrann coming in second and another from his stable, Juja Kibo, third. The Joseph O’Brien-trained Sons and Lovers finished fourth.
It is the second time Maher has overseen a winner in the “race that stops the nation”, while victory for Brown marked a stunning turnaround in his fortunes after he nearly died in a horrendous fall three years ago.
Point of Law was bought by an Australian syndicate from King Charles in August and surged to the top of the betting after a strong performance in the Geelong Cup.
View image in fullscreenEthan Brown rides Point Of Law to victory in the 2026 Melbourne Cup Day at Flemington Racecourse.Photograph: Quinn Rooney/Getty Images
“He’s going to be a superstar. Stunning horse this,” Brown told Channel Nine after his victory, adding that winning the Melbourne Cup was a dream come true.
“Please don’t wake me up,” he said. “It’s every jockey’s dream to do this. And I can’t believe it. I was confident in the horse. Everyone I’ve spoken to said they’ve never gone in with that confidence.
“He’s in such good hands with Ciaron. He had the best turn of foot in the race. I thought he ran really well and he’s going to be a future star if he’s not already one today.”
Brown spent six months out of the saddle after a serious fall in the 2023 Australian Guineas at Flemington that left him in hospital and considering his future in racing.
“There was something burning inside me,” Brown said. “I was inches from losing my life, but a bit of time off and I realised I wasn’t any good at anything else. There was a slow burn inside of me [to come back].”
Point of Law was purchased from the royal stable in the UK after winning the Group 3 Bahrain Trophy at Newmarket in July.
“I knew I had my best hand going into it, but we just had to execute,” Maher told Nine. “I certainly didn’t know that Royal Supremacy would lead by that far, but it is a true test of staying and, Point of Law, he’s just thrived.
“It has been a whirlwind but I’m very proud of all the team to get three horses in the first three spots.”
After pop star Robbie Williams had urged those massed at Flemington to “let me entertain you” and then delivered a typically uplifting pre-race performance, focus returned to the horses, with 23 of the expected 24 runners parading through the mounting yard.
View image in fullscreenRobbie Williams entertains the crowd on Melbourne Cup Day at Flemington Racecourse.Photograph: Martin Keep/AAP
Earlier, top trainer Chris Waller was fined $50,000 after his contender Asterix was scratched having been found to have received anti-inflammatory medication on race-day.
The application of Penetrene is generally allowed on horses but there is a blanket ban on race-day treatments. Waller revealed its use on the forelegs of Asterix, part-owned by former New Zealand cricketer Mark Greatbatch, hours before the race was a mistake.
“The horse gets the same treatment every day,” Waller said. “It’s a very basic liniment most stables use and I guess the pressure of race day, the person that looks after the horse, put it on his legs right in front of the security guard, nothing to hide.
“It’s not her fault, I’ve got to wear the responsibility, it’s my team. It’s rare for us to make mistakes but the pressure of race day, you can’t explain how it affects everybody, everyone is on edge on Melbourne Cup Day and you think a little bit differently.”
It left Hall of Fame trainer Waller with just one horse in the race, Soul of Spain, who finished 13th.
evidence_pages.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/horse-racing:
Melbourne Cup: King's former horse Point Of Law wins prestigious Australian race - BBC Sport
Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,
Point of Law is going to be a "superstar", says jockey Ethan Brown
Point of Law, a horse previously owned by King Charles, snatched victory in a thrilling 166th staging of the Melbourne Cup.
The three-year-old colt, who was bought from the King for an undisclosed sum earlier this year, reeled in Royal Supremacy for a win on just his sixth career start.
Ridden by Australian jockey Ethan Brown, Point Of Law emerged from the middle of the pack and raced clear in the final 100m to finish ahead of Zahrann and Juja Kibo as Ciaron Maher became the first trainer to saddle the top three finishers.
The Melbourne Cup, run in Australia since 1861 is often referred to as the "race that stops a nation". With a prize of A$10.2m ($7.04m; £5.3m), it is the country's third richest race, but is considered the most prestigious.
"Don't wake me up, this is every jockey's dream," said a triumphant Brown.
He added that he was telling himself "just stay cool, stay patient" as Royal Supremacy raced more than a dozen lengths ahead, before pushing Point of Law to overtake on the home stretch.
The King sold Point of Law to a group of investors including former AFL player Chris Judd and his wife Bec.
"He's going to be a superstar horse. He's something special," said Brown of the horse that won the Geelong Cup last month. "He's in the best of hands with Ciaron Maher."
Maher had a record seven of the 23 horses in this year's cup.
Brown, who grew up in Alice Springs, said he never dreamed as a kid that he would be riding the Melbourne Cup, but he had been given "a lot of great support" in his career.
Brown was "inches from losing my life" after a fall from his horse in a 2023 race sent him to hospital and kept him out of racing for six months.
Tens of thousands of people enjoyed sunny weather at Flemington on Tuesday, where they were also entertained by Robbie Williams. Organisers said the UK pop star's appearance, which included a 10-piece band, dancers and pyrotechnics, was the biggest pre-cup performance ever staged at Flemington.
The day was not without controversy. One horse, Asterix, was scratched from the race earlier on Tuesday, after it was discovered a stable worker had administered it the medication penetrene earlier that morning.
The medication is used to treat inflammation and muscle soreness, but no treatments of any kind are permitted on race day. Race stewards said the medication was applied in error but still constituted a "serious breach", the Age reported. Trainer Chris Waller was reportedly fined A$50,000 (£26,000; $35,000) for what he described as a simple mistake by a staff member under pressure.
Outside Flemington, crowds from the Australia-wide "Nup to the Cup" movement also gathered to protest against horse racing on the industry's most high profile day. Some held signs with slogans including "horse racing kills", "don't bet on cruelty" and "no more whips".
Interest in the race among Australians has been declining, according to a Guardian Essential poll, which this year found just 9% of people said they had high interest in the race, and 23% had moderate interest. However more than 60% said it was a unique part of Australia's national identity.
Last year the Melbourne Cup drew a record $382.5 million in bets.

King Charles III showed off his dance moves during a colourful Junkanoo street parade in Nassau, the capital of the Bahamas, on Wednesday, 28 October, as part of his first Caribbean tour since becoming monarch.
TheBritish kingjoined in the celebrations,dancing to the rhythm of the traditional Junkanoo festivalbefore watching performers and decorated floats pass through the streets. Footage showsCharles dancing during the paradein an unusual moment of informality during theroyal visit to the Bahamas.
After the parade,Charles walked through Nassau's Parliament Square, stopping at market stalls tomeet local vendorsand examine handmade goods such as woven raffia baskets.
The king alsogreeted members of the publicwho gathered to see him.Junkanoois a longstanding Bahamian tradition celebrated through elaborate costumes, music, dancing and street processions.
The Bahamasgained independence from Britain in 1973butremains a Commonwealth realm with Charles III as its head of state. His visit brings together the country's cultural heritage and itscontinuing constitutional ties to the British monarchy.

“I was inches from losing my life, but a bit of time off and I realised I wasn’t any good at anything else.
There was a slow burn inside of me [to come back].”
Point of Law was purchased from the royal stable in the UK after winning the Group 3 Bahrain Trophy at Newmarket in July.
“I knew I had my best hand going into it, but we just had to execute,” Maher told Nine.

Earlier, top trainer Chris Waller was fined $50,000 after his contender Asterix was scratched having been found to have received anti-inflammatory medication on race-day.
The application of Penetrene is generally allowed on horses but there is a blanket ban on race-day treatments.

“The horse gets the same treatment every day,” Waller said.
“It’s a very basic liniment most stables use and I guess the pressure of race day, the person that looks after the horse, put it on his legs right in front of the security guard, nothing to hide.
“It’s not her fault, I’ve got to wear the responsibility, it’s my team.
It’s rare for us to make mistakes but the pressure of race day, you can’t explain how it affects everybody, everyone is on edge on Melbourne Cup Day and you think a little bit differently.”

The Melbourne Cup, run in Australia since 1861 is often referred to as the "race that stops a nation".

Image source,ShutterstockImage caption,
Nuno Espirito Santo took charge of West Ham in September 2025
West Ham United have sacked head coach Nuno Espirito Santo after their disappointing start to the Championship season.
The 52-year-old has been in charge since September 2025 and oversaw the Hammers' relegation from the Premier League last season.
Widely seen as favourites for automatic promotion, the London side are currently eighth in the table, six points behind leaders Middlesbrough.
They have won two of their last six games and have lost back-to-back home matches - going down 3-2 to Southampton and then 3-1 to West Bromwich Albion on Saturday - losses that have seen them drop down from second place.
Assistant head coach Rui Pedro Silva and goalkeeper coach Rui Barbosa have also left the club.
Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville will take temporary charge of the side for their Championship trip to Cardiff City on Wednesday night.
"Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the board of directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the club's objectives and expectations remain on track," a West Ham United statement read.
"West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the Club, and wish them all the very best for the future.
"The process of recruiting a new head coach is already under way."
West Ham appoint Nuno after sacking Potter
What happens now at relegated West Ham?
The decision means West Ham are looking for their fourth permanent manager since David Moyes left the London Stadium in May 2024.
His successor Julen Lopetegui was sacked after just six months in charge with the Hammers mid-table having won six of their 20 Premier League matches.
He was replaced by former Chelsea and Brighton boss Graham Potter, who oversaw a 14th-placed finish, but was sacked after only eight months in charge with the club 19th in the table.
The club opted to stick with former Wolves and Tottenham Hotspur boss Espirito Santo despite him being unable to turn around the club's fortunes. They were relegated at the end of last season after finishing two points behind Spurs.
This season had a troubled start for the Hammers - they failed to win any of their first three league matches and were 19th in the table.
But a run of four successive wins in the first half of September, where they scored 16 goals and went top of the table, appeared to show they had adapted to the second tier, with a 6-0 win over Wrexham the highlight of the run.
But just two league victories have come since - a 6-0 win at nine-man Lincoln City and a 1-0 victory at Swansea City came after draws with London rivals Millwall and QPR.

Trump will get 'trounced' in midterms, Anthony Scaramucci saysSkip Navigation
MarketsBusinessInvestingTechPolitics & PolicyVideoWatchlistInvesting ClubPROLivestreamMenu
President Donald Trump will get "trounced" in the U.S. midterm elections, according to Anthony Scaramucci.
The former White House communications director also said the Republican party was facing a "civil war" after the result.
He also said he was "bearish" when it came to the outlook for the Iran war.
watch nowVIDEO14:4014:40Scaramucci: Trump is going to get trounced in the midterms and he knows itSquawk Box Europe
U.S. PresidentDonald Trumpwill get "trounced" in Tuesday's midterm elections, former White House communications director and SkyBridge Capital founder Anthony Scaramucci told CNBC.
Speaking to CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Tuesday, Scaramucci said America is in the throes of a cultural and economic struggle, with the two main parties fighting to deliver "two different visions of where the country should go."
"I think the president's going to get trounced, by the way, and I think he knows he's going to get trounced," he said.
Trump's economic approval rating hit an all-time low last month, according toCNBC's All-America Economic Survey, with 65% of respondents disapproving of the president's handling of the economy, while 80% rated the economy as fair or poor.
"You have one vote. You have one customer relations survey that you can do on the American president — that's at the midterms, and people are not happy," Scaramucci added.
"He promised affordability, he promised no more forever wars, he promised transparency on the Epstein files," Scaramucci said on Tuesday. "He didn't deliver on any of that stuff, and so there's a lot of people inside MAGA that are now also breaking from him."
The White House did not immediately respond to a CNBC request to comment. The White House previously told CNBC that Scaramucci's "relevance ended almost a decade ago." Scaramucci was White House communications directorfor 10 daysin 2017, during Trump's first term.
Prediction markets are nowpricing inaround a three-in-four chance of the Democrats winning control of the Senate in Tuesday's election. Odds and gambling platforms do not use methodologies used by traditional political polling, and therefore are not substitutes for political polls.
Scaramucci 'bearish' on Iran breakthrough
On the Iran war, Scaramucci said he was "bearish" on a potential diplomatic breakthrough after the ballot.
"I don't see any alignment between the Iranians, the Israelis, and the Americans for a potential negotiated solution right now," he said. "If the Americans are going to ramp up the military strikes alongside of the Israelis ... I don't really understand how that's going to necessarily help the region either."
The U.S. launched"defensive" strikes on Iran's Qeshm Islandovernight, a U.S. official told MS Now. Trump previously said American forces would not attack Iran before the midterms.
"Wars are very bad for business," Scaramucci told CNBC Tuesday. "They're not great for the stock market. So I would like to have a negotiated settlement, but there's nothing on the matrix where you see the concentric circles lining up, where these three groups would say, 'okay, that's a deal that all three of us are willing to accept.'"
Scaramucci also said "disarray" within the Democratic Party had been "the best thing that has happened for Donald Trump."
"And so, if he gets trounced here, there will be bicameral investigations that will be the main show because there's a lot of things that's going on in the administration that the Democrats are going to want to uncover," he said.
"The Republicans, in my mind, I think there'll be a great intellectual civil war. The Republicans are going to have to reconcile where do they want to go. It's no longer the party of Ronald Reagan, certainly not the party of George W. Bush, but is it the party of Donald Trump after he leaves the stage?"
Scaramucci added that it was going to take a long while to get away from the so-called MAGA movement.
"There'll be DNA elements of MAGA in the next presidential candidate for sure, because looming large over that presidential candidate will be Donald Trump and several hundred million dollars of his PAC money, and so they're not going to want to get too far away from him in 2028. So there will be elements of MAGA, but I also think there'll be a civil war in that party," he said.

Wheelchair rugby league: England beat USA 134-0 to reach World Cup semi-finals - BBC Sport
England have reached the final in all four previous editions of the Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup
England have improved to a "seven out of 10" rating at the 2026 Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup as they secured their place in the semi-finals, according to captain Mason Billington.
Billington led England as they dispatched minnows USA with a clinical 134-0 win, driving in 23 tries at Wollongong Entertainment Arena.
It means England will face France or Australia in the semi-finals next week.
Luis Domingos, an ex-Portugal basketball international who switched sports as well as countries and now plays for Sheffield Eagles and England, scored four tries on his first appearance at the tournament.
Chris Haynes and Billington also scored four tries apiece as eight different players got on the score sheet.
The England team who can still win the Rugby League World Cup
Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league
Last week, player Rob Hawkins said England "were not playing to our standards" in their opening 98-18 win over Wales and rated the team five out of 10.
Asked how he would rate England's showing against the USA, Billington told Premier Sports: "At least a seven. All week, we have been banging on about playing the way we want to play, and the boys really stuck to their principles.
"I'm over the moon for the guys to put on such senior performances."
Finlay O'Neill was named player of the match as he recorded 38 points, with two tries and 15 conversions.
"It was a good team effort, not just myself," O'Neill said. "We talked about how we could improve, and I think we did that.
"We need to take the positives - [there are a] few areas to work on but I think we can be very happy with that performance."
The four semi-finalists have now been set, with the final group games to decide who faces who in the knockouts.
In Pool A, Ireland ensured they will qualify alongside England with a 68-28 victory over Wales.
Ireland, who are ranked third in the world, will face the English in their final group game on Friday in Wollongong (06:00 GMT).
In Pool A, two-time champions France and hosts Australia both booked their passages through while scoring triple figures.
France, who were losing finalists against England in 2022, thrashed New Zealand 120-10.
Australia beat Scotland 104-24, and will play the French on Friday to determine the pool winners.
Scotland, New Zealand, Wales and USA all go into a ranking competition to determine fifth through to eighth place.
Wales will face USA in Pool A on Friday, while Scotland play New Zealand.

fact_units.text: Wheelchair rugby league: England beat USA 134-0 to reach World Cup semi-finals - BBC Sport
England have reached the final in all four previous editions of the Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup
England have improved to a "seven out of 10" rating at the 2026 Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup as they secured their place in the semi-finals, according to captain Mason Billington.
Billington led England as they dispatched minnows USA with a clinical 134-0 win, driving in 23 tries at Wollongong Entertainment Arena.
It means England will face France or Australia in the semi-finals next week.

Luis Domingos, an ex-Portugal basketball international who switched sports as well as countries and now plays for Sheffield Eagles and England, scored four tries on his first appearance at the tournament.
Chris Haynes and Billington also scored four tries apiece as eight different players got on the score sheet.
The England team who can still win the Rugby League World Cup
Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league
Last week, player Rob Hawkins said England "were not playing to our standards" in their opening 98-18 win over Wales and rated the team five out of 10.
Asked how he would rate England's showing against the USA, Billington told Premier Sports: "At least a seven.
All week, we have been banging on about playing the way we want to play, and the boys really stuck to their principles.
"I'm over the moon for the guys to put on such senior performances."
Finlay O'Neill was named player of the match as he recorded 38 points, with two tries and 15 conversions.
"It was a good team effort, not just myself," O'Neill said.
"We talked about how we could improve, and I think we did that.
"We need to take the positives - [there are a] few areas to work on but I think we can be very happy with that performance."
The four semi-finalists have now been set, with the final group games to decide who faces who in the knockouts.
In Pool A, Ireland ensured they will qualify alongside England with a 68-28 victory over Wales.
Ireland, who are ranked third in the world, will face the English in their final group game on Friday in Wollongong (06:00 GMT).
In Pool A, two-time champions France and hosts Australia both booked their passages through while scoring triple figures.
France, who were losing finalists against England in 2022, thrashed New Zealand 120-10.
Australia beat Scotland 104-24, and will play the French on Friday to determine the pool winners.
Scotland, New Zealand, Wales and USA all go into a ranking competition to determine fifth through to eighth place.
Wales will face USA in Pool A on Friday, while Scotland play New Zealand.

Brookfield plans $27 billion AI data center at power station; Drax rises 8%Skip Navigation
MarketsBusinessInvestingTechPolitics & PolicyVideoWatchlistInvesting ClubPROLivestreamMenu
Brookfield is planning a data center with more than one gigawatt of capacity at a site in England.
The asset manager estimated that the potential investment for the project could exceed £20 billion ($26.8 billion).
Drax Group, which operates the power station the facility will be housed at, saw shares rise more than 8% on Tuesday morning.
Follow your favorite stocksCREATE FREE ACCOUNT
Brookfieldis targeting a massive artificial intelligence data center in the north of England, as Europe scrambles to develop infrastructure to support the rollout of AI amid high energy and land costs.
Energy companyDrax Groupsaid Tuesday it has signed an agreement with Brookfield and the asset manager's neocloud platform Radiant to jointly develop an AI data center on the Drax Power Station estate in North Yorkshire. London-listed shares of Drax were up 8.8% in early morning trading.
The project is initially targeting up to 100 megawatts of capacity to be operational from the first quarter of 2028, with an additional 500 MW of capacity to be brought online between 2028 and 2031. It is then looking to secure more than 1 gigawatt of capacity at the site by an unspecified date.
Brookfield estimates total investment, including semiconductors, could exceed £20 billion ($26.8 billion), with an initial £2.5 billion investment in phase 1.
"This is a unique opportunity for the UK's AI ecosystem to build at scale," Radiant CEO Mahdi Yahya said in a statement. "By designing, building and operating from the UK, it will give British researchers, startups and enterprises access to frontier compute at home."
The first phase of Brookfield's project in North Yorkshire will use power from the grid and target commercial customers from early 2028.
The initial phase is subject to planning, regulatory and network approvals from the government and relevant agencies, alongside securing a tenant for the project, Drax said in a statement said. The company added that final investment decisions are yet to be made.
While the U.S. has surged ahead on developing the huge data centers needed to power AI, Europe has been slower to break ground on the facilities. The U.K. in particular has struggled withhigh energy costsand challenges with long waiting times for businesses to connect to the grid.
In October, it wasreportedthat Microsoft had pulled out of a deal to anchor an Nscale data center just outside London, amid delays connecting to the country's power grid. An Nscale spokesperson told CNBC at the time that it remained "committed" to the project and was "exploring alternative power sources for the site."
Unlike the U.K., the Nordics benefit from abundant power and available land. Countries in the region, like Finland, have seen major commitments to develop AI data centers this year. In September,Googlesaid it would invest at least13 billion euros ($15.1 billion) into AI infrastructurein the country, marking the tech giant's largest single investment in Europe.

OpenAI pitches data center power plants as a way to protect nearby areas
As public opinion has soured on data centers, it’s selling ‘AI campuses’ as protectors, instead of noisy polluters.
Image: The VergePart OfAll the latest updates on AI data centerssee all updatesEmma Roth
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.
Inan announcement on Monday, OpenAI says it will pilot its “Grid Protectors Program” at an upcoming data center in Effingham County, Georgia, where the company promises to free up to 1,000 megawatts of power during extreme weather or emergencies, enough to power air conditioners in around 700,000 homes.
The announcement comes asopposition to data centersspreads across the US, in response to massive projects that have begun development and construction, frequently with little or no input from local residents. In Utah,residents protestedafter Box Elder County commissioners signed off on a data center expected to consume more than double the state’s peak electricity demand in 2025, and spread hot air in the desert valley surrounding the data center.
Now OpenAI’s approach is to pitch the construction of power plants that feed the electricity required by the new AI data centers it’s building as “a resource that utilities can call on when communities need it most.”
Several stateslike Tennessee, Florida, Oklahoma, Oregon, and others have enacted laws that say they will prevent AI companies from passing energy costs on to residents, in addition tomoratoriumsand other restrictions. This is besides the environmental impacts, asa recent study by the Houston Advanced Research Center (HARC)said that powering proposed Texas data center projects could undo decades of air quality gains over just five years.
Anthropic is burning gas to feed the AI boom
Sam Altman says it’s better for RAM to be in a data center than on your desk
OpenAI, which has switched to calling itsAI data centers “compute campuses”in an effort to separate from theirpoor public reputation, claims it helps reduce costs for customers by operating year-round:
“Electricity demand also rises and falls with the seasons, with different regions facing their biggest peaks at different times,” OpenAI’s announcement says. “Our compute campuses need power year-round. With the right agreements, that steady demand can help spread the grid’s fixed costs across more electricity sales, while flexibility lets us reduce demand when the system is busiest.”
OpenAI says it’s going to continue working with policymakers and utility services to make “arrangements for our future campus to reduce electricity demand when the grid is under strain.” Along with its data center in Georgia, OpenAI is also partnering with Oracle and SoftBank to build its “Stargate” data centers across the US, including in Shackelford County, Texas; Doña Ana County, New Mexico; and Milam County, Texas.

Judge Says xAI Must Face NAACP Lawsuit On Data Center Pollution
Judge says xAI must face NAACP lawsuit on data center pollution
The legal battle revolves around the AI company’s operations in southern Memphis.
ByJackson ChenNov. 1, 2026 2:19 pm ESTharhar38/ShutterstockAdd Engadget on Google:Preferred SourceGoogle Discover
A federal judge'slatest rulinghas denied xAI's request to dismiss a lawsuit that alleges its data center campus in Memphis, Tennessee is running turbines without proper permits and violating the Clean Air Act. The decision, from US District Judge Debra M. Brown, allows the lawsuit, which was filed by the NAACP, to move forward.
The organization filed itslegal actionagainst xAI in April, accusing the company that's now known as SpaceXSI of using unpermitted methane gas turbines to power data centers in the Memphis area. Despite the ongoing lawsuit that also claimed it's violating the Clear Air Act, Elon Musk's company continued to add moregas turbinesto another AI data center site in the nearby Southhaven, Mississippi community. In response, xAI requested to dismiss the NAACP lawsuit and evenreceived supportfrom the Justice Department, which claimed that the company's operations are a crucial part of US military operations.
xAI said the lawsuit should be dismissed, claiming that its turbines were exempt from permitting requirements since they were mobile. Judge Brown wrote in her decision that the power plant where all the turbines were providing power to xAI's data center wasn't mobile and therefore not exempt from the permitting process. The lawsuit comes at a time when AI companies are ramping up the construction of data centers to fuel their AI needs, while neighbors are becomingincreasingly averseto these buildouts.

West Virginia and data centers: State faces new extractive industry : NPRAccessibility links
West Virginia and data centers: State faces new extractive industryResidents are fighting back against plans for a project that would span thousands of acres near the Monongahela National Forest and popular outdoor recreation, ski areas and dark sky sites.
Plans for a data center threaten scenic wilderness and dark skies in West Virginia
White Grass Ski Touring Center in Canaan Valley , W.Va., is celebrated for its unusually curvy and hilly cross-country skiing terrain.Chris Jackson for NPRhide caption
toggle captioniChris Jackson for NPR
DAVIS, W.Va. — Stretching nearly a million acres through the rugged mountains of eastern West Virginia, the Monongahela National Forest links some of the state's best known natural attractions. The vast area ranges from the ski slopes of Canaan Valley to the dark skies of Blackwater Falls and Spruce Knob and includes the small towns of Davis and Thomas that serve as gateways for visitors to the region.
Data centers are booming. But there are big energy and environmental risks
For the past seven months, Kaleb Skelton, his wife, Ella, their 2-year-old son, Ryder, and dog Mabel have lived in a camper in this corner of West Virginia's "almost heaven." Kaleb is finishing a seasonal stint as a campground manager on a lake near Spruce Knob, the state's highest point.
On clear nights atop the isolated peak, they get to experience a river of stars in one of thevery few pockets of darknessremaining in the Eastern United States. The area has become a draw for amateur astronomers.
Spruce Knob Lake Campground hosts Kaleb and Ella Skelton, at their site at Spruce Knob on Saturday, Oct. 10 2026 in Spruce Knob, W.Va. The couple from Texas have been at the site since April and said they have never seen darker skies than atop Spruce Knob.Chris Jackson for NPRhide caption
During summer's new moons, Kaleb says, one in four campsites he oversees is occupied by someone with a telescope. He thought his family's cabin in eastern Texas offered "the craziest" dark skies he'd ever seen, "but coming out here definitely rivals it."
Those inky-black nights — and the natural beauty they shelter — are now under threat from what many residents see as a modern-day version of extractive industries like logging and mining that once defined the region. In a place where tourism, outdoor recreation and community are deeply intertwined, a gigantic power plant and data center campus in nearby Tucker County would bring large-scale development into the heart of it all.
A stark image of the town of Davis from 1885, during the heyday of logging, is a reminder of that transformation. The photo shows a handful of squat buildings amid a broad clearing littered with forest remains.
They used to call it "Stump Town," says Kim Williams, president of the Snow Sports Museum of West Virginia in Canaan Valley. At the turn of the century, massive first-growth trees dominated the landscape.
Then, logging companies "came in and clear-cut the whole valley and everything around it," he says.
West Virginia paid digital nomads to move there during COVID. Many are staying
By the early 20th century, entire mountainsides of red spruce and eastern hemlock had been stripped bare. Then came the coal companies, which left the nearby Blackwater River acidic and dangerous to drink.
Today, the scars still show. The big trees won't return for generations, but a century of natural regrowth, conservation and deliberate restorationmeans the land is on its way to healing.
While few expect that the latest tech boom presages anything like the environmental destruction of the past, many see the proposed new Ridgeline data center as a big step backward, undoing the progress the local community has made to recover.
A roughly 785-megawatt generating plant is slated to be the first part of "a large-scale data and energy infrastructure project designed to support artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and enterprise systems," according toPurcellville, Va.-based Fundamental Data LLC, the company behind Ridgeline.
The photo "The Birth of a city, Davis, W. Va. in 1885" by William Henry Jackson shows a handful of squat buildings amid a broad clearing littered with forest remains.hide caption
The complex would rely primarily on natural gas, with diesel as a backup fuel source. Power generated on-site, rather than purchased from the regional grid, could ease some concerns about the project's effects on electricity rates. It does not, however, resolve concerns over air and water pollution.
Located on a reclaimed coal-mining site, plans are for an initial 291 acres thatcould eventually expand to 10,000 acres— 15 square miles — andinclude parts of neighboring Grant County, according to local news reports.
Speaking to NPR, Casey Chapman, listed in court documents as Fundamental Data's "responsible individual," declined to speculate on the facility's ultimate size, saying only that "if fully developed … it would be thousands of acres."
The data center backlash is reshaping American politics — one community at a time
Light pollution is acommon complaintfrom residents living near data centers. Chapman says the company will use "well-designed" lighting to help minimize the effects of sky glow, in an effort not to jeopardize nearby Blackwater Falls State Park's pursuit ofan official dark-sky certification.
Ananalysisby the Northern Virginia Astronomy Club, which hosts an annual star party in the region, found that Ridgeline's initial footprint could increase sky glow near Blackwater by 528%, transforming its nighttime rural sky to one comparable to a suburban area. (The same analysis found only a minimal impact on Spruce Knob.)
But safety and security — not light pollution — take precedence, Chapman says. The facility will be "an industrial plant that runs around the clock," he notes. "Crews need proper lighting to operate and maintain equipment safely."
Chip Chase is among the skeptics. He runs White Grass Ski Touring Center, a popular cross-country ski area that he helped found 45 years ago. He is a fixture in the local community that he describes as "Vermont, with Southern hospitality."
"If you're an outdoor person, this place is paradise," he says. "People come here to get away from data centers. People want dark skies here. People want to have a peaceful, quiet recreational area."

fact_units.text: Brookfield plans $27 billion AI data center at power station; Drax rises 8%Skip Navigation
Brookfield is planning a data center with more than one gigawatt of capacity at a site in England.
The asset manager estimated that the potential investment for the project could exceed £20 billion ($26.8 billion).
Drax Group, which operates the power station the facility will be housed at, saw shares rise more than 8% on Tuesday morning.

Brookfieldis targeting a massive artificial intelligence data center in the north of England, as Europe scrambles to develop infrastructure to support the rollout of AI amid high energy and land costs.

Energy companyDrax Groupsaid Tuesday it has signed an agreement with Brookfield and the asset manager's neocloud platform Radiant to jointly develop an AI data center on the Drax Power Station estate in North Yorkshire.
London-listed shares of Drax were up 8.8% in early morning trading.
The project is initially targeting up to 100 megawatts of capacity to be operational from the first quarter of 2028, with an additional 500 MW of capacity to be brought online between 2028 and 2031.
It is then looking to secure more than 1 gigawatt of capacity at the site by an unspecified date.
Brookfield estimates total investment, including semiconductors, could exceed £20 billion ($26.8 billion), with an initial £2.5 billion investment in phase 1.
"This is a unique opportunity for the UK's AI ecosystem to build at scale," Radiant CEO Mahdi Yahya said in a statement.
"By designing, building and operating from the UK, it will give British researchers, startups and enterprises access to frontier compute at home."
The first phase of Brookfield's project in North Yorkshire will use power from the grid and target commercial customers from early 2028.
The initial phase is subject to planning, regulatory and network approvals from the government and relevant agencies, alongside securing a tenant for the project, Drax said in a statement said.
The company added that final investment decisions are yet to be made.
has surged ahead on developing the huge data centers needed to power AI, Europe has been slower to break ground on the facilities.
in particular has struggled withhigh energy costsand challenges with long waiting times for businesses to connect to the grid.
In October, it wasreportedthat Microsoft had pulled out of a deal to anchor an Nscale data center just outside London, amid delays connecting to the country's power grid.
An Nscale spokesperson told CNBC at the time that it remained "committed" to the project and was "exploring alternative power sources for the site."
Unlike the U.K., the Nordics benefit from abundant power and available land.
Countries in the region, like Finland, have seen major commitments to develop AI data centers this year.
In September,Googlesaid it would invest at least13 billion euros ($15.1 billion) into AI infrastructurein the country, marking the tech giant's largest single investment in Europe.

OpenAI pitches data center power plants as a way to protect nearby areas
As public opinion has soured on data centers, it’s selling ‘AI campuses’ as protectors, instead of noisy polluters.
Image: The VergePart OfAll the latest updates on AI data centerssee all updatesEmma Roth
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more.
Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

Inan announcement on Monday, OpenAI says it will pilot its “Grid Protectors Program” at an upcoming data center in Effingham County, Georgia, where the company promises to free up to 1,000 megawatts of power during extreme weather or emergencies, enough to power air conditioners in around 700,000 homes.

The announcement comes asopposition to data centersspreads across the US, in response to massive projects that have begun development and construction, frequently with little or no input from local residents.

In Utah,residents protestedafter Box Elder County commissioners signed off on a data center expected to consume more than double the state’s peak electricity demand in 2025, and spread hot air in the desert valley surrounding the data center.

Now OpenAI’s approach is to pitch the construction of power plants that feed the electricity required by the new AI data centers it’s building as “a resource that utilities can call on when communities need it most.”

Several stateslike Tennessee, Florida, Oklahoma, Oregon, and others have enacted laws that say they will prevent AI companies from passing energy costs on to residents, in addition tomoratoriumsand other restrictions.

This is besides the environmental impacts, asa recent study by the Houston Advanced Research Center (HARC)said that powering proposed Texas data center projects could undo decades of air quality gains over just five years.
Anthropic is burning gas to feed the AI boom
Sam Altman says it’s better for RAM to be in a data center than on your desk

OpenAI, which has switched to calling itsAI data centers “compute campuses”in an effort to separate from theirpoor public reputation, claims it helps reduce costs for customers by operating year-round:
“Electricity demand also rises and falls with the seasons, with different regions facing their biggest peaks at different times,” OpenAI’s announcement says.
With the right agreements, that steady demand can help spread the grid’s fixed costs across more electricity sales, while flexibility lets us reduce demand when the system is busiest.”

Công an vào cuộc vụ nữ tài xế ô tô chèn ép, tông đổ xe máy của phụ nữ mang thai
Công an phường Lào Cai (tỉnh Lào Cai) đang làm rõ phản ánh nữ tài xế xe VF 3 liên tục chèn ép một phụ nữ đi xe máy điện, sau đó còn tông đổ xe khi người này đang dừng chờ đèn đỏ.
Tài xế ô tô tông đổ xe máy của người phụ nữ mang bầu khi đang dừng chờ đèn đỏ - Ảnh cắt từ clip
Trao đổi vớiTuổi Trẻtrưa 3-11, một lãnh đạo UBND phường Lào Cai (tỉnh Lào Cai) cho biết đơn vị đã giao công an phường mời các bên liên quan đến để làm rõ phản ánh nữ tài xếxe VF 3liên tục chèn ép một phụ nữ đi xe máy, sau đó còn tông đổ xe khi người này đang dừng chờ đèn đỏ.
Tài xế ô tô có phải chịu trách nhiệm với tai nạn khi người đi bộ bất ngờ băng qua cao tốc?ĐỌC NGAY
Trước đó ngày 2-11, trên mạng xã hội chia sẻ đoạn clip do camera an ninh ghi lại cảnh một tài xế xe VF 3 liên tục có hành vi chèn ép người phụ nữ đi xe máy khiến người này phải đi lên khu vực vỉa hè.
Sau đó, người phụ nữ đi xe máy lao lên vỉa hè rồi di chuyển tiếp.
Tuy nhiên, người lái ô tô VF 3 tiếp tục đuổi theo và đâm thẳng vào đuôi xe máy khi đang dừng chờ đèn đỏ, khiến chiếc xe đổ xuống đường.
Bực tức vì bị tông trúng, người lái xe máy lao tới kéo cửa ô tô bên ghế phụ. Một nam thanh niên ngồi ghế phụ lao ra định hành hung người đi xe máy. Sau đó, nữtài xế ô tôcũng lao ra khỏi xe và xô đẩy người đi xe máy.
Sự việc chỉ dừng lại khi có một người đàn ông lao vào căn ngăn. Nữ tài xế ô tô sau đó đã lái xe rời khỏi hiện trường.
Trao đổi thêm vớiTuổi Trẻ,anh Mai Văn Chương (38 tuổi, ở phường Cam Đường) cho biết người phụ nữ đi xe máy trong đoạn clip là vợ anh và đang mang bầu 6 tháng.
Theo anh Chương, khoảng 14h50 ngày 1-11, vợ anh là chị P.T.T. (36 tuổi) đang đi xe máy trên đường Hoàng Liên thì suýt xảy ra va quẹt với xe VF 3 vì chiếc xe này không xi nhan khi đi từ vị trí đỗ xe ven đường ra phần đường chính.
Anh Chương cho biết sau đó vợ anh có nhìn lái xe VF 3 rồi đi tiếp. Tuy nhiên, chiếc xe VF 3 bất ngờ đi lên và ép vợ anh vào lề đường.
"Giữa vợ tôi và nữ lái xe VF 3 có nói qua nói lại, xong tài xế ô tô tiếp tục chèn ép vợ tôi vào lề đường, vợ tôi phải đi lên vỉa hè để đi tiếp. Khi vợ tôi dừng chờ đèn đỏ thì tài xế xe VF 3 bất ngờ tông từ phía sau khiến chiếc xe đổ ra đường" - anh Chương chia sẻ.
Cũng theo anh Chương, sau sự việc, vợ anh vào viện điều trị, truyền thuốc liên tục vì có nguy cơ bị sinh non.
"Hôm qua, tôi đã lên công an phường để trình báo. Tôi mong cơ quan chức năng xác minh khách quan, làm rõ hành vi của tài xế ô tô và xử lý đúng quy định pháp luật" - anh Chương nói.
Khởi tố tài xế xe tải không chú ý quan sát, gây tai nạn khiến 2 người chết
Hồ Sỹ Trung trong quá trình điều khiển xe tải do không chú ý quan sát, không làm chủ tốc độ nên đã xảy ra va chạm với chiếc xe máy chở 3 thanh niên. Vụ việc khiến 2 người chết, 1 người bị thương.

Nguồn: BV Phương Nam03/11/2026 14:43 GMT+7Chia sẻChọn BáoThanh Niênlàmnguồn ưu tiêntrên Google tìm kiếm.Xem hướng dẫn.BƯỚC1Nhấp vào nút"ThêmThanh Niêntrên Google"hoặc mở trực tiếp đường dẫn này:https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thanhnien.vnBƯỚC2Tại trang vừa mở, tìm dòng"BáoThanh Niên"và bấm vào ô vuông bên phải.Khi ô vuông chuyển thành dấu tích xanh là bạn đã thành công rồi!LƯU Ý NHỎ:Nếu muốn kiểm tra xem cài đặt còn hiệu lực không, bạn chỉ cầnmở lại link trênlà thấy ngaydấu tích xanhvẫn đang hiển thị.Chúc bạn đọc báo vui vẻ!
Mang thai ở tuần 36, sản phụ H.T bất ngờ chuyển dạ, vỡ ối trong tình trạng thai ngôi mông và có nhiều khối u xơ tử cung. Trong cuộc mổ lấy thai, các bác sĩ không chỉ đón bé gái chào đời an toàn mà còn bóc tách trọn 3 khối u xơ kích thước lớn.
Combo u xơ tử cung, thai ở ngôi mông, vỡ ối sớm
Niềm vui mang thai lần đầu của chị T. xen lẫn nỗi lo khi kết quả siêu âm cho thấy chị có u xơ tử cung. Đây là tình trạng cần được theo dõi trong thai kỳ, đặc biệt khi các khối u có kích thước lớn hoặc nằm ở những vị trí có thể ảnh hưởng đến quá trình mang thai và sinh nở.
Khi thai kỳ ở 36 tuần 5 ngày, chị T. bất ngờ xuất hiện dấu hiệu chuyển dạ và vỡ ối. Đáng chú ý, thai nhi vẫn ở ngôi mông, tức phần mông hoặc chân của em bé hướng xuống phía dưới tử cung thay vì đầu như thường gặp. Sản phụ được đưa đếnBệnh viện Phương Nam, TP.HCM (Thành viên Tập đoàn Y tế Phương Châu) trong tình trạng ối đã vỡ khoảng 2 giờ, kèm theo nhiều yếu tố cần lưu ý.
Ngoài ra, hồ sơ bệnh án còn ghi nhận sản phụ đang được theo dõi block nhánh phải không hoàn toàn, một bất thường về dẫn truyền điện trong tim. Về phía thai nhi, kết quả thăm khám trước đó cũng ghi nhận yếu tố cần theo dõi liên quan đến chiều dài xương đùi. Trước tình trạng trên, các bác sĩ quyết định phẫu thuật lấy thai.
Bác sĩ chuyên khoa 2 Văn Phụng Thống, Giám đốc chuyên môn bệnh viện Phương Nam, cùng ê-kíp tiến hành ca phẫu thuật. Sau khi mở bụng theo đường ngang trên xương vệ và tiếp cận đoạn dưới tử cung, các bác sĩ đưa một bé gái ra ngoài bằng phương pháp lấy thai ngôi mông. Sau khi lấy thai, ê-kíp tiếp tục kiểm tra buồng tử cung và các cấu trúc liên quan.
Vì sao bác sĩ quyết định bóc tách u xơ trong cùng cuộc mổ lấy thai?
Tuy nhiên, khi kiểm tra tử cung sau bóc nhau, ê-kíp phát hiện 3 khối u xơ kích thước lớn làm biến dạng tử cung: một khối nằm dưới thanh mạc mặt trước, khối thứ hai ở đáy tử cung và khối thứ ba ở mặt sau.
Khối u được các bác sĩ nhẹ nhàng bóc tách
Việc bóc u xơ tử cung trong lúc mổ lấy thai vốn là thách thức lớn do tử cung mang thai chứa lượng máu rất dồi dào, dễ gây mất máu ồ ạt. Tuy nhiên, với trường hợp chị T. nếu không xử lý, 3 khối u kích thước lớn sẽ cản trở sự co hồi tử cung hậu phẫu, gây bế sản dịch, đờ tử cung và dẫn đến nguy cơ nhiễm trùng hoặc chảy máu muộn. Hơn nữa, việc loại bỏ u xơ ngay trong cuộc mổ giúp người bệnh tránh được một cuộc phẫu thuật can thiệp thứ hai trong tương lai.
Dưới sự phối hợp chặt chẽ giữa ê-kíp Sản khoa và Gây mê hồi sức, các bác sĩ đã quyết định bóc tách trọn vẹn cả 3 khối u xơ và khâu phục hồi cơ tử cung. Quá trình phẫu thuật kiểm soát cầm máu tốt, tổng lượng máu mất chỉ khoảng 450 ml và bệnh nhân không cần truyền thêm máu.
Phục hồi nhanh sau phẫu thuật, sẵn sàng đồng hành cùng con
Sau cuộc mổ "kép", chị T. cùng em bé tiếp tục được theo dõi và chăm sóc hậu phẫu chuyên sâu tại Bệnh viện Phương Nam. Trong khi bé gái được bác sĩ Nhi - Sơ sinh kiểm tra sức khỏe tổng quát và đánh giá sát chỉ số phát triển xương đùi, chị T. được kiểm tra liên tục tình trạng tim mạch, lượng sản dịch cũng như mức độ co hồi tử cung.
Nhờ quy trình phẫu thuật chuẩn xác cùng sự chăm sóc tích cực từ ê-kíp y tế, sản phụ phục hồi nhanh chóng, vết mổ khô tốt và có thể vận động nhẹ nhàng từ sớm. Cả hai mẹ con đủ điều kiện xuất viện an toàn trong niềm hạnh phúc trọn vẹn của gia đình.
Đối với phụ nữ mang thai có u xơ tử cung, bác sĩ nhấn mạnh việc khám thai định kỳ giúp bác sĩ theo dõi sự thay đổi của khối u, đánh giá ngôi thai và xây dựng phương án sinh phù hợp.
Đặc biệt, khi xuất hiện các dấu hiệu như ra nước âm đạo nghi vỡ ối, đau bụng từng cơn, ra máu bất thường hoặc thai máy giảm, thai phụ cần đến cơ sở y tế để được kiểm tra kịp thời.
Là thành viên của Tập đoàn Y tế Phương Châu - hệ thống y tế đầu tiên tại Việt Nam đạt chuẩn JCI Enterprise, Bệnh viện Phương Nam kế thừa nền tảng quản lý an toàn và chất lượng điều trị theo chuẩn quốc tế, không chỉ chú trọng điều trị hiệu quả mà còn hướng đến các can thiệp tối ưu nhằm bảo tồn chức năng sinh sản và nâng cao chất lượng cuộc sống.

Công an vào cuộc vụ nữ tài xế ô tô chèn ép, tông đổ xe máy của phụ nữ mang thai
Công an phường Lào Cai (tỉnh Lào Cai) đang làm rõ phản ánh nữ tài xế xe VF 3 liên tục chèn ép một phụ nữ đi xe máy điện, sau đó còn tông đổ xe khi người này đang dừng chờ đèn đỏ.
Tài xế ô tô tông đổ xe máy của người phụ nữ mang bầu khi đang dừng chờ đèn đỏ - Ảnh cắt từ clip

Trao đổi vớiTuổi Trẻtrưa 3-11, một lãnh đạo UBND phường Lào Cai (tỉnh Lào Cai) cho biết đơn vị đã giao công an phường mời các bên liên quan đến để làm rõ phản ánh nữ tài xếxe VF 3liên tục chèn ép một phụ nữ đi xe máy, sau đó còn tông đổ xe khi người này đang dừng chờ đèn đỏ.
Tài xế ô tô có phải chịu trách nhiệm với tai nạn khi người đi bộ bất ngờ băng qua cao tốc?ĐỌC NGAY
Trước đó ngày 2-11, trên mạng xã hội chia sẻ đoạn clip do camera an ninh ghi lại cảnh một tài xế xe VF 3 liên tục có hành vi chèn ép người phụ nữ đi xe máy khiến người này phải đi lên khu vực vỉa hè.
Sau đó, người phụ nữ đi xe máy lao lên vỉa hè rồi di chuyển tiếp.
Tuy nhiên, người lái ô tô VF 3 tiếp tục đuổi theo và đâm thẳng vào đuôi xe máy khi đang dừng chờ đèn đỏ, khiến chiếc xe đổ xuống đường.
Bực tức vì bị tông trúng, người lái xe máy lao tới kéo cửa ô tô bên ghế phụ.
Một nam thanh niên ngồi ghế phụ lao ra định hành hung người đi xe máy.
Sau đó, nữtài xế ô tôcũng lao ra khỏi xe và xô đẩy người đi xe máy.
Sự việc chỉ dừng lại khi có một người đàn ông lao vào căn ngăn.
Nữ tài xế ô tô sau đó đã lái xe rời khỏi hiện trường.
Trao đổi thêm vớiTuổi Trẻ,anh Mai Văn Chương (38 tuổi, ở phường Cam Đường) cho biết người phụ nữ đi xe máy trong đoạn clip là vợ anh và đang mang bầu 6 tháng.
Theo anh Chương, khoảng 14h50 ngày 1-11, vợ anh là chị P.T.T.
(36 tuổi) đang đi xe máy trên đường Hoàng Liên thì suýt xảy ra va quẹt với xe VF 3 vì chiếc xe này không xi nhan khi đi từ vị trí đỗ xe ven đường ra phần đường chính.
Anh Chương cho biết sau đó vợ anh có nhìn lái xe VF 3 rồi đi tiếp.
Tuy nhiên, chiếc xe VF 3 bất ngờ đi lên và ép vợ anh vào lề đường.
"Giữa vợ tôi và nữ lái xe VF 3 có nói qua nói lại, xong tài xế ô tô tiếp tục chèn ép vợ tôi vào lề đường, vợ tôi phải đi lên vỉa hè để đi tiếp.
Khi vợ tôi dừng chờ đèn đỏ thì tài xế xe VF 3 bất ngờ tông từ phía sau khiến chiếc xe đổ ra đường" - anh Chương chia sẻ.
Cũng theo anh Chương, sau sự việc, vợ anh vào viện điều trị, truyền thuốc liên tục vì có nguy cơ bị sinh non.
"Hôm qua, tôi đã lên công an phường để trình báo.
Tôi mong cơ quan chức năng xác minh khách quan, làm rõ hành vi của tài xế ô tô và xử lý đúng quy định pháp luật" - anh Chương nói.
Khởi tố tài xế xe tải không chú ý quan sát, gây tai nạn khiến 2 người chết
Hồ Sỹ Trung trong quá trình điều khiển xe tải do không chú ý quan sát, không làm chủ tốc độ nên đã xảy ra va chạm với chiếc xe máy chở 3 thanh niên.
Vụ việc khiến 2 người chết, 1 người bị thương.

Việt Nam chính thức có bản quyền phát sóng FIFA U17 World Cup 2026
Ngày 3-11, TV360, FPT Play và MyTV công bố bản quyền phát sóng giải đấu, mang đến cho người hâm mộ Việt Nam cơ hội theo dõi hành trình của các tài năng bóng đá trẻ thế giới tại FIFA U17 World Cup 2026.
Việt Nam đã có bản quyền FIFA U17 World Cup 2026 - Ảnh: AFC
FIFA U17 World Cup 2026diễn ra từ ngày 19-11 đến 13-12 tại Qatar, quy tụ 48 đội tuyển, trong đó có U17 Việt Nam.
U17 Việt Nam tập tại Hàn Quốc, chuẩn bị cho World Cup
U17 Việt Nam có mặt tại Hàn Quốc, sẵn sàng cho chiến dịch tiền World Cup trẻ
U17 Việt Nam dự kiến giao hữu 5 trận trước World Cup trẻ
Đây là sân chơi dành cho các đội tuyển U17 xuất sắc nhất thế giới, nơi những cầu thủ trẻ có cơ hội thể hiện tài năng, rèn giũa bản lĩnh thi đấu trên con đường trở thành cầu thủ chuyên nghiệp.
"Với mong muốn đưa giải đấu tiếp cận với đông đảo khán giả, MyTV, FPT Play và TV360 đã cùng trở thành 3 đơn vị dịch vụ truyền hình sẽ phát sóng trọn vẹn VCK FIFA U17 World Cup 2026 tại lãnh thổ Việt Nam.
Khán giả trong nước có thể theo dõi giải đấu trên các nền tảng của ba đơn vị, bao gồm các trận đấu của đội tuyển U17 Việt Nam tại vòng bảng" - thông cáo ba đơn vị phát sóng có đoạn.
FIFA U17 World Cup 2026 trở nên đáng chú ý hơn khi có sự góp mặt của U17 Việt Nam. Lần đầu tiên trong lịch sử, U17 Việt Nam giành quyền góp mặt ở sân chơi danh giá này. Được đối đầu với những đội tuyển đến từ nhiều châu lục được xem là cơ hội để các cầu thủ trẻ Việt Nam thử sức ở môi trường thi đấu đỉnh cao của bóng đá trẻ.
Tại FIFA U17 World Cup 2026, U17 Việt Nam ở bảng G cùng Bỉ, New Zealand và Mali. Theo lịch thi đấu, U17 Việt Nam sẽ lần lượt gặp Bỉ (20-11), New Zealand (23-11) và Mali (26-11).
FIFA U17 World Cup 2026 được chia làm 12 bảng. Sau khi kết thúc vòng bảng, 24 đội nhất nhì mỗi bảng và 8 đội đứng thứ 3 có thành tích tốt nhất sẽ giành vé đi tiếp. Bồ Đào Nha hiện là đương kim vô địch của giải.
Sáng 21-10, U17 Việt Nam nhận thất bại 1-4 trước U18 FC Seoul, trong trận đấu tập đầu tiên của chuyến tập huấn ở Hàn Quốc.

Việt Nam ra mắt chip bảo mật đầu tiên do trong nước làm chủ thiết kế
(Dân trí) - Chip bảo mật VGC v1.0 do Ban Cơ yếu Chính phủ và Viettel phối hợp phát triển có 300 triệu bóng bán dẫn, sản xuất trên tiến trình 28nm, tốc độ mã hóa, giải mã nhanh gấp 15 lần giải pháp thuần phần mềm.
Chiều 3/11, Ban Cơ yếu Chính phủ và Tập đoàn Công nghiệp - Viễn thông Quân đội (Viettel) công bố chip bảo mật VGC v1.0 cùng nền tảng bán dẫn bảo mật do Việt Nam làm chủ thiết kế.
Sự kiện diễn ra tại Hà Nội, với sự tham dự của Đại tướng Phan Văn Giang, Ủy viên Bộ Chính trị, Phó Thủ tướng Chính phủ, Bộ trưởng Bộ Quốc phòng, cùng lãnh đạo các bộ, ngành và cơ quan liên quan.
Đại tướng Phan Văn Giang, Ủy viên Bộ Chính trị, Phó Thủ tướng Chính phủ, Bộ trưởng Bộ Quốc phòng, cùng các khách mời tham quan khu vực triển lãm (Ảnh: Bảo Trung).
VGC v1.0 tích hợp trực tiếp thuật toán mật mã Việt Nam vào phần cứng
VGC v1.0 là sản phẩm đầu tiên trong nền tảng bán dẫn bảo mật do hai đơn vị phối hợp phát triển. Theo công bố, chip có kích thước đóng gói 10 x 10mm, chứa khoảng 300 triệu bóng bán dẫn (transistor), được chế tạo trên tiến trình CMOS 28nm.
Kết quả đo kiểm cho thấy chip có tốc độ mã hóa, giải mã nhanh gấp khoảng 15 lần so với giải pháp thuần phần mềm khi thực hiện cùng tác vụ. Ngoài hiệu năng xử lý, nhóm phát triển cũng áp dụng các biện pháp kỹ thuật nhằm bảo vệ bản thiết kế trước khi chuyển tới nhà máy chế tạo, hạn chế nguy cơ lộ lọt hoặc dịch ngược.
Theo Ban Cơ yếu Chính phủ và Viettel, điểm đáng chú ý của VGC v1.0 là việc tích hợp trực tiếp thuật toán mật mã Việt Nam vào phần cứng. Đây là hướng tiếp cận nhằm tăng cường khả năng bảo vệ dữ liệu, thay vì chỉ dựa vào các giải pháp mã hóa trên phần mềm.
Trong quá trình phát triển, Ban Cơ yếu Chính phủ đảm nhiệm việc xác định yêu cầu bảo mật, xây dựng thuật toán và tiêu chí đánh giá. Trung tâm Bán dẫn Viettel phụ trách thiết kế vi mạch và hiện thực hóa bản thiết kế thành chip.
Lô chip VGC v1.0 đầu tiên đã vượt qua các hạng mục đo kiểm kỹ thuật trong quý I/2026 và được cấp giấy chứng nhận với phạm vi sử dụng trong lĩnh vực kinh tế - xã hội.
Trên thế giới, một số hãng công nghệ đã tích hợp phần cứng bảo mật chuyên dụng vào thiết bị, chẳng hạn Titan M trên một số điện thoại Pixel của Google hay Secure Enclave trên các nền tảng của Apple. Những bộ phận này hỗ trợ xử lý các tác vụ bảo mật và bảo vệ dữ liệu trên thiết bị.
Hướng tới ứng dụng trong chữ ký số và hạ tầng trọng yếu
VGC v1.0 bước đầu được ứng dụng trong USB lưu trữ an toàn dành cho các cơ quan Đảng, Nhà nước và Quốc phòng. Các đơn vị phát triển dự kiến tiếp tục đưa chip vào hệ thống chứng thực chữ ký số quốc gia, hiện có hơn 2 triệu chứng thư số đang lưu hành.
Chip bảo mật VGC v1.0 (Ảnh: Viettel).
Ngoài lĩnh vực quốc phòng, an ninh, chip có tiềm năng ứng dụng trong bảo vệ hồ sơ, hợp đồng và dữ liệu khách hàng của các tổ chức tài chính, ngân hàng; bảo đảm an toàn cho camera giám sát, cảm biến môi trường, trạm quan trắc và các hệ thống thông tin thuộc hạ tầng trọng yếu như điện, nước, dầu khí, viễn thông.
Trung tướng Vũ Ngọc Thiềm, Trưởng Ban Cơ yếu Chính phủ, cho biết VGC v1.0 mới là bước khởi đầu. Các sản phẩm phục vụ bảo vệ bí mật nhà nước phải đáp ứng đầy đủ tiêu chuẩn và điều kiện theo quy định.
Theo ông Thiềm, năng lực công nghệ chỉ thực sự có ý nghĩa khi được kiểm chứng bằng độ an toàn, độ tin cậy và hiệu quả trong thực tiễn.
Phát biểu tại sự kiện, Đại tướng Phan Văn Giang nhấn mạnh chip bán dẫn đã trở thành tài nguyên chiến lược, trong khi mật mã là công cụ cốt lõi để bảo vệ thông tin và dữ liệu.
"Làm chủ nền tảng bán dẫn bảo mật không chỉ là nhiệm vụ khoa học công nghệ mà là nhiệm vụ chính trị, nội dung thiết thực bảo vệ chủ quyền quốc gia trên không gian mạng, bảo vệ Tổ quốc từ sớm, từ xa", Đại tướng Phan Văn Giang nói.
Phát triển nền tảng cho các thế hệ chip tiếp theo
Bên cạnh VGC v1.0, hai đơn vị cũng công bố nền tảng bán dẫn bảo mật dựa trên kiến trúc tập lệnh mở RISC-V. Nền tảng này cho phép đội ngũ kỹ sư chủ động điều chỉnh thiết kế bộ xử lý, làm chủ kiến trúc và quy trình kiểm chứng, tạo cơ sở phát triển các dòng chip tiếp theo.
Trung tướng Tào Đức Thắng, Ủy viên BCH Trung ương Đảng, Chủ tịch kiêm Tổng Giám đốc Viettel, cho biết nghiên cứu, thiết kế và phát triển chip bán dẫn bảo mật là lĩnh vực khó, đòi hỏi quá trình tích lũy lâu dài về tri thức, công nghệ và nhân lực chất lượng cao.
Theo ông Thắng, nếu có chiến lược phù hợp, tập trung nguồn lực và kiên trì theo đuổi mục tiêu, Việt Nam có thể từng bước rút ngắn khoảng cách, tiến tới làm chủ các công nghệ chiến lược.
Lễ ký kết giữa Ban cơ yếu Chính phủ và tập đoàn Viettel về sản xuất, phát triển vi mạch, phát triển nguồn nhân lực (Ảnh: Viettel).
Trong khuôn khổ sự kiện, Ban Cơ yếu Chính phủ và Viettel ký thỏa thuận hợp tác với 4 nội dung chính, gồm đưa VGC v1.0 vào sản xuất hàng loạt; phát triển nền tảng vi mạch bảo mật đa lõi; đào tạo nhân lực chuyên sâu về thiết kế vi mạch, mật mã và an toàn phần cứng; thử nghiệm, kiểm định và đánh giá sản phẩm trên thiết bị thực tế trước khi đưa vào sử dụng.
Cùng với dự án nhà máy chế tạo chip bán dẫn công nghệ cao tại Hòa Lạc do Viettel triển khai, việc phát triển nền tảng bán dẫn bảo mật được kỳ vọng góp phần nâng cao năng lực thiết kế và sản xuất chip trong nước, giảm phụ thuộc vào công nghệ bên ngoài.
FPT đưa nhà máy công suất 300 triệu chip/năm vào vận hành thử nghiệm
Nhà máy kiểm thử và đóng gói chip bán dẫn của FPT tại Bắc Ninh bắt đầu vận hành thử nghiệm với 6 dây chuyền, công suất thiết kế tối đa 300 triệu chip mỗi năm.
Giá smartphone có thể tiếp tục tăng cao
Nhiều dự báo cho rằng tình trạng khan hiếm nguồn cung chip nhớ có thể kéo dài đến năm 2030. Điều này ảnh hưởng tiêu cực đến nhiều ngành hàng như smartphone, máy tính, máy chơi game.
Cơn khát chip nhớ đang thay đổi thị trường di động tại Việt Nam
Tình trạng thiếu hụt chip nhớ trên phạm vi toàn cầu đang tạo ra những tác động sâu rộng, làm thay đổi thị trường điện thoại thông minh.
Thiết kế chip do người Việt phát triển được quan tâm trên thị trường
CT Group tổ chức chuỗi sự kiện tiến đến Kỷ niệm 33 năm thành lập tập đoàn (29/6/1992 – 29/6/2025) và tổng kết kế hoạch 3 năm lần thứ nhất (vòng 30 năm lần 2), cùng nhiều kế hoạch, sự kiện trong 6 tháng cuối năm.

fact_units.text: Việt Nam chính thức có bản quyền phát sóng FIFA U17 World Cup 2026 - Tuổi Trẻ OnlineBỏ qua đến nội dung chính
Đăng ký Tuổi Trẻ SaoVào trang Tuổi Trẻ Sao
Việt Nam chính thức có bản quyền phát sóng FIFA U17 World Cup 2026

Ngày 3-11, TV360, FPT Play và MyTV công bố bản quyền phát sóng giải đấu, mang đến cho người hâm mộ Việt Nam cơ hội theo dõi hành trình của các tài năng bóng đá trẻ thế giới tại FIFA U17 World Cup 2026.
Việt Nam đã có bản quyền FIFA U17 World Cup 2026 - Ảnh: AFC
FIFA U17 World Cup 2026diễn ra từ ngày 19-11 đến 13-12 tại Qatar, quy tụ 48 đội tuyển, trong đó có U17 Việt Nam.
U17 Việt Nam tập tại Hàn Quốc, chuẩn bị cho World Cup
U17 Việt Nam có mặt tại Hàn Quốc, sẵn sàng cho chiến dịch tiền World Cup trẻ
U17 Việt Nam dự kiến giao hữu 5 trận trước World Cup trẻ
Đây là sân chơi dành cho các đội tuyển U17 xuất sắc nhất thế giới, nơi những cầu thủ trẻ có cơ hội thể hiện tài năng, rèn giũa bản lĩnh thi đấu trên con đường trở thành cầu thủ chuyên nghiệp.

"Với mong muốn đưa giải đấu tiếp cận với đông đảo khán giả, MyTV, FPT Play và TV360 đã cùng trở thành 3 đơn vị dịch vụ truyền hình sẽ phát sóng trọn vẹn VCK FIFA U17 World Cup 2026 tại lãnh thổ Việt Nam.
Khán giả trong nước có thể theo dõi giải đấu trên các nền tảng của ba đơn vị, bao gồm các trận đấu của đội tuyển U17 Việt Nam tại vòng bảng" - thông cáo ba đơn vị phát sóng có đoạn.
FIFA U17 World Cup 2026 trở nên đáng chú ý hơn khi có sự góp mặt của U17 Việt Nam.
Lần đầu tiên trong lịch sử, U17 Việt Nam giành quyền góp mặt ở sân chơi danh giá này.
Được đối đầu với những đội tuyển đến từ nhiều châu lục được xem là cơ hội để các cầu thủ trẻ Việt Nam thử sức ở môi trường thi đấu đỉnh cao của bóng đá trẻ.
Tại FIFA U17 World Cup 2026, U17 Việt Nam ở bảng G cùng Bỉ, New Zealand và Mali.
Theo lịch thi đấu, U17 Việt Nam sẽ lần lượt gặp Bỉ (20-11), New Zealand (23-11) và Mali (26-11).

Florida plane crash investigators say jet may have broken apart before impact as family named - BBC News
Dashcam footage captures Florida private jet crash
ByNardine Saad,Kathryn ArmstrongandRachel Flynn
Investigators believe parts of a private jet which crashed in Florida and killed all nine on board may have broken off in the air.
The Learjet 60 was bound for the Bahamas from Austin, Texaswhen it nosedivedinto a multi-lane highway and exploded on impact.
A tech entrepreneur and his young family, as well as the 20-year-old copilot, were among those who died on Sunday.
The US National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) said weather conditions would be a major focus of the investigation, but that it was struggling to access the wreckage due to a huge crater on the road which was formed by the jet in Palm Beach.
The plane crashed on Military Trail, a six-lane road that features businesses and restaurants, at around 12:50 local time.
"The biggest obstacle that we're going to have is recovering the major wreckage from the impacted crater on the roadway," lead investigator Tim Monville said at a news conference on Monday.
The NTSB said the crater, near the entrance to a mobile home park, was partially filled with water because of severe storms. Heavy rainfall and thunderstorms had been reported in the area at the time of the crash.
Debris was scattered across sports fields, businesses and homes in the area.
"We do have some evidence that there was some breakup of the aircraft before impact," the NTSB's Tom Chapman said.
"We may find parts of the aircraft some distance away from the actual impact site."
Officials are also trying to find out whether a cockpit voice recorder was on board at the time of the crash and if it can be recovered.
Flight analysis indicates that the jet was plummeting hundreds of feet per second before crashing.
In air traffic control audio recordings, someone in the cockpit can be heard reporting "moderate turbulence" and that the crew was "managing the ice".
They can then be heard saying the plane was "picking up precipitation" and "we need to climb". Moments later, the same voice said the plane was descending at a rate of 10,000ft (3,048m) per minute.
An emergency was declared and they can be heard yelling "we are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000ft per minute", before saying, "we are going to crash into the ground".
Seven passengers died on board the flight - named in a joint statement as tech entrepreneur Adam Robinson, his wife Helen Sharp, and their two children - Emma, four, and Charlie, two - as well as Rachael Reed, Charmi Fehr and Anita Maria Cetina.
The pilot was named in media reports as Jeffery Gregory, while Nathalia Filgueiras, 20, who earned her pilot's licence when she was 17, was reported to be the copilot.
One man in a car on the ground sustained a leg injury.
Image source,Anthony Robinson/FacebookImage caption,
Tech entrepreneur Adam Robinson and his wife Helen Sharp with their two small children, Emma and Charlie
Robinson and Sharp's family described them as "devoted parents" and said their children were "the light of their lives".
"Helen and Adam were the love affair that will last forever. Their warmth, generosity and gift for making people feel welcome touched so many lives," the statement reads.
On his LinkedIn page, Robinson described himself as the founder and CEO of RB2B and Retention.com, and the CEO of Moltsets. Helen Sharp was an artist, according to media reports.
Robinson previously worked at global financial services business Lehman Brothers and the banking group Barclays. The BBC has contacted the companies for a statement.
Image source,Anthony Robinson / FacebookImage caption,
Anita Maria Cetina, Charmi Fehr and Rachel Reed
The joint statement also named Anita Maria Cetina and said she "cared for Emma and Charlie with tenderness and devotion, and she was truly part of the family".
It added: "She showed us a legacy of unconditional love and devotion."
Rachel Reed and Charmi Fehr were described in the joint family statement as "full of joy and adventure".
"They loved their people fiercely, fully and without hesitation. From the moment they met, they were all in on each other and the life they were building."
Image source,Nathalia Filgueiras/ThreadImage caption,
Nathalia Filgueiras received her pilot's licence when she was in high school
Nathalia Filgueiras's mother, Camila Corteleti, confirmed to US media that her daughter had died in the fireball.
Corteleti told the New York Times: "She loved the freedom. It was completely different seeing the world from the top."
In a 2023 interview with a local news affiliate of CBS News, Filgueiras spoke proudly of receiving her pilot's licence while still a senior in high school.
"I like being different than everyone," she said. "Some people think that it's weird that I can fly planes, but I can't drive a car, I mean I can but, a lot of people think it's funny."
A spokesperson for East Coast Jets, where pilot Jeff Gregory used to work, said: "We are deeply saddened to learn that Capt Jeff Gregory was among those who lost their lives in yesterday's tragic aviation accident in Palm Beach."

The pilot in charge of the Learjet was identifiedby TMZand other media outlets on Monday as Jeff Gregory, 55, an experienced aviator from Pennsylvania.
The plane crashed at 12.51pm local time on Sunday, exploding on impact, leaving a giant crater in the ground, and scattering debris all around the crash site near a mobile home park in the city of Greenacres.
At a briefing on Monday, Tom Chapman, head of a team of about 20 National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) personnel in West Palm Beach, said conditions in south Florida on Sunday were “pretty crazy”, and that the weather would be “a major focus” of the investigation.

“She loved the freedom. It was completely different seeing the world from the top,” Cortelini said, adding that her daughter enjoyed plane spotting at local airports as a young girl.
Filgueiras graduated high school in Boca Raton, Florida, in 2024, having already obtained her private pilot’s license at the age of 17, according to the Palm Beach CBS affiliate12 News.
Aurora Aviation, which operated the aircraft under its trading name of Upper Jets, did not respond to a request for comment.
Robinson was the founder of several technology companies, and his wife owned a public relations firm, according to relatives.
“Adam and Helen were devoted parents, and Emma and Charlie were the light of their lives,” the statement said.
“Helen and Adam were the love affair that will last for ever. Their warmth, generosity and gift for making people feel welcome touched so many lives. Their loss will be felt deeply by all those who loved them and who they loved in return.
“Charmi and Rachel were full of joy and adventure. They loved their people fiercely, fully and without hesitation. From the moment they met, they were all in on each other and the life they were building. They are deeply loved, and we will miss them endlessly.
“Anita Maria cared for Emma and Charlie with tenderness and devotion, and she was truly part of the family. She showed us a legacy of unconditional love and devotion.”
Chapman of the NTSB said at the press conference: “I want to express our profound, profound condolences to the family and friends of those who were lost in this tragedy. We are truly, truly sorry for your loss.”

“The crew transmitted to ATC that they were encountering light, clear ice, which was manageable, and also moderate turbulence,” Chapman said, noting the plane was at 35,000ft at that point.

Chapman added: “Less than 30 seconds later, a transmission from the airplane announced a descent, followed by a mayday call. About 12.48pm, the airplane transmitted, “We are in an overspeed condition, descending,’ with the rest unintelligible. Sadly, all aboard were lost.”

Multiple videos circulating on social media capture the Learjet striking the ground almost vertically, and at a high rate of speed.

The crash occurred during an outbreak of severe weather and thunderstorms in south Florida that briefly closed Miami international airport and forced commercial airliners to divert to other airports.

9 dead as jet nosedives near busy roadway in South Florida : NPRAccessibility links
9 dead as jet nosedives near busy roadway in South FloridaU.S. Transportation Secretary Duffy says all nine people died aboard a business jet that crashed into a Florida neighborhood. The aircraft departed from Austin, Texas, and was headed to the Bahamas.
9 dead as jet nosedives and erupts into fireball near busy roadway in South Florida
Law enforcement respond to a plane crash in Palm Beach County, Fla., on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026.Mark Elias/APhide caption
A business jet carrying nine people nose-dived into a South Florida neighborhood Sunday and erupted into a giant fireball that appeared to just miss homes near a busy roadway. Everyone on board was killed, the nation's transportation secretary said.
Video recorded by people inside their cars captured the terrifying moment the Bahamas-bound aircraft plunged from the sky before striking near the Palm Beach County roadway and exploding. Flames flickered around chunks of pavement lining a crater as people milled about, expressing shock that it landed only feet from homes and inches from passing vehicles. Thick black smoke engulfed the crash site.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy posted on X that the Learjet 60 crashed in Palm Beach County at 12:50 p.m. and called it a "horrific tragedy." The Federal Aviation Administration is sending a team to support the National Transportation Safety Board's investigation, he said.
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said there were no immediate reports of anyone on the ground injured or killed.
"It was a cataclysmic plane crash," DeSantis told reporters at the scene. "It looked like a missile going down and left a big crater on the side of the road."
Rain pounded the region on Sunday. A flood watch due to excessive rainfall was in effect through Monday afternoon, the National Weather Service said.
The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. Authorities did not immediately say what caused the jet to go down or who was on it.
The plane was heading east at 35,000 feet (about 11 kilometers) when pilots reported turbulence, icing and precipitation and requested to climb another 2,000 feet (about 610 meters).
Moments later, the plane entered a steep dive, first 10,000 feet per minute, then 20,000 feet per minute and up to 30,000 feet per minute, speeding the plane beyond its design limits, according to air traffic control recordings and flight tracking data.
A pilot declared an emergency and issued distress calls. The plane banked sharply to the right before it smashed into the ground.
Minutes before the crash, the pilot reported ice accumulating on the jet and turbulence that was jolting it by as much as 700 feet (213 meters), according to air traffic control recordings captured by LiveATC.net.
"We have light, clear ice that is manageable and moderate turbulence," the pilot told controllers.
But the situation rapidly deteriorated. After encountering precipitation and requesting to climb, the pilot declared an emergency as the aircraft began losing altitude at an alarming rate.
"We're descending 8,000 – mayday, mayday - we're descending 10,000 feet per minute," the pilot radioed.
"We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute," the pilot radioed, before delivering a devastating acknowledgment of what was about to happen. "We're going to crash into the ground."
Jim Reynolds, a spokesperson for Austin-Bergstrom International Airport, said the jet was a private aircraft. He could not immediately provide details about who was on the flight.
Steve Arroyo, an aviation safety expert, said icing and turbulence could have been factors in the crash and may have caused the plane to stall while it was cruising at 34,000 feet (10,363 meters).
There are many potential factors and the NTSB will consider all of them, including how the pilot responded to the icing and turbulence reported over the radio. But investigators won't rule anything out at this early stage, he said.
The NTSB said investigators were expected to arrive at the crash site on Sunday and Monday. A media briefing is scheduled for Monday in West Palm Beach.
Palm Beach County authorities were evacuating about 600 people from a nearby mobile home community while federal officials investigate the crash. The road will be closed until further notice, county officials said.
The crash occurred in Greenacres, Florida, according to Palm Beach County sheriff's officials. The city of 45,000 people is about 7 miles (11 kilometers) southwest of West Palm Beach.

lead_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

evidence_pages.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cw23:
'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why - BBC News
Image source,Getty ImagesByMitchell LabiakBusiness reporter
The so-called "quiet quitting" trend where workers do the basic requirements of a job but refuse to do anything more might be hitting the economy, analysis has found.
Over the last decade, Britons have become less engaged with the jobs they do and are less willing to put in extra effort, according to a Resolution Foundation report.
The thinktank said this could partly help explain the slump in productivity since the pandemic.
"This is self-evidently bad for workers, but it also doesn't bode well for productivity and labour supply, both of which are vital for lifting living standards in the years ahead," said Hannah Slaughter, principal economist at the Resolution Foundation.
Quiet quitting waspopularised on social media shortly after the pandemic.
Frustrated by high demands, low pay, and a squeeze in living standards, many online posts said workers should only do what their bosses asked and nothing more.
So you still show up for work, but no more helping out with additional tasks or checking emails outside work hours, instead focusing on work-life balance and "acting your wage".
Yet, far from being just a talking point on TikTok, the Resolution Foundation said the findings in its report were "consistent" with the idea of quiet quitting.
'I was working 60 hours a week so I quiet quit'
The percentage of those surveyed willing to go the extra mile to help their employer has sunk from 69% in 2015 to 55% in 2025, according to their survey of 4,656 adults.
Meanwhile, those who were not even "fairly" satisfied with their roles has sank to one-in-four, the lowest level on record.
In addition, workers are less likely than 10 years ago to say they have an interesting job, with 63% of those surveyed saying so, down from 74%.
"Workers today are indeed a little less committed to their employers, and a little less intrinsically drawn to work in general, than workers were a decade ago," the report added.
This shift over the last decade "may have contributed to weak productivity growth", which has slowed since the financial crisis and weakened again after the pandemic, the Resolution Foundation found.
Workers were also more focused on pay than in the past, which it said was "perhaps unsurprising... given the flatlining living standards of the past decade".
Sir John Curtice, politics professor and co-editor of the report, said the analysis does not mean that young people have "become more 'work-shy', nor have workers in general become more reluctant to change jobs".
"But if workers are to be fully engaged in their work, it has seemingly become more important for employers to provide jobs that are both financially rewarding and have flexible work hours," he added.
