lead_title: UK Officials Said AI Would Add £400 Billion to the Economy. That Figure Mainly Came From Google

evidence_pages.https://www.wired.com/story/uk-officials:
UK Officials Said AI Would Add £400 Billion to the Economy. That Figure Mainly Came From Google | WIREDSkip to main content
For the lasttwo years, the UK government has been telling the British public that the country could receive an economic boost of £400 billion, thanks to AI, a figure intended to calm fears that the technology would lead to sweeping job losses and even an economic crash.
But the UK AI minister admitted last week that figure was significantly higher than the government’s actual projections after it was revealed that assessment came solely from a report commissioned by Google, and that its own estimation of AI’s economic benefit was less than a third of that £400 billion figure.n
AI minister Kanishka Narayan, answering a parliamentary question on the issue, said that AI adoption and data investment could add £55 billion to £140 billion to the UK economy by 2030, bringing the central estimate to £120 billion. But even this “more recent assessment,” he said, was a “hugely uncertain” estimate.
Narayan said the £400b figure “was drawn from a publicly available 2023 report commissioned by Google and produced by Public First,” a British consultancy firm now referred to as PF Global.
Responding to WIRED’s questions about the difference between the figures, PF Global’s head of economics, Jonathan Dupont, said the disparity was partially because of what they saw as the government’s slow adoption of AI. “AI is a very fast moving technology, and, as we learn more, we inevitably have to update the assumptions lying behind our models. Compared to our older model, the numbers the government uses assume a much slower rate of adoption than looked possible back in our model that was created in 2023.”
Government departments and agencies used Google’s £400 billion figure for almost two years, under two governments. Ministers have had the lower estimate since at least November 2025, almost a year before this week’s admission, yet Skills England, a government agency responsible for apprenticeships, was still publishing the old figure four months later.
Nayaran’s parliamentary answer is the first recorded evidence WIRED could find of the government setting the two numbers side by side, or saying that the report was commissioned by Google. The answer did not withdraw the £400 billion figure or say it had been wrong.
Dame Chi Onwurah, the Labour MP who chairs the Commons Science, Innovation and Technology Committee, told WIRED: “The government is right to promote the potential for technology like AI to improve public services. However, these reports highlight one of the central barriers to delivering the digital transformation of public services my committee has identified: hype.
“Economic projects inevitably rely on assumptions, but overstating the benefits of technology risks undermining the case for change. The government needs to be realistic about what technology like AI can deliver and be transparent with the public about potential savings.”
PF Global highlighted more top-down adoption of AI and integration into civil service workflows as examples of how take-up could improve. “While we haven’t changed our view on the overall potential of technology, given the slower rate of adoption we’ve seen in practice, our central estimate for the amount of potential likely to be achieved by 2030 is much closer to the Government’s number—with growth ramping up in the next few years after that.”
Lord Holmes of Richmond, the Conservative peer who asked ministers in January 2025 about the origins of the £400 billion claim but did not receive a response, told WIRED: “It is unfortunate that the figure used repeatedly by the government, and then, unsurprisingly, by multiple other organizations has now been significantly and rightly adjusted. Google faces backlash for plan that would turn off Search for schools that restrict AI
Amanda Silberling8:17 AM PST · November 4, 2026
Google was met with swift backlash on Tuesday after itannouncedthat schools using Google’s K-12 software will not be able to use Search unless they opt in to using AI tools.
Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google,toldThe New York Times that “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” so if a student’s school doesn’t opt in to using AI tools like Gemini, then students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.”
Even as Google made this announcement on a busy Election Day, several left-leaning politicians took time to speak up about their concerns.
Senator Bernie Sanders (I-VT)accusedGoogle in an X post of “extortion,” writing that “Google is threatening schools: if you stop your students from using AI, we will cut off your access to Google Search.” Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT)said on Xthat Google is “more concerned with forcing Gemini into schools than enabling students to succeed.”
President Trump claimed that AI oligarchs could regulate themselves because they “love our country.”
Now, Google is threatening schools: if you stop your students from using AI, we will cut off your access to Google Search.
— Sen. Bernie Sanders (@SenSanders)November 3, 2026
Lina Khan, the former FTC chair and staunch advocate against monopolies, also condemned Google’s decision as anti-competitive.
“This highlights the danger of allowing an unregulated monopolist to control an essential service,” shewrote. “Multiple courts have found Google liable for violating antitrust laws, and this latest move shows it remains unchastened.”
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused Google of being a monopoly,commenting, “No corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children.”
Google is using its search monopoly to coerce schools into adopting AI. This highlights the danger of allowing an unregulated monopolist to control an essential service.
Multiple courts have found Google liable for violating antitrust laws, and this latest move shows it remains…https://t.co/eajJN9yfQF
— Lina Khan (@linamkhan)November 3, 2026
While Search is a necessary tool for information gathering, educators worry that its built-in AI overviews could dissuade students from finding answers themselves. For millions of students required to use Chromebooks and Google education tools,using a different search engineisn’t a simple fix.
Google says that it’s working on a “Guided Learning” tool for student accounts in Search, which is supposed to walk students through the process of solving a problem or finding information, rather than just handing them the answer. If a student is struggling with a math problem, for example, the feature may prompt them to refresh their memory about the rules for dividing exponents, instead of spitting out a number.
In response to the backlash, Google pointed out ina post on Xthat it had listened to educators by turning off access to AI products by default, and noted that schools could turn on Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search individually.
We want to clarify what we announced today about our education services. Today’s announcements give schools more choice, not less. Here’s what we announced:
– Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search will be OFF 🔴 by default. This is based on K-12 schools asking for more control…
— News from Google (@NewsFromGoogle)November 3, 2026
“We know there’s concern about students using AI to shortcut schoolwork, and schools have told us they want control,” Googlewrotein a statement. “That’s exactly why we are making these changes today to address the feedback we’ve heard from educators in recent months. And we’ll continue to engage deeply with educators to ensure we are giving schools more choice, more controls, and improved Search for learning.”

fact_units.text: UK Officials Said AI Would Add £400 Billion to the Economy.
That Figure Mainly Came From Google | WIREDSkip to main content

For the lasttwo years, the UK government has been telling the British public that the country could receive an economic boost of £400 billion, thanks to AI, a figure intended to calm fears that the technology would lead to sweeping job losses and even an economic crash.

But the UK AI minister admitted last week that figure was significantly higher than the government’s actual projections after it was revealed that assessment came solely from a report commissioned by Google, and that its own estimation of AI’s economic benefit was less than a third of that £400 billion figure.n

AI minister Kanishka Narayan, answering a parliamentary question on the issue, said that AI adoption and data investment could add £55 billion to £140 billion to the UK economy by 2030, bringing the central estimate to £120 billion.
But even this “more recent assessment,” he said, was a “hugely uncertain” estimate.
Narayan said the £400b figure “was drawn from a publicly available 2023 report commissioned by Google and produced by Public First,” a British consultancy firm now referred to as PF Global.

Responding to WIRED’s questions about the difference between the figures, PF Global’s head of economics, Jonathan Dupont, said the disparity was partially because of what they saw as the government’s slow adoption of AI.
“AI is a very fast moving technology, and, as we learn more, we inevitably have to update the assumptions lying behind our models.
Compared to our older model, the numbers the government uses assume a much slower rate of adoption than looked possible back in our model that was created in 2023.”
Government departments and agencies used Google’s £400 billion figure for almost two years, under two governments.

Ministers have had the lower estimate since at least November 2025, almost a year before this week’s admission, yet Skills England, a government agency responsible for apprenticeships, was still publishing the old figure four months later.
Nayaran’s parliamentary answer is the first recorded evidence WIRED could find of the government setting the two numbers side by side, or saying that the report was commissioned by Google.
The answer did not withdraw the £400 billion figure or say it had been wrong.

Dame Chi Onwurah, the Labour MP who chairs the Commons Science, Innovation and Technology Committee, told WIRED: “The government is right to promote the potential for technology like AI to improve public services.
However, these reports highlight one of the central barriers to delivering the digital transformation of public services my committee has identified: hype.
“Economic projects inevitably rely on assumptions, but overstating the benefits of technology risks undermining the case for change.
The government needs to be realistic about what technology like AI can deliver and be transparent with the public about potential savings.”
PF Global highlighted more top-down adoption of AI and integration into civil service workflows as examples of how take-up could improve.

“While we haven’t changed our view on the overall potential of technology, given the slower rate of adoption we’ve seen in practice, our central estimate for the amount of potential likely to be achieved by 2030 is much closer to the Government’s number—with growth ramping up in the next few years after that.”

Lord Holmes of Richmond, the Conservative peer who asked ministers in January 2025 about the origins of the £400 billion claim but did not receive a response, told WIRED: “It is unfortunate that the figure used repeatedly by the government, and then, unsurprisingly, by multiple other organizations has now been significantly and rightly adjusted.
It would have been better for the government to clarify this much sooner and more directly.”
He added: “Robust data is critical, not least as billions of pounds of our money and how the government chooses to deploy it depend on it.”
The spat over these two numbers—£120 billion and £400 billion—is part of a wider debate over the line between government support and boosterism.

Former technology minister Peter Kyle also used the £400 billion while promoting the benefits of AI, while many parliamentarians outside of government raised questions about potential issues around the technology.

“The government’s revised estimates for how much AI could add to the economy are welcome—but it’s concerning that they come after almost two years of ministers citing a figure from research that was paid for by Google,” Sumedha Deshmukh of the Ada Lovelace Institute told WIRED.
Figures about AI that look precise often have assumptions and incentives built into them, and industry often funds or shapes the research behind them.
“The government should test the numbers it is given before it builds policy on them, fund independent research, and measure whether promised gains are delivered.

It should always start by asking simple questions before it uses any number around economic or productivity gains from AI—where did it come from, what does it assume, and who actually benefits from a given figure?”
The Cabinet Office, the department responsible for AI in government and Google, were approached for comment.
PF Global said their work for Google continued but all research was independent and all judgments and assumptions were their own.

Bodycam footage from a police officer killed in the attack captures the moments before a Russian bomb strikes a shelter in Komyshuvakha, in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, killing at least 37 people.
The recording shows people gathered outside a former school building, anxiously discussing the threat of further attacks. "Misha, is it coming again?" a woman asks, before a warning crackles over a police radio:"Guided aerial bombs heading towards Komyshuvakha! Take shelter!"Officers urgently direct people down the stairs into an underground refuge. Moments later, the camera records aviolent explosion.
The strikekilled at least 37 people, according to Ukraine's national police,including the officer whose bodycam captured the attack. The shelter, located inside a former school building, was hit by aRussian FAB-3000 aerial bomb, a powerful weapon weighing approximately three tonnes.
Rescue workers continued searching through the wreckage for victims as the scale of the destruction became clear. The footage provides a harrowing record of the final warnings and frantic efforts to reach safety before the building was struck, offering arare first-hand perspectiveon the deadly bombardment.

toggle captioniUkrainian Emergency Service/via AP
KYIV, Ukraine — The death toll from a Russian attack in southern Ukraine on a site where people had gathered to receive humanitarian aid rose to 29 on Tuesday, with 48 still missing, as a wave of overnight strikes targeted power plants across the country, damaged hospitals and wounded scores of people.
A brief ceasefire in Ukraine's Kherson region has ended
Dozens of rescuers and volunteers continued to search the cratered blast site of a destroyed aid facility and shelter in Komyushuvakha, a village in Ukraine's southern Zaporizhzhia region, hoping to find missing residents alive under the rubble. Instead, more bodies were pulled out and carried away in white plastic sheeting.
"The scale of the tragedy is terrifying," Mykhailo Semikin, acting head of the region's military administration, wrote in an online post. "This is one of the worst tragedies in terms of the number of civilian victims in our region since the start of the full-scale war."
A woman and her cat take shelter from a Russian drone and missile attack, in a metro station, now used as a bomb shelter, in Kyiv, Ukraine, Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026.Danylo Antoniuk/APhide caption
Russia launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles across nine regions, triggering emergency power cuts, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in an online post that noted the barrage coincided with U.S. elections.
"The Russians think America won't notice this signal of theirs," he said. "But we need to notice and stop such terror. We need to help Ukraine defend its skies; otherwise, Russia will never stop its missile strikes."
Three days of mourning were declared in Zaporizhzhia where Russian bunker-busting bombs, filled with nearly 1.5 tons of explosives, were used in Monday's attack.
The dead included four police officers and two rescue workers, Semikin said Tuesday. At least five people were hurt.
In this photo provided by the Ukrainian Emergency Service, a residential building is seen following a Russian air attack in Dnipro, Ukraine, Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026.Ukrainian Emergency Service/via APhide caption
In the northeast region of Kharkiv, a combined Russian missile and drone attack wounded at least 62 people, local authorities said.
A strike damaged a medical facility in the Nemyshlianskyi district, shattered windows in four apartment buildings and damaged cars. More than 200 patients were transferred to other medical facilities, head of the regional military administration Oleh Syniehubov said.
In the Dnipro area, rescuers pulled a woman alive from the rubble Tuesday morning, after a Russian attack killed one person and wounded 17, local authorities said.
The attack damaged an outpatient clinic and a hospital. Patients were transferred to other hospitals, Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the regional military administration, said.
Russia's Ministry of Defense said Tuesday that it had shot down 856 Ukrainian drones overnight. Moscow mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 493 drones were fired toward the Russian capital.
How AI drones are influencing the course of the Ukraine war
A Ukrainian drone attack wounded two employees at an oil refinery in the Russian city of Yaroslavl, regional Gov. Mikhail Yevrayev said Tuesday. He added that there was damage to the refinery's infrastructure.
Rolling blackouts have been instituted in the south, west and east of Russian-occupied Crimea following attacks on energy infrastructure, Moscow-installed officials said Tuesday.

Ukraine defies Trump to resume attacks on Russian oil refineries
Kremlin says Kyiv is ‘simply ignoring’ US wishes days before midterm elections after reported strikes on two oil sites
Ukraine has resumed its attacks on Russian oil refineries in defiance of pressure fromDonald Trumpahead of the US midterm elections, as a ceasefire in the occupied town of Oleshky ended on Sunday night.
Russian state media said on Sunday Ukrainian long-range drones had set fire to the Kstovo refinery in Nizhny Novgorod oblast overnight, soon after a major strike against another big refinery in Samara oblast, owned by the Russian state energy giant Rosneft.
The Wall Street Journal hadreported that Ukraine had given in to pressurefrom the White House to stop bombing Russian energy infrastructure.
Ukrainian officials, however, told the Kyiv Independent newspaper thatthey never agreed to a demandfrom Jared Kushner, the US president’s son-in-law, to pause refinery strikes for 30 days. The raids on Russia restarted on Friday, Kremlin officials said, complaining that Kyiv was now “simply ignoring” US wishes.
Trump has blamed the Ukrainian president,Volodymyr Zelenskyy, for the rise in global fuel prices, and last month lifted US sanctions on Russian diesel.
Ukraine war briefing: Oleshky truce shows de-escalation is possible, says ZelenskyyRead more
Zelenskyy has not acknowledged the latest refinery attacks, in an apparent attempt to avoid angry US reprisals. Instead, he said his armed forces had hit a defence industry enterprise in Russia’s Rostov region that made missiles. A Pantsir missile system was destroyed, he said, as part of Ukraine’s continuing “long-range sanctions”.
View image in fullscreenA satellite image shows smoke rising from the Novokuybyshevsk oil refinery in the Samara region of Russia after a reported Ukrainian drone attack on Friday.Photograph: European Union/Copernicus/Sentinel-2/Reuters
Zelenskyy said his country was obliged to retaliate because of a remorseless campaign by Moscow, using drones and ballistic missiles, against vulnerable city-based energy facilities. Four Ukrainian regions were hit by Russia overnight, with electricity cut as a result in hundreds of thousands of households.
“The intensity of the strikes is very high, and the Russians are seeking to maximally exploit the ​deficit of ballistic missile interceptors,” the Ukrainian president said on Telegram.Kyivexperienced power cuts lasting eight to 10 hours on Sunday after a critical thermal power plant was damaged.
Zelenskyy said Russia was suffering record losses, with 54,400 military personnel killed and wounded in October – the highest monthly figure since the full-scale war began. He said Ukraine recaptured 96.2 sq km (37 sq miles) of its territory last month, 10.4 sq km (4 sq miles) more than Moscow managed to seize, and emphasised: “Russia is losing.”
The latest attacks came beforea six-day local ceasefirebrokered by the US first lady, Melania Trump, came to an end in the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky. Hundreds of residentswere reunited with their loved onesover the weekend in northern Ukraine, with both sides hailing the evacuation mission as a success.
“The ceasefire, which was in effect from October 27 to November 1, has ended,” said Ukraine’s human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets, hailing what had been an “important step in our joint humanitarian efforts”.
Ukrainian observers say the Russian military used the truce to reinforce its positions and to swap hungry and exhausted troops garrisoned in Oleshky. The town sits on the left bank of the Dnipro River, to the east, and is opposite the larger city of Kherson, which Ukraine recaptured in autumn 2022. A renewed Russian onslaught is inevitable, the observers believe.
The pope said on Sunday he hoped cooperation between ⁠Russia and Ukraine in implementing the Oleshky ceasefire – the most significant since 2022 – would ⁠pave the ⁠way ​for broader peace efforts.
“I hope that the cooperation between the parties, which made this necessary humanitarian gesture possible, will strengthen their willingness to engage in dialogue,” he said during his Sunday prayer.
Later on Sunday Ukraine’s air force and anti-disinformation centre said they suspected the country’s air raid alert system had been hacked, after false alerts of a radiation threat appeared on the application. The announcement came minutes after the end of the truce.
A separate app, which deals specifically with the Ukrainian capital, is still working normally, the Kyiv city authorities said.
Hours later, Russia’s emergencies ministry claimed that a “massive cyber-attack” had hit its own application designed to warn people of incoming drone attacks and other threats.
Trilateral talks involving Russia, Ukraine and the US are likely to take place later this month, and Kremlin officials said on Sunday thatVladimir Putinwas willing to talk directly to Zelenskyy by phone. They added that European leaders who support Ukraine should not be involved in any such call.
There is little prospect of a wider breakthrough, however, as the Russian president’s maximalist demands remain unchanged.
He is insisting that Ukraine give up all of the eastern Donetsk oblast – which Russia has been unable to seize since 2014 – as well as further territory in Kherson and Zaporizhzhia provinces, which the Kremlin does not control but says it has “annexed”.

Strike on Ukraine Humanitarian Hub Is Feared to Be Among War’s Deadliest - The New York Times
A day after a Russian glide bomb attack killed at least 31 Ukrainians at a school distributing medicine and food, emergency workers braved armed Russian drones on Tuesday as they searched for dozens of people still missing, officials said.
It could take days to determine the exact toll: The threat of continued Russian strikes limits rescuers to short bursts of activity. But the attack was the deadliest against civilians in the southern Zaporizhzhia region during nearly five years of war, and could amount to one of the deadliest of the entire conflict.
Hours after the strike on Monday, the Trump administration’s peace envoy, Steve Witkoff, announced that talks among the United States, Russia and Ukraine would be held early next week in Abu Dhabi, in the United Arab Emirates.
The meeting, the first since February involving all three countries, would address postwar security arrangements and steps toward peace, Mr. Witkoff said. The Russian and Ukrainian governments confirmed on Tuesday that they would send negotiators to Abu Dhabi.
But even as the Trump administration tries to restart peace talks, President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine said that Russia had made clear its intention to continue the war by striking the humanitarian hub in the village of Komyshuvakha on Monday.
Russia hit the village with at least nine glide bombs, each loaded with around 3,000 pounds of explosives, Ukrainian officials said. The attack served as a stark reminder of the limits ofa rare local cease-firein the neighboring Kherson region, which ended a day before.
That six-day truce allowed the evacuation of hundreds of civilians facing starvation in the besieged city of Oleshky, which Russia has occupied since 2022.
The school that was hit in the village of Komyshuvakha doubled as a bomb shelter. The attack trapped civilians and rescue workers inside.
ImageUkrainian soldiers firing at a Russian drone at the site of Monday’s strike.Credit...Reuters
At least two rescue workers and four police officers who arrived to treat the wounded after the first bomb landed were killed in the subsequent round of bombing, Ukraine’s emergency response services said. Russia has long used this tactic, known as a double tap, to target emergency workers responding to attacks.
On Tuesday, Russia continued to send armed drones over the village, Ukrainian officials said. About 50 people remained missing, they said.
“Every single hour, the rescue operations are being interrupted because of F.P.V. drone threats,” said Mykhailo Semikin, the acting head of Zaporizhzhia’s regional military administration, referring to first-person-view drones. “It’s a cynical thing to do.”
Residents had visited the school each week to receive humanitarian aid, Mr. Zelensky said on social media. “This is yet another proof that Russia does not want any de-escalation or real justice,” he wrote.
The temporary cease-fire in the neighboring Kherson region lasted from Tuesday through Sunday. The evacuation operation in Oleshky raised hopes for further cooperation between Kyiv and Moscow to ensure the safety of civilians near the front line. It was the first truce of its kind since Russia’s 2022 invasion.
The deal, brokered in part by the American first lady, Melania Trump, offered “a moment when the next steps could have shown that a move towards peace was possible,” Mr. Zelensky wrote. But after the bombing of Komyshuvakha, he added, “Russia is sending a completely opposite signal — Russia is counting on further killings.”
ImageThe crater where a school once stood.Credit...Associated Press
Zaporizhzhia is one of four Ukrainian regions that President Vladimir V. Putin of Russiaclaimed to have annexedin 2022, though his forces never managed to seize Zaporizhzhia’s regional capital, a city of the same name. The front line stretches across the region, and fierce fighting has continued for years, including around Komyshuvakha, where Russian drones have tormented civilians who stayed behind.
The school was built after the full-scale invasion with a reinforced concrete basement that was used as a shelter. But by the time the school was ready for class, the situation in Komyshuvakha had become grim. While the front line had not significantly shifted, drones could now fly much farther, leaving Komyshuvakha trapped in the middle of what is known as the “kill zone.”
Students attended the school for only a few months before officials evacuated all children from the area. Adults were urged to leave as well, but many hesitated for common reasons: They had animals to care for, or they feared being a burden in a new town away from their own land. Many of those who stayed were older or disabled.
Each Monday, they received aid from volunteers at the school. This week, when the first glide bomb struck the village, residents rushed to the school’s basement for shelter. But the heavier bombs that came next were designed to cause mass destruction, officials said.
The concrete could not withstand the impact, and many people hiding from the attack were buried underground.
Mr. Semikin rushed to the scene on Monday, stopping to take cover from Russian drones along the way, he said. A video he posted showed that little of the school remained. Behind him, smoke rose over piles of debris.
ImageBags holding the bodies of some of those killed in the strike.Credit...Reuters
Siobhán O’Grady is a Ukraine correspondent for The Times, based in Kyiv.

Ukraine: Police footage captures Russian strike on Komyshuvakha shelter
Updated:4 November 2026 - 17:31 GMT+1
Bodycam footage from a police officer killed in the attack captures the moments before a Russian bomb strikes a shelter in Komyshuvakha, in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, killing at least 37 people.
The recording shows people gathered outside a former school building, anxiously discussing the threat of further attacks.
"Misha, is it coming again?" a woman asks, before a warning crackles over a police radio:"Guided aerial bombs heading towards Komyshuvakha!
Take shelter!"Officers urgently direct people down the stairs into an underground refuge.
The strikekilled at least 37 people, according to Ukraine's national police,including the officer whose bodycam captured the attack.
The shelter, located inside a former school building, was hit by aRussian FAB-3000 aerial bomb, a powerful weapon weighing approximately three tonnes.
Rescue workers continued searching through the wreckage for victims as the scale of the destruction became clear.
The footage provides a harrowing record of the final warnings and frantic efforts to reach safety before the building was struck, offering arare first-hand perspectiveon the deadly bombardment.

Cánh đồng dứa mọc trên đại lộ ngàn tỉ: Tỉnh cho để lại đến khi thu hoạch xong
Lãnh đạo UBND tỉnh Ninh Bình cho biết sẽ tạm thời giữ lại cánh đồng dứa người dân tự ý trồng trên đại lộ Hoa Lư, cho người dân thu hoạch xong vụ, không cho phát sinh trồng mới.
Cánh đồng dứa xanh mướt mọc trên dải phân cách đại lộ Hoa Lư, tỉnh Ninh Bình - Ảnh: THÀNH NAM
Tối ngày 4-11, trao đổi vớiTuổi Trẻ, một lãnh đạo UBND tỉnh Ninh Bình, cho biết tỉnh đã nắm được thông tin liên quan đến vụ việc người dântrồng dứatrên dải phân cách đại lộ Hoa Lư.
Vụ cánh đồng dứa mọc trên đại lộ ngàn tỉ: Đẹp thì có đẹp nhưng vẫn sai quy địnhĐỌC NGAY
Theo lãnh đạo UBND tỉnh Ninh Bình, trước mắt tỉnh thống nhất phương án tạm thời giữ lại ruộng dứa để người dân thu hoạch xong, không cho phát sinh trồng mới, nhưng phải có giải pháp đảm bảo an toàn vấn đề giao thông.
Liên quan đến vấn đề này, sáng 4-11, trao đổi vớiTuổi Trẻ, ông Đặng Hữu Trường, Phó giám đốc Ban Quản lý dự án đầu tư xây dựng số 1 tỉnh Ninh Bình, khẳng định việc làm này là không đúng quy định.
Khu vực này là đất giao thông nên công năng chỉ để phục vụ giao thông, người dân không thể lấy đất giao thông đi làm nông nghiệp được.
Theo ông Trường, sự việc được đơn vị phát hiện từ cuối năm 2025. Ngay sau đó, Ban đã có văn bản gửi các địa phương dọc tuyến và nhà thầu, đề nghị phối hợp vận động người dân dừng việc trồng dứa.
Dải phân cách có chiều dài khoảng 3-5km đoạn qua xã Phú Long, tỉnh Ninh Bình được người dân trồng kín dứa - Ảnh: THÀNH NAM
Tuy nhiên, ông Trường thừa nhận dù sự việc được phát hiện từ gần một năm trước nhưng đến nay vẫn chưa được xử lý triệt để, công tác giám sát ở một số thời điểm còn chưa chặt chẽ.
Cũng theo ông Trường, dự án dự kiến kết thúc vào ngày 31-12-2026, sau đó sẽ được bàn giao cho Sở Xây dựng tỉnh Ninh Bình quản lý, khai thác.
Đối với tình trạng người dân vẫn trồng dứa, ông Trường cho biết Ban sẽ tiếp tục phối hợp với nhà thầu và chính quyền địa phương vận động người dân chấp hành.
Trường hợp người dân không đồng thuận, đơn vị sẽ rà soát cụ thể từng hộ để yêu cầu dừng việc canh tác trong phạm vi dự án.
NhưTuổi Trẻđã thông tin, trên dải phân cách và bên hành lang đại lộ Hoa Lư có tổng mức đầu tư gần 2.000 tỉ đồng đoạn qua xã Phú Long, Cúc Phương, tỉnh Ninh Bình bỗng xuất hiện những cánh đồng dứa xanh mướt, kéo dài nhiều cây số.
Ghi nhận thực tế dọc tuyến đường sáng 2-11 cho thấy việc người dân trồng dứa chỉ bắt đầu xuất hiện tại địa bàn xã Phú Long và xã Cúc Phương. Trong đó, tập trung nhiều nhất tại xã Phú Long.
Chủ đầu tư khẳng định, việc người dân trồng dứa trong phạm vi dự án đại lộ Hoa Lư là không được phép - Ảnh: THÀNH NAM
Tại đoạn đường này, dải phân cách xuất hiện những cánh đồng dứa được trồng kín. Có chỗ dứa đã bén rễ, xanh tốt và đang chuẩn bị ra quả, có nơi dứa vừa mới được trồng. Không chỉ trồng dứa, một số đoạn trên dải phân cách, người dân còn trồng cả ngô, lạc.
Trái với những đoạn đường này, tại nhiều vị trí không trồng dứa, cỏ cây mọc um tùm, có nơi cây lau sậy mọc cao quá đầu người, tràn cả ra đường giao thông.
Vụ việc sau đó nổ ra tranh cãi trên mạng xã hội. Chủ đầu tư cho rằng việc trồng dứa trên dải phân cách, trong phạm vị dự án là không được phép. Trong khi, nhiều ý kiến cho rằng, trồng dứa trên khu vực này tránh cỏ dại mọc um tùm che khuất tầm nhìn, đường lại trở nên thông thoáng.
Tuy nhiên, nhiều độc giả lại cho rằng khi người dân tự ý cải tạo đất trồng dứa, quá trình chăm sóc và thu hoạch dứa sẽ tiềm ẩn nguy cơ gây ra tai nạn giao thông.
Chủ đầu tư nói gì về cánh đồng dứa mọc trên đại lộ ngàn tỉ gây tranh cãi?
Lãnh đạo Ban Quản lý dự án đầu tư xây dựng số 1 tỉnh Ninh Bình khẳng định việc người dân trồng dứa trong phạm vi dự án đại lộ Hoa Lư là không được phép, đồng thời cho biết đang phối hợp với các đơn vị liên quan vận động người dân không tiếp tục canh tác.

Tạm thời giữ lại ruộng dứa trên đại lộ nghìn tỷ, cấm người dân vào chăm sóc | Báo Dân trí
Sự kiệnXử lý vi phạm tại 12 dự án của Mường ThanhBa xã ở Phú Thọ dự kiến sáp nhập về Hà Nội
Tạm thời giữ lại ruộng dứa trên đại lộ nghìn tỷ, cấm người dân vào chăm sóc
(Dân trí) - Những ruộng dứa trên dải phân cách giữa đại lộ Hoa Lư ở Ninh Bình tạm thời được giữ nguyên nhưng đơn vị thi công sẽ cấm tuyệt đối người dân ra vào chăm sóc, tránh nguy cơ tai nạn.
Ngày 4/11, trao đổi với phóng viênDân trí, đại diện đơn vị thi công dự án xây dựng đại lộ Hoa Lư (Ninh Bình) cho biết, nhà thầu đang khẩn trương thực hiện các biện pháp đảm bảo an toàn giao thông trên tuyến đường sau khi có chỉ đạo từ chủ đầu tư dự án là Ban Quản lý dự án đầu tư xây dựng số 1 tỉnh Ninh Bình.
Ruộng dứa xanh tốt trên dải phân cách giữa ở đại lộ nghìn tỷ đồng sẽ được giữ lại cho đến khi thu hoạch xong (Ảnh: Thái Bá).
Vị này cho biết thêm, đối với phương án xử lý những ruộng dứa người dân đã trồng trên dải phân cách giữa và hai bên tuyến đường dự án, đơn vị thi công sẽ phối hợp với chính quyền địa phương cấm tuyệt đối người dân ra vào khu vực này, tránh nguy cơ xảy ra tai nạn giao thông.
"Những khu vực người dân đã trồng dứa, nhà thầu sẽ tạm thời giữ nguyên hiện trạng nhưng cấm tuyệt đối người dân ra vào khu vực này chăm sóc cây. Chúng tôi sẽ lên phương án hỗ trợ chi phí người dân đã bỏ ra để trồng và chăm sóc cây dứa", đại diện đơn vị thi công cho hay.
Cũng theo vị đại diện, trước mắt giữ nguyên ruộng dứa, không phá bỏ đi vì số lượng lớn, dứa sắp cho thu hoạch, nếu phá bỏ rất lãng phí. Hơn nữa, cây dứa trồng ở dải phân cách giữa và hai bên đường hiện tại không làm ảnh hưởng tầm nhìn người tham gia giao thông.
Đơn vị thi công dự án sẽ cấm tuyệt đối người dân ra vào khu vực trồng dứa trên đường để canh tác, tránh nguy cơ tai nạn xảy ra (Ảnh: Thái Bá).
"Đến khi dứa cho thu hoạch, nhà thầu sẽ có phương án đảm bảo an toàn để thu hoạch dứa, sau đó cho dẹp bỏ thân cây để trả lại mặt bằng nguyên trạng cho tuyến đường", vị đại diện nói.
Trước đó, trao đổi với phóng viênDân trí, đại diện chủ đầu tư chia sẻ, nói về lý việc người dân trồng dứa trên công trình giao thông là vi phạm pháp luật. Việc canh tác làm thay đổi hiện trạng của hồ sơ thiết kế công trình, gây mất an toàn giao thông... Nói về tình, thực tế cây dứa không gây nguy hiểm gì, hợp với thổ nhưỡng tại đây nên phát triển xanh tốt tạo cảnh quan rất đẹp, hạn chế được cỏ dại mọc um tùm.
Tuy nhiên, pháp luật không cho phép việc làm này, vì thế phải cấm tuyệt đối hành vi này, tránh nguy cơ không may tai nạn giao thông xảy ra đối với người dân và các phương tiện.
NhưDân tríđã phản ánh, việc người dân tự ý cày xới, canh tác trồng cây dứa trong phạm vi dải phân cách giữa đại lộ Hoa Lư đã diễn ra thời gian dài nhưng không được xử lý dứt điểm.
Cây dứa xanh tốt trên đại lộ Hoa Lư, sắp ra quả cho thu hoạch (Ảnh: Thái Bá).
Một số người dân chăm sóc dứa tại đây cho biết, họ không biết chủ những ruộng dứa này là ai. Họ chỉ được thuê làm công chăm sóc, mỗi ngày từ 250-300 nghìn đồng.
Đại lộ Hoa Lư có tổng chiều dài gần 23km, có tổng mức đầu tư hơn 1.900 tỷ đồng, thời gian thực hiện 2021-2026. Tuyến đường được xây dựng theo tiêu chuẩn vận tốc thiết kế 100km/h, giai đoạn I phân kỳ đầu tư vận tốc thiết kế là 80km/h.
Toàn cảnh đại lộ Hoa Lư có tổng mức đầu tư 2.000 tỷ đồng ở Ninh Bình (Ảnh: Thái Bá).
Đại lộ Hoa Lư là dự án giao thông kết nối liên vùng lớn nhất tỉnh Ninh Bình hiện nay, được ví như cao tốc kết nối giữa miền núi và đồng bằng của tỉnh.
Những ruộng dứa trên đại lộ nghìn tỷ: Gần một năm không xử lý dứt điểm
Việc người dân tự ý cày xới, canh tác trong phạm vi dải phân cách giữa đại lộ Hoa Lư diễn ra thời gian dài. Chủ đầu tư, chính quyền địa phương đã không quyết liệt khiến diện tích trồng tăng lên.
Những ruộng dứa xuất hiện trên đại lộ 2.000 tỷ đồng ở Ninh Bình
Giải phân cách giữa, hành lang hai bên đường thuộc dự án đầu tư xây dựng tuyến đường Đại lộ Hoa Lư trị giá gần 2.000 tỷ đồng, thời gian qua bất ngờ bị biến thành ruộng trồng dứa của người dân.
Ruộng dứa trên đại lộ nghìn tỷ: Trồng dứa ở dải phân cách đúng hay sai?
Phó Giám đốc Ban Quản lý dự án đầu tư xây dựng số 1 tỉnh Ninh Bình khẳng định, việc người dân tự ý trồng dứa trên dải phân cách, hành lang hai bên đường là tự phát, vi phạm quy định pháp luật.
Sẽ xử lý việc người dân trồng dứa trên dải phân cách ở Ninh Bình
Theo ông Đặng Hữu Trường, việc người dân trồng dứa trên dải phân cách ở Ninh Bình là vi phạm pháp luật, chủ đầu tư sẽ phối hợp với chính quyền địa phương xử lý tình trạng trên.

Đăng ký Tuổi Trẻ SaoVào trang Tuổi Trẻ Sao
Cánh đồng dứa mọc trên đại lộ ngàn tỉ: Tỉnh cho để lại đến khi thu hoạch xong
Lãnh đạo UBND tỉnh Ninh Bình cho biết sẽ tạm thời giữ lại cánh đồng dứa người dân tự ý trồng trên đại lộ Hoa Lư, cho người dân thu hoạch xong vụ, không cho phát sinh trồng mới.
Cánh đồng dứa xanh mướt mọc trên dải phân cách đại lộ Hoa Lư, tỉnh Ninh Bình - Ảnh: THÀNH NAM
Tối ngày 4-11, trao đổi vớiTuổi Trẻ, một lãnh đạo UBND tỉnh Ninh Bình, cho biết tỉnh đã nắm được thông tin liên quan đến vụ việc người dântrồng dứatrên dải phân cách đại lộ Hoa Lư.
Vụ cánh đồng dứa mọc trên đại lộ ngàn tỉ: Đẹp thì có đẹp nhưng vẫn sai quy địnhĐỌC NGAY

Theo lãnh đạo UBND tỉnh Ninh Bình, trước mắt tỉnh thống nhất phương án tạm thời giữ lại ruộng dứa để người dân thu hoạch xong, không cho phát sinh trồng mới, nhưng phải có giải pháp đảm bảo an toàn vấn đề giao thông.
Liên quan đến vấn đề này, sáng 4-11, trao đổi vớiTuổi Trẻ, ông Đặng Hữu Trường, Phó giám đốc Ban Quản lý dự án đầu tư xây dựng số 1 tỉnh Ninh Bình, khẳng định việc làm này là không đúng quy định.
Khu vực này là đất giao thông nên công năng chỉ để phục vụ giao thông, người dân không thể lấy đất giao thông đi làm nông nghiệp được.
Theo ông Trường, sự việc được đơn vị phát hiện từ cuối năm 2025.
Ngay sau đó, Ban đã có văn bản gửi các địa phương dọc tuyến và nhà thầu, đề nghị phối hợp vận động người dân dừng việc trồng dứa.
Dải phân cách có chiều dài khoảng 3-5km đoạn qua xã Phú Long, tỉnh Ninh Bình được người dân trồng kín dứa - Ảnh: THÀNH NAM
Tuy nhiên, ông Trường thừa nhận dù sự việc được phát hiện từ gần một năm trước nhưng đến nay vẫn chưa được xử lý triệt để, công tác giám sát ở một số thời điểm còn chưa chặt chẽ.
Cũng theo ông Trường, dự án dự kiến kết thúc vào ngày 31-12-2026, sau đó sẽ được bàn giao cho Sở Xây dựng tỉnh Ninh Bình quản lý, khai thác.
Đối với tình trạng người dân vẫn trồng dứa, ông Trường cho biết Ban sẽ tiếp tục phối hợp với nhà thầu và chính quyền địa phương vận động người dân chấp hành.
Trường hợp người dân không đồng thuận, đơn vị sẽ rà soát cụ thể từng hộ để yêu cầu dừng việc canh tác trong phạm vi dự án.

NhưTuổi Trẻđã thông tin, trên dải phân cách và bên hành lang đại lộ Hoa Lư có tổng mức đầu tư gần 2.000 tỉ đồng đoạn qua xã Phú Long, Cúc Phương, tỉnh Ninh Bình bỗng xuất hiện những cánh đồng dứa xanh mướt, kéo dài nhiều cây số.
Ghi nhận thực tế dọc tuyến đường sáng 2-11 cho thấy việc người dân trồng dứa chỉ bắt đầu xuất hiện tại địa bàn xã Phú Long và xã Cúc Phương.
Trong đó, tập trung nhiều nhất tại xã Phú Long.
Chủ đầu tư khẳng định, việc người dân trồng dứa trong phạm vi dự án đại lộ Hoa Lư là không được phép - Ảnh: THÀNH NAM
Tại đoạn đường này, dải phân cách xuất hiện những cánh đồng dứa được trồng kín.
Có chỗ dứa đã bén rễ, xanh tốt và đang chuẩn bị ra quả, có nơi dứa vừa mới được trồng.
Không chỉ trồng dứa, một số đoạn trên dải phân cách, người dân còn trồng cả ngô, lạc.
Trái với những đoạn đường này, tại nhiều vị trí không trồng dứa, cỏ cây mọc um tùm, có nơi cây lau sậy mọc cao quá đầu người, tràn cả ra đường giao thông.
Vụ việc sau đó nổ ra tranh cãi trên mạng xã hội.
Chủ đầu tư cho rằng việc trồng dứa trên dải phân cách, trong phạm vị dự án là không được phép.
Trong khi, nhiều ý kiến cho rằng, trồng dứa trên khu vực này tránh cỏ dại mọc um tùm che khuất tầm nhìn, đường lại trở nên thông thoáng.
Tuy nhiên, nhiều độc giả lại cho rằng khi người dân tự ý cải tạo đất trồng dứa, quá trình chăm sóc và thu hoạch dứa sẽ tiềm ẩn nguy cơ gây ra tai nạn giao thông.
Chủ đầu tư nói gì về cánh đồng dứa mọc trên đại lộ ngàn tỉ gây tranh cãi?

Israel's president begins consultations with parties after election deadlock - BBC News
President Isaac Herzog received the official results from the Central Election Committee on Wednesday morning
Israel's President Isaac Herzog has begun consultations with political parties on whom to task with forming a new coalition government, after he received the official results of a general election last week he said had no clear winner.
Herzog told party leaders that "not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled" if they want to avoid a new election.
Neither the bloc of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his rival Gadi Eisenkot secured a majority in parliament.
Earlier, electoral officials said there was no evidence of irregularities and that unsubstantiated claims by Netanyahu's camp of Arab-led parties "stealing" the election did not justify delaying the results' certification.
The Shin Bet security service is investigating allegations of foreign interference in the election, but the head of the Central Elections Committee stressed that they would not fundamentally change the outcome.

Israel's election deadlock is a sign of the country's deep divisions
In the election on 27 October, Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies won 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc won 48.
Two Arab-led alliances, the United Arab List and the Joint List, together won an unprecedented 19 seats following a surge in turnout among Arab voters.
That makes them potential kingmakers. However, all but one of the Jewish parties pledged before the polls not to work with them to form a government.
The role of Israel's president is largely ceremonial, but after an election they have the role of inviting a Knesset member to form a government. That person will be given 28 days to do so, with a potential 14-day extension.
The president has wide discretion to pick someone they believe has the best chance of building a coalition. They do not have to choose the leader of the party with the most seats.
On Wednesday morning, Herzog was presented with the official results by Central Elections Committee chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg at a ceremony in Jerusalem.
"In recent days, we have heard voices trying to cast doubt on the election results and to undermine their legitimacy. This is a real danger," Sohlberg said.
"One of the foundations of democracy is the ability to have a peaceful transfer of power. This stems from the understanding that the will of the electorate obligates us all."
Herzog announced that he would begin the consultation process on Wednesday evening.
"In order to prevent another round of elections and to build a stable and good government here for the people of Israel, I expect the factions and their representatives to understand that, in the current reality, not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled," he said.
The president also expressed confidence in the Shin Bet's ability to investigate the allegations of foreign interference in the election and appealed for patience.
But he warned that Arab Israelis - who make up about one fifth of the population and often refer to themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel - "must not be smeared".
"I condemn the coarseness and racist expressions that we have heard recently. There is no place for them toward any community in Israel," he said.
Earlier, Sohlberg told a meeting of the Central Elections Committee that the Shin Bet's intelligence appeared to point to a "widespread phenomenon involving the influx of substantial funds into Israel from foreign states", some of which were hostile.
It believed further investigation was needed to "connect the dots and determine the scale of the phenomenon with a high degree of certainty", he said.
Last week, Israeli media reported that the committee had been presented with a claim that Qatar had provided funding aimed at increasing voter turnout in Arab communities. Qatar's foreign ministry said it categorically denied the allegation.
Far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, the leader of the Jewish Power party and an ally of the prime minister, called on the Shin Bet to arrest all the leaders of Arab parties and interrogate them "until these suspicions are fully clarified".
Joint List chairman Yousef Jabareen accused Ben-Gvir and the prime minister of attempting to "steal the election from the public".
On Tuesday, Eisenkot alleged that Netanyahu and his Likud party were "trying to carry out a veritable pogrom against democracy and the rule of law".
His comments came after Attorney-General Gali Baharav-Miara rejected a reported demand by Shin Bet chief David Zini - an appointee of the prime minister - to interrogate four Arab politicians, saying no evidence of wrongdoing had been presented.
Likud accused Baharav-Miara of trying to "obstruct the investigation and to cover up this serious case of manipulation of the electoral process by foreign actors".

Israel’s election commission rejects Netanyahu claims of voting fraud
Move comes after attorney general blocks Shin Bet call to interrogate politicians from Palestinian-led parties
Israel’s election commission on Wednesday confirmed the final results of last week’s vote that stripped Benjamin Netanyahu’s far-right coalition of its governing majority, rejecting claims of mass fraud promoted by the prime minister.
The main challenger, Gadi Eisenkot, said Netanyahu had launched a “pogrom against democracy” in attempting to hold on to power by discrediting valid votes and weaponising security forces against parties led by Palestinian citizens ofIsrael.
Hours earlier, Israel’s attorney general said she had blocked a demand from the Shin Bet security service to interrogate senior politicians from the Palestinian-led parties because she had not been presented with any evidence of wrongdoing.
“In a country governed by the rule of law, neither citizens nor elected officials can be interrogated without evidence that justifies doing so,” Gali Baharav-Miara said in a statement, after Haaretz reported on the attempt to target four politicians.
Election authorities on Wednesday presented the final results to the president, Isaac Herzog, after rejecting allegations they had been tainted by large-scale foreign interference and voter fraud.
“The review found no evidence of irregularities that compromised the integrity of the election or affected its results,” the Central Elections Committee said in a statement.
View image in fullscreenPeople take part in a rally in Tel Aviv calling for the opposition to form a government with the Palestinian-led parties after last week’s general election.Photograph: Jamal Awad/Reuters
The body’s chair, Noam Sohlberg, said some “suspicions” were still under investigation but “they do not cast doubt on the election as a whole or justify delaying the election results”.
When the results were handed over, Herzog denounced racist attacks on Palestinian citizens who had turned out to vote at historic rates.
“I condemn the coarseness and racist expressions that we have heard recently,” he said. “I hold Arab society in Israel in great respect. I value its contribution to the country in every area of life, and its desire to integrate.”
Herzog will play a key role in the formation of the next government by choosing which politician has the first chance to create a coalition. He is expected to name Eisenkot, and the announcement could come as early as Thursday evening.
A former leader of the Israeli military who lost his son fighting in Gaza, Eisenkot has secured the public support of all of the Jewish Israeli opposition parties. Palestinian-led parties have said their priority is removing Netanyahu, so they are expected to back him as the strongest contender to achieve that.
However, negotiations could take weeks and Eisenkot warned of ongoing attempts to undermine trust in the election results. He accused Netanyahu of weaponising the security services against domestic opponents in an effort to hold on to power.
View image in fullscreenGadi Eisenkot has secured the public support of all the Jewish Israeli opposition parties.Photograph: Paulina Patimer/JNA/Zuma Press/Shutterstock
“The employees of the Ministry of Defense, law enforcement and the civil service in Israel are servants of the state, not the king,” he said in a statement. “Woe to anyone who abuses their authority and role for political considerations.”
The Shin Bet chief, David Zini, handpicked for the role by Netanyahu, had ordered the interrogations and sought to classify the investigation as a security file, which would have allowed harsher conditions including barring the politicians from having legal counsel.
Nadav Eyal, an Israeli journalist and commentator, said the public should brace for more extreme attempts to dismiss election results and discredit the leading opposition parties.
“The groundwork is steadily being laid for violence,” he wrote on X. “What you’re hearing breaking right now is the foundation of the legal and governmental orders in Israel.”
Netanyahu presided over a racist campaign targeting Palestinian citizens of Israel – about 20% of the population – and on election day began promoting the unfounded accusations of mass fraud now rejected by election authorities.
Ahmad Tibi, one of the most prominent and effective Palestinian politicians, was reportedly among those the Shin Bet sought to interrogate. He responded to the latest allegations, as news broke ofsweeping victories for Democratsin the US midterms, with a swipe at Netanyahu’s fear of democracy.

This comes after the Netanyahu-led bloc won 53 parliamentary seats in the October 27 vote, while Gadi Eisenkot’s opposition bloc got 48, and the Arab-led parties Ra’am and the Joint List secured a record 19.
With neither bloc able to attain the 61-member majority needed to govern in the 120-seat Knesset, Herzog said both sides needed to accept that “not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled” and to avoid new elections.
“In the current reality, in which there is no clear winner after the elections, I ask for originality and creativity, courage and goodwill, so that the State of Israel emerges the winner,” Herzog said as he formally received the election results.
The election saw soaring support for lists from the Arab minority, descendants of Palestinians who stayed in Israel after its 1948 creation and who have largely been outraged by the harsh rhetoric and actions of Netanyahu’s far-right government.
Netanyahu and his allies have repeatedly claimed, without evidence, that Arab-led parties “stole” the election, possibly with foreign help.
Speaking at the official results ceremony at Herzog’s residence, Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, who is also the chairman of the Central Elections Committee, said those casting doubt on the results pose “a real danger” to Israel’s democracy.
The committee said a review of 9,069 polling stations found no irregularities that compromised the integrity of the election or changed its results. Its acting director general, Dean Livne, said every complaint had been examined individually and the results accurately reflected voters’ choices.
In the committee’s five-member presidium, representatives of Yesh Atid and Blue and White voted to ratify the results, while Likud and Shas abstained. Justice Sohlberg cast the deciding vote.
The election deadlockraises the possibility of a unity government or an alliance between Eisenkot and Arab-led parties. If no one is able to form a governing coalition, Israel would hold another election early next year.
In a break from custom, The Times of Israel reported that Herzog will meet the smaller parties’ leaders first, starting with Religious Zionism, followed by Shas and Yisrael Beytenu. It is expected the remaining factions will meet with the president on Thursday, ending withEisenkot’s Yashar and, finally, Likud.
After holding two days of consultations, the president will give a contender 28 days to form a government, with a potential 14-day extension.
It took Netanyahu, who at the time had a better showing by Likud, 58 days to form a government after the last election in November 2022.
Israel held five elections between 2019 and 2022 after repeated deadlocks.
Election results ‘binding on us all’
Justice Sohlberg of the elections committee said Israeli authorities would keep investigating allegations of vote misconduct but that they would not fundamentally change the results.
After the vote, the internal security agency Shin Bet told the committee that intelligence pointed to widespread foreign funding and influence operations involving “thousands of people and possibly more”, The Times of Israel reported. Law enforcement sources told Haaretz daily they were unaware of any operation of that size.
The Shin Bet is reportedly seeking to question four Arab politicians, but has not given prosecutors evidence regarding three of them. Likud accused Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara of blocking the interrogations. In turn, she effectively accused Shin Bet chief David Zini, a Netanyahu appointee, of undermining the rule of law, according to The Times of Israel.
National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir called on Zini to arrest all Arab party leaders and question them in Shin Bet cells, even without the attorney general’s approval. He also demanded a freeze on certification and on forming a government. “The elections were stolen, the results are fraudulent, foreign countries interfered,” Ben-Gvir wrote on X, adding that his far-right Otzma Yehudit party would therefore vote against approving the results.
Likud legislator Amit Halevi resigned from the committee. He alleged that some lawmakers “bought their seats with bribe money” and that the vote reflected “the choice of the rulers of Qatar, Iran or Turkey”.Qatar has rejected claimsthat it funded Arab-led parties, calling them “disinformation”.
Haaretz reported that Likud had weighed refusing to recognise the results altogether. Such a move would be unprecedented in Israel and would likely be swiftly overturned by the courts. Sohlberg rejected a Likud demand to discuss the results before certifying them, writing that no party, “however distinguished or senior”, could withhold their publication. He has said even if foreign interference were confirmed, it would not undermine the overall result.
Warning not to erode democracy, Sohlberg said: “There is one thing on which we must agree: election results, as lawfully determined, are binding on us all.”

NASA Space Grant Students Fuel Agency’s Inspiration Tour
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman addresses a standing-room-only crowd during an Inspiration Tour stop at Iowa State University.Credit: NASA
NASA’s Inspiration Tour spread the excitement of space exploration and aeronautical innovation by connecting the public, industry, and academia with the people, technologies, and organizations that drive American leadership in space. At nearly every stop across the country,NASA Space Granthas brought students into the heart of the action.
In Iowa, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman toured the Make to Innovate program lab at Iowa State University. Students from the Iowa Space Grant Consortium’s Mission Moon program, along with consortium-funded student organizations including Cardinal Space Mining, CySat, and CyLaunch, shared research findings and demonstrated the institution’s strong connection to NASA via agency-funded projects. During a well-attended town hall event NASA experts briefed students on the agency’s Moon Base efforts and how their work can contribute to future exploration.
“We’re grateful for the opportunity to welcome NASA leadership to Iowa State,” said Sara Nelson Iowa Space Grant director. “The excitement among students was incredible, and the visit highlighted how the research and innovation happening in Iowa can help advance Artemis and NASA’s future exploration efforts.”
At the University of Arizona, the NASA administrator saw firsthand the space research and engineering capabilities that are enabled by the Arizona Space Grant Consortium. From satellite communications testing to complex optics for peering into deep space to student-built high-altitude balloon payloads and even small satellites, students at the University of Arizona have a long history of contributing to NASA missions and making aerospace career connections. This tour stop also included a Q&A session where the NASA administrator answered questions from local high school and college students.
“It was incredible to present the high-altitude ballooning research we do in SEDS (Students for the Exploration and Development of Space) to Jared Isaacman and those at NASA,” said Ella Miller, a junior studying mechanical engineering at the University of Arizona. “Arizona Space Grant has allowed me to get hands-on experience through an entire mission design process every semester, helping me pursue a career in space research and secure internships in this field.”
Space Grant students from the University of Alaska Fairbanks shared their research with NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman during a Science Fair event in conjunction with the agency’s Inspiration Tour stop.Credit: NASA/Bill Ingalls
At the University of Alaska in Fairbanks, the Administrator toured two Geophysical Institute facilities: Poker Flat Research Range, the university’s scientific rocket launching facility, and the Alaska Satellite Facility. During an Alaska Space Grant science fair, students shared research in hibernation biology and showcased CubeSat technology advancements. Students were also able to learn about the agency’s Moon Base program and ask questions about opportunities available to the next generation of innovators and explorers.
In North Dakota, the Inspiration Tour focused on future exploration capabilities. Space Grant-funded research at the University of North Dakota is helping to shape the future of exploration across STEM fields. Student fellows and NASA interns shared their projects on supercell mergers using satellite imagery, geomagnetic conditions of aurora borealis, and in-situ resource utilization, to name a few. North Dakota Space Grant STEM ambassador students also shared robotics and drone activities as part of “Mission Moon”, which centers Artemis initiatives in statewide collaborations with educators and other North Dakota colleges and universities.
“Getting to speak with the NASA Administrator was an amazing opportunity!” said research fellow and STEM ambassador Malissa Reinhardt. “He genuinely cared about what we students had to say and the research we’re working on, which makes all the hard work we put into our research and North Dakota Space Grant Consortium so rewarding.”
Students at the University of North Dakota’s spacesuit lab demonstrated design advancements for lunar surface spacesuits for NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman during a tour of their lab during the agency’s Inspiration Tour stopCredit: NASA

NASA is racing against time to save the Hubble Space Telescope
Date:November 4, 2026Source:NASASummary:NASA is exploring a daring plan to save the legendary Hubble Space Telescope from its eventual fiery plunge into Earth's atmosphere. After more than 35 years of groundbreaking discoveries, Hubble is slowly losing altitude, and without intervention, it could fall back to Earth as early as 2033 or 2034. To keep the iconic observatory operating, NASA is asking private space companies to propose innovative ways to boost Hubble into a higher orbit, upgrade its capabilities, or safely dispose of it when its mission finally ends.Share:FacebookTwitterPinterestLinkedINEmailFULL STORYNASA is exploring a potential rescue mission to save the Hubble Space Telescope from a fiery return to Earth and give it more years to uncover the universe's mysteries. Credit: ESA/Hubble (M. Kornmesser & L. L. Christensen)
NASA is investigating whether private space companies could help extend the life of the Hubble Space Telescope, which has spent more than 35 years transforming our understanding of the universe.
On October 29, the agency issued a Request for Information seeking details about commercial technologies that could be used to service Hubble while it remains in orbit. The goal is to determine whether new spacecraft capabilities could keep the iconic observatory operating longer, improve its performance, or help bring its mission to a safe conclusion.
"Hubble still has important science ahead of it, and we should be looking at every reasonable opportunity to keep it delivering for as long as possible," said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. "If there are innovative and cost-effective ways to extend the life of an asset already on orbit, we owe it to the American taxpayer and the scientific community to explore them. Extending Hubble's life would mean more discoveries, more science, and more opportunities to expand our understanding of the universe."
NASA Considers Raising Hubble Into a Higher Orbit
One possibility under consideration is sending a spacecraft to push Hubble into a higher orbit. This could counteract the gradual loss of altitude that threatens the telescope's future and potentially allow it to continue making scientific discoveries for additional years.
NASA is also interested in missions that could service the telescope and improve its capabilities. Another option would focus on safely retiring Hubble when its scientific work is complete, either by guiding it through a controlled descent into Earth's atmosphere or arranging for its disposal in orbit.
These possibilities are being explored rather than formally approved. By reaching out to commercial companies, NASA hopes to better understand what technologies are available and whether they could provide practical, affordable solutions.
"Hubble is a national icon that has fundamentally changed how humanity views our universe for more than 35 years," said Nicky Fox, associate administrator, Science Mission Directorate, NASA Headquarters in Washington. "Commercial industry has rapidly evolved in recent years to offer new capabilities for in-space satellite capture and servicing. Given the time we have until Hubble's anticipated re-entry, we are eager to explore the breadth of possibilities to boost Hubble to a higher orbit while we develop the flagship mission to follow."
Companies interested in participating can reviewNASA's Request for Information online. The agency is accepting responses until 3 p.m. EST on Monday, November 30.
Why Hubble Could Fall Back to Earth by 2034
Although Hubble continues to operate in space, its orbit is gradually shrinking. The telescope travels through low Earth orbit, where traces of Earth's atmosphere create drag that slowly reduces the altitude of orbiting spacecraft.
Even hundreds of miles above the planet, the atmosphere is not completely absent. The tiny amount of remaining gas produces resistance as spacecraft move through it. Over long periods, this effect can cause satellites to lose altitude and eventually descend into denser layers of the atmosphere.
Unlike spacecraft equipped with engines that can periodically raise their orbits, Hubble has no propulsion system capable of maintaining its altitude. Without outside assistance, it cannot reverse this gradual orbital decline.
NASA's current analysis suggests that Hubble will likely reenter Earth's atmosphere sometime between 2033 and 2034. To prevent that outcome through an orbital boost, the agency expects that a mission would need to occur by 2032.
That timeline leaves a limited window to evaluate potential solutions, develop a mission, and carry it out before the telescope descends too far.
Extending Hubble's Legacy of Cosmic Discoveries
Since beginning operations more than three decades ago, Hubble has become one of the most influential scientific observatories ever launched. Its observations have helped reshape astronomers' understanding of the cosmos, and the telescope continues to produce discoveries that advance research across many areas of astronomy.
Hubble is also the product of a longstanding international partnership between NASA and ESA (European Space Agency).
NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, oversees the telescope and its mission operations, with additional operational support from Denver-based Lockheed Martin Space.
Scientific operations are handled by the Space Telescope Science Institute in Baltimore, which is operated by the Association of Universities for Research in Astronomy on NASA's behalf.
With commercial spaceflight technology advancing, NASA is now evaluating whether Hubble could benefit from capabilities that were not available when it was originally designed. A successful mission to raise its orbit or enhance its systems could allow the historic telescope to continue exploring the universe well beyond its currently projected orbital lifetime.

The teams have been named, and here they jolly well are!Five changes forLiverpool, with Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak among those dropping to the bench and Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas among those hopping into the first XI.
Fenerbahce:Ederson, Nelson Semedo, Skriniar, Oppong, Brown, Guendouzi, Kante, Yuksek, Greenwood, Lukaku, Kahveci.Subs:Tarik Cetin, Gunok, Akturkoglu, Demir, Muldur, Muriqi, Mercan, Elmaz, Dorgeles, Aydin, Mimovic.

Earlier today Liverpool’s Under-19sbeat theirFenerbahcecounterparts 5-3, with Will Wright scoring a hat-trick. They were 3-1 up after just 20 minutes, and 4-2 up after half an hour, while Fenerbahce finished with 10 men after Ali Demirbilek was sent off in stoppage time. Also on the scoresheet was Finn Inglethorpe, son of Liverpool’s long-time academy director, Alex.
View image in fullscreenWill Wright of Liverpool scores against Fenerbahce in the Uefa Youth League.Photograph: ANP/Shutterstock
Here’s Andy Hunter’s pre-match missive from Istanbul:
Andoni Iraola has said Liverpool must improve their attacking play but dismissed concerns over the contrast between his team’s output in the Premier League and Champions League.
Liverpool boast a 100% record in Europe this season and can take a significant step towards qualification for the knockout phase with victory away at Fenerbahce on Wednesday.
Iraola’s side failed to register a shot on target, according to Opta, during Sunday’s defeat by Arsenal, the first time Liverpool have drawn a blank in a Premier League home game since their records began in 2003-04. The Liverpool head coach believes the statistic did not reflect his team’s performance but admitted there is room for improvement.
Andoni Iraola calls on Liverpool to sharpen up in attack before Fenerbahce testRead more
Yesterday afternoon former Liverpool striker Dirk Kuyttold the media how excited he was to be facing his former team as Fenerbahce’s interim manager. “As soon as the draw was done, I was really excited because everyone knows how muchFenerbahceand Liverpool mean to me and, from that moment, you know it will be a special occasion,” he beamed. “Of course, tomorrow will be a very special occasion for me but at the stage we’re in, I’m not here for myself. I’m here for the club and that’s what is important, to show the fans who deserve much more, a reaction, positive energy and a good performance.”
Then, at 11.25pm local time last night, the Turkish side announced that former Newcastle midfielder Emre Belozoglu – veteran also of two spells at Fener as a player and one as interim manager in 2021 – was replacing Kuyt, and his special occasion was imperilled. In the cold light of a new day it looks like Emre won’t take over until after this game, at which point Kuyt will either return to the role of assistant he held under previous head coach Ismail Kartal, or leave the club.
Either way, this promises to be a raucous farewell/not farewell. Fenerbahce are having a stinker of a season, sixth in the Super Lig having lost their last two league games, most recently experiencing a Hallowe’en nightmare at home to Goztepe, but this gives them a probably welcome distraction. Let’s see what they do with it, shall we?

Jesus de Miguel: Goalkeeper Jesus Owono defended by FC Andorra team-mate after Tenerife forward's death
FC Andorra's Argentinian defender Lautaro Spatz took to Instagram to pay tribute to Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel after he died following a collision with Jesus Owono, but also defended the goalkeeper, who has deleted his account on the social media platform
Image:Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono walks off the pitch after he collided with FC Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel
Jesus Owono's team-mate has insisted the FC Andorra goalkeeper would never intend to hurt a fellow player following the death of Jesus de Miguel.
The Tenerife forward died on Tuesday morning following a collision with Owono during a Spanish second division match on Monday.
Owono was sent off for the clash having raced from his goal and struck 30-year-old De Miguel at force, withthe Tenerife player subsequently suffering a cardiac arrest.

There has been shock and grief across football following the tragic incident, while Spanish police have opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter.
That is, though, standard practice under Spanish law and Santa Cruz de Tenerife chief prosecutor Jose Luis Sanchez-Jauregui told Spanish news agency EFE that criminal proceedings were "very unlikely".
Andorra's Argentinian defender Lautaro Spatz took to Instagram to pay tribute to De Miguel but also to defend Owono, who has deleted his account on the social media platform.
Spatz called De Miguel's death "a tragedy that has left us completely broken, without words and with a sadness difficult to explain".
The 25-year-old continued: "I also want to have some words for my team-mate, goalkeeper and friend, who is deeply affected by what happened.
"Those of us who know him know the type of person he is, how much he is suffering in these moments and that he would never intend to hurt anyone.
"In football, unfortunate incidents happen but no-one could imagine that one of these could end in such tragic circumstances."
Image:Tributes were paid to Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel outside the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez Stadium in Santa Cruz
Fans gathered at Tenerife's Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium to lay tributes to De Miguel, with the club declaring six days of official mourning.
A memorial service will be held at the ground on Saturday evening for the striker, with supporters invited to attend.
Tuesday's domestic Spanish games were called off as a mark of respect but Champions League matches went ahead, including Barcelona's clash with Aston Villa at the Nou Camp.
A minute's silence was held ahead of the contest, which Barca won 3-0, with Raphinha scoring twice.
Speaking to CBS Sports afterwards, the Brazilian refused to talk about the game, saying: "I want to send a lot of strength to the family of Jesus. Today I'm not going to talk about football.
"For me, the truth is it was quite difficult (to play). After seeing the news, of course I didn't have good feelings. He's a fellow player and it could have happened to anyone, it could have happened to me.

Jesus de Miguel death: Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono 'would never intentionally hurt anyone' says team-mate - BBC Sport
Fans pay respects to Tenerife's De Miguel
ByDavid WatkinsonBBC Sport senior journalist
Goalkeeper Jesus Owono "would never intentionally hurt anyone" and has been "deeply affected" by the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel, an FC Andorra team-mate said on Wednesday.
Tenerife player De Miguel, 30,died after suffering a serious injury in a collision with Owonoduring a Spanish second division match on Monday.
The world of football has paid tribute to De Miguel, a father-of-one who joined Tenerife in summer 2025, with a minute's silence being held at all European games this week.
Writing on social media, FC Andorra centre-back Lautaro Spatz said Owono was devastated.
He paid tribute to De Miguel but added: "I also want to say a few words about my team-mate, goalkeeper and friend, who is deeply affected by what has happened.
"Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone.
"In football, unfortunate incidents can happen but no-one could imagine that one of them might end with such tragic consequences."
Players from Andorra held a minute's silence before a voluntary training session on Wednesday. Owono did not attend the session.
Football world mourns Tenerife striker De Miguel
Tenerife and Andorra were drawing 2-2 seven minutes into stoppage time when the incident occurred.
Owono ran towards the centre circle to clear a long ball when his knee appeared to collide with De Miguel.
The striker lay motionless on the pitch as medical staff treated him before he was taken by ambulance from Tenerife's Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez to hospital.
Owono was sent off and the match was abandoned.
The 25-year-old goalkeeper, who had over 30,000 followers on Instagram on Tuesday morning, has since deactivated his account.
Police in Spain opened a routine investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter following De Miguel's death.
Under Spanish law, any death that is deemed non-natural automatically triggers a judicial inquiry.
Owono has made 47 international appearances for Equatorial Guinea.
The president of Equatorial Guinea's football federation, Venancio Tomas Micha, issued a statement on Tuesday offering "all our human and professional backing" to the player.
"As the involuntary protagonist of this tragic incident in the game, he is living through this situation with deep sorrow and distress," he added.
Jesus de Miguel joined Tenerife in 2025 on a three-year deal
On Tuesday, mourners laid flowers and lit candles beneath a black and white image of De Miguel at the Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez.
Tenerife said in a statement they will commence six official days of mourning, with all club activities suspended during this time.
The club's players, staff and officials will attend De Miguel's funeral, which will take place in Navahermosa, Toledo.
Tenerife will also open their home ground on Saturday evening to allow supporters to "bid a fitting farewell".
"Jesus de Miguel's family would like to thank everyone for their messages of support and, from the bottom of their hearts, ask that their privacy be respected at this terrible time. May he rest in peace," added the club statement.
Tenerife and Andorra's Spanish second division matches scheduled for the weekend, against Granada and Mallorca respectively, have been postponed.
